READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:2 "you shall not add to the word. . .nor take away from it"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 4:2 "you shall not add to the word. . .nor take away from it" This does not refer to scribes updating the text of the Law, but rather that you cannot add to the essence of the Law (cf. Deut. 12:32; Prov. 30:5-6; Eccl. 3:14; Jer. 26:2; this is similar to Rev. 22:18-19). These bans on "adding to" or "subtracting from" are characteristic of Ancient Near Eastern literature. However, there is a slight difference between the Ten Words as recorded in Exodus 20 and Deuteronomy 5. See Hard Sayings of the Bible, pp. 782-784.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:3 "Baal-peor"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 4:3 "Baal-peor" This (BDB 128) refers to the place where Israelites turned from following YHWH and went after the fertility gods of Moab (cf. Num. 25:1-9). The LXX and Peshitta translate this as referring to the local Ba'al.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:4 "you who held fast to the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:4 "you who held fast to the Lord" The Hebrew word "hold," "cleave" (BDB 180) is translated as a VERB in NASB. It is the opposite of "follow after" in Deut. 4:3 (i.e. Ba'al). The VERB form of this word is used:

  1. of Adam's love for Eve ‒ Gen. 2:24
  2. of holding fast to YHWH ‒ Deut. 10:20; 11:22; 13:4; Josh. 22:5; 23:8; 2 Kgs. 18:6; Ps. 101:3
  3. of Boaz telling Ruth to stay close to his female servants ‒ Ruth 2:8, 21, 23
  4. of Solomon's idolatry to his young wives' gods ‒ 1 Kgs. 11:2
  5. of holding fast to YHWH's covenant ‒ Ps. 119:31

It denotes an attitude of loyalty or commitment. It is used in parallel with "love" in Gen. 34:3; 1 Kgs. 11:2; Prov. 18:24 (see NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 911).

Even in the election of YHWH, humans had to respond appropriately. Even as God chose Israel to be His priestly nation (cf. Exod. 19:5-6), each individual had to choose God. This is a balance between God's sovereignty and human freewill. It is also the balance of corporality ("you" PLURAL) versus individual ("everyone of you") response.

These is no VERB in Deut. 4:4; the VERBAL idea is conveyed by two ADJECTIVES (BDB 180, 311).

4:5
NASB, NRSV, JPSOA, LXX  "See"
NKJV  "surely"
TEV   —
NJB  "look"
REB  "You saw for yourselves"
Peshitta  "behold"

This is a Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 906, KB 1157). It was a literary way of asserting that Moses had fulfilled his responsibility and now the people must respond appropriately.

▣ "possess it" See SPECIAL TOPIC: POSSESS THE LAND

4:6
NASB  "So keep and do them"
NKJV  "therefore be careful to observe them"
NRSV  "You must observe them diligently"
TEV  "Obey them faithfully"
NJB  "Keep them, put them into practice"
Peshitta, LXX  "that you should do them"

There are two VERBS in this phrase:

  1. "keep" (BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal PERFECT with waw), which means "keep," "watch," or "preserve." This VERB is used often in the Pentateuch (Deuteronomy, cf. Deut. 2:4; 4:2,6,9,15,23,40; many other places)
  2. "do" (BDB 793, KB 889, Qal PERFECT with waw) means "do" or "make." The VERB is also used often in the OT (e.g. Deut. 4:1,3,6,13,14,16,23,25).

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:6 "wisdom"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:6 "wisdom" This term (BDB 315) is used in Prov. 1:2,7 and the ADJECTIVE in Deut. 1:6. This wisdom is knowledge of God and His will. It is what humans seek because they are made

  1. in the image and likeness of God (cf. Gen. 1:26-27)
  2. for fellowship with Him (cf. Gen. 3:8; Deut. 4:7-8)

▣ "understanding" This term (BDB 108) is parallel to wisdom. Its goal is an informed, godly, happy life (e.g. Deut. 32:28; Prov. 2:1-22; 3:13-18).

▣ "Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people" Did YHWH choose Israel because He loved them more than any others? He loves all humans equally (cf. Ezek. 18:23,32; 33:11; John 3:16; 1 Tim. 2:4; 2 Pet. 3:9). God simply needed a place to begin. He chose Abraham and his seed to be a kingdom of priests to the world (cf. Gen. 12:3; Exod. 19:4-6; Acts 3:25; Gal. 3:8). Theirs was an election for purpose rather than election because of special love.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELECTION

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:7 "what great nation is there that has a god so near to it"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:7 "what great nation is there that has a god so near to it" This refers to YHWH's personal presence (i.e. immanence) with Israel in the form of the Shekinah cloud (wilderness wandering period) and later the ark of the covenant (beyond Jordan and into the monarchial period).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE CLOUD

SPECIAL TOPIC: ARK OF THE COVENANT

▣ "whenever we call on Him" This shows that the Israelites had confidence that the God who made the world was the God who would respond to them when they prayed. He is both powerful and personal (e.g. Ps. 34:18; 145:18)! A God who hears their prayers, and acts on their behalf, just opposite from the Canaanite idols!

SPECIAL TOPIC: CALL ON THE NAME

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:8 "statutes and judgments. . .law"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:8 "statutes and judgments. . .law" Israel is unique among all the nations because of YHWH's covenant presence and revelation. YHWH's character is revealed in His acts and laws.

SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

▣ "righteous" This is imagery from a river reed. God' righteousness is the standard or ruler by which we are measured. The law is based on the character of God.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

▣ "this whole law" This phrase refers to the book of Deuteronomy.

4:9
NASB, Peshitta  "Only give heed to yourself and keep your
  soul diligently"
NKJV  "Only take heed to yourself, and diligently
  keep yourself"
NRSV  "But take care and watch yourselves closely"
TEV  "Be on your guard! Make certain. . ."
NJB  "But take care, as you value your lives"
REB  "But take care: keep careful watch on
  yourselves"
LXX  "Take heed to yourself, and guard your soul
  closely"
JPSOA  "But take utmost care and watch yourselves
  scrupulously"

This phrase has two IMPERATIVES from the same root:

  1. "give heed" ‒ BDB 1036, KB 1581, Niphal IMPERATIVE, cf. Deut. 4:15; Josh. 23:11; Jer. 17:21).
  2. "keep" ‒ BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal IMPERATIVE in the sense of "keep by doing" (cf. Deut. 7:12).

For "soul," see SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH.

Obedience is a life-and-death issue (cf. Deut. 30:15-20)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

▣ "so that you do not forget. . .they do not depart" See Deut. 8:11-20.

▣ "heart" In Hebrew psychology the emotions are centered in the bowels. The heart is the center of the intellect (especially memory) and personality. God is saying, "Do not forget the law!"

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART

SPECIAL TOPIC: INWARD PARTS

▣ "all the days of your life" A lifestyle commitment is required (cf. Deut. 4:10; 6:2; 12:1; 16:3). Biblical faith is not only an initial decision but a lifelong commitment.

▣ "make them known to your sons and your grandsons" This is a recurrent theme in Deuteronomy (cf. Deut. 4:10; 6:7, 20-25; 11:19; 31:13; 32:46; and note Exod. 10:2; 12:26; 13:8,14). If believers do not teach their children about YHWH, they are failures as parents (biblically speaking)! Faith runs through families (cf. Deut. 5:10; 7:9)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:10 "Remember the day you stood before the Lord your God at Horeb"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:10 "Remember the day you stood before the Lord your God at Horeb" This refers to a previous generation. This specifically refers to Exodus 19-20. Remembering and passing on YHWH's great acts of deliverance (i.e. exodus) is a recurrent theme (cf. Deut. 5:15; 7:18; 8:2,18; 9:7,27; 11:2; 15:15; 16:3,12; 24:9,18,22; 25:17; 32:7).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S COVENANT REQUIREMENTS OF ISRAEL

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOREB

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOCATION OF MT. SINAI

▣ "so they may learn to fear Me" YHWH acted as He did on Mt. Horeb so that they would hold Him in reverential awe (cf. Exod. 20:20; Prov. 1:7; 9:10; Eccl. 12:15; Isa. 11:2-3; Ps. 34:11).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR (OT)

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:11 "the mountain burned with fire"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:11 "the mountain burned with fire" Fire is a symbol of YHWH's presence (cf. Exod. 19:18; Deut. 5:23; 9:15; Heb. 12:18). It may symbolize purity.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE

▣ "darkness, cloud and thick gloom" YHWH's physical presence can be understood in two ways:

  1. volcanic activity ‒ Exod. 19:18; Ps. 68:7-8; 77:18; 97:2-5; Jdg. 5:4-5; 2 Sam. 22:8; Isa. 29:6; Jer. 10:10
  2. storm ‒ Exod. 19:16,19; Ps. 68:8; 77:18; Jdg. 5:4; Isa. 29:6; Nahum 1:3
  3. a supernatural event (i.e. Shekinah)

Therefore, the deep darkness (cf. Deut. 5:22; 2 Sam. 22:10; 1 Kgs. 8:12; 2 Chr. 6:1) might be:

  1. ash clouds
  2. rain clouds

This covering was for Israel's protection (cf. Exod. 19:18). They thought that if humans looked upon God they would die (cf. Gen. 16:13; 32:30; Exod. 3:6; 20:19; 33:20; Jdg. 6:22-23; 13:22).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEKINAH

SPECIAL TOPIC: DEEP DARKNESS

SPECIAL TOPIC: CAN HUMANS SEE GOD AND LIVE?

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:12 "but you saw no form"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 4:12 "but you saw no form" YHWH has no physical form (cf. John 4:24). He allowed Moses to see His "afterglow" in Exod. 33:23. YHWH desires no physical representation because of fallen mankind's tendency toward idolatry (cf. Deut. 4:15-19). See full note online at Exod. 33:17-23.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:13 "He declared to you His covenant"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:13 "He declared to you His covenant" This VERB (BDB 616, KB 665, Hiphil IMPERFECT with waw), when used with YHWH as the subject, denotes new revelation (e.g. 2 Sam. 7:11; Isa. 42:9; 45:19; Amos 4:13).

The IMPERFECT tense implies that the "ten words" are not all of YHWH's revelation. Much of the books of Exodus and Deuteronomy are explanations of the implications of the Decalog.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

▣ "Ten commandments" Literally this means "ten words" (BDB 797 CONSTRUCT 182) and is known in Greek as the Decalogue. They are very brief, a summary of God's revelation (cf. Exodus 20; Deuteronomy 5).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TEN COMMANDMENTS

▣ "He wrote them" YHWH Himself wrote (anthropomorphic) the "ten words" (cf. Exod. 31:8; 32:15-16). Reflecting on the imagery of this statement does not affect the divine source of the commands!

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN (anthropomorphism)

▣ "two tablets of stone" From recent archaeological discoveries and what we call the Suzerain Hittite Treaties (of the 2nd millennium B.C.), we know that Deuteronomy follows their outline and form. I think that the "two tablets" refers to two, exact copies of the Ten Commandments required by these treaty patterns (also a documenting of the past act of the major power making the treaty, i.e. Deuteronomy 1-4). This establishes the historicity of Deuteronomy. See introduction to the book, VII.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HITTITE (SUZERAIN) TREATIES

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:14 "you might perform them"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:14 "you might perform them" It is not enough to know God's will for your life, but to do it (cf. Deut. 4:1,2,5,6; Luke 6:46; James 2:14-20). Biblical faith is a lifetime of faithful worship, obedience, and service, not a one-time religious event

▣ "possess it" See SPECIAL TOPIC: POSSESS THE LAND

4:15
NASB  "So watch yourselves carefully"
NKJV, Peshitta  "Take careful heed to yourselves"
NRSV  "take care and watch yourselves closely"
TEV  "For your own good, then, make certain"
NJB  "be very careful what you do"
LXX  "Guard your souls closely"
JPSOA  "therefore, be most careful"

The VERB (BDB 1036, KB 1581, Niphal PERFECT with waw) is used in Deut. 4:2,6,9(twice),15,23,40. Israel's actions were conditionally connected to YHWH's covenant. They were to strenuously avoid idolatry (cf. Deut. 5:8-10).

▣ "you did not see any form" See SPECIAL TOPIC: CAN HUMANS SEE GOD AND LIVE?).

▣ "at Horeb" see SPECIAL TOPIC: LOCATION OF MT. SINAI

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOREB

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:16 "act corruptly and make a graven image"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:16 "act corruptly and make a graven image" This sin is a reference to the golden calf made by Aaron (cf. Exodus 32), which violated YHWH's incorporality. The Israelites were not to represent YHWH by anything physical (cf. Deut. 4:16-18,23,25; 5:8; Exod. 20:4).

▣ "the likeness of male or female" Mankind's tendency has been to make YHWH like a man or woman. If we put God in a human form, we have put Him into a form which we can manage.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:17 "likeness of any animal"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:17 "likeness of any animal" This may refer to

  1. other nations' use of animals to represent their gods and goddesses
  2. characteristics of animals to describe God

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:18 "creeps on the ground"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 4:18 "creeps on the ground" This possibly refers to the Egyptian Scarab beetle which was holy to them.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:19 "the sun and the moon and the stars, all the host of heaven"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:19 "the sun and the moon and the stars, all the host of heaven" The ancients, as well as the moderns (horoscope), felt that the stars represented forces or powers that control the lives of humans. The worship of astral bodies seems to have started in Babylon (Genesis 1 may represent a reaction to this type of idolatry, as Exodus 20 represents a reaction to Egyptian idolatry). Israel is to vigorously reject this kind of idolatry!

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOON WORSHIP

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS

SPECIAL TOPIC: IDOLATRY

▣ "those which the Lord your God has allotted to all the peoples" The VERB (BDB 323, KB 322, Qal PERFECT) means "to divide," but in the sense of allotment or apportionment. This could imply that God encouraged astral worship, but I think instead it is another way to show YHWH's sovereignty over all heavenly bodies and all the earth (cf. Deut. 29:26; 32:8 in LXX). Astral idolatry was never YHWH's plan or will for any human.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:20 "the iron furnace"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:20 "the iron furnace" A furnace takes unusable ore, heats it and makes it usable metal. This is an analogy of what YHWH did to Israel in Egypt (cf. 1 Kgs. 8:51; Jer. 11:4 and the same imagery in Isa. 48:10).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD TESTS HIS PEOPLE (OT)

▣ "to be a people for His own possession" This was a special title for YHWH's covenant people (e.g. Exod. 19:5; Deut. 7:6; 14:2; 26:18; Titus 2:14; and 1 Pet. 2:9). They have a divine inheritance (YHWH and land) because YHWH had chosen them even before creation (cf. Deut. 32:8-9; Ps. 33:6-12; Jer. 10:16; 51:19) to represent Himself to the world.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HE CHOSE US

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:21 "the Lord was angry with me on your account"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:21 "the Lord was angry with me on your account" Moses was reminding the people of YHWH's punishment to him because of his disobedience (cf. Deut. 1:37; 3:26; Num. 20:7-13). If they disobey, they will be punished also!

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:23 "So watch yourselves"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:23 "So watch yourselves" The VERB (BDB 1036, KB 1581, Niphal IMPERATIVE) is repeated often in this chapter. There are covenant benefits, but also covenant consequences (cf. Deut. 4:25; chapters 27-30; Leviticus 26).

▣ "that you do not forget the covenant" The VERB (BDB 1013, KB 1489,Qal PERFECT) is also found several times in this chapter (cf. Deut. 4:9,23,31) and also in Deut. 6:12; 8:11,14,19[twice]; 9:7; 24:19[twice]; 25:19; and 30:13; 31:21; 32:18. This is a major recurrent theme!

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:24 "jealous"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:24 "jealous" YHWH is described in this verse in two ways:

  1. "a consuming fire" (BDB 77 and BDB 37, KB 46, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE, cf. Exod. 24:17; Deut. 4:24; 9:3; Heb. 12:29) which denotes"
    1. YHWH is the covenant-making God of Sinai
    2. He is the God of judgment if the covenant is violated
  2. "a jealous God" (BDB 888 and 42, cf. Exod. 20:5; 34:14; Deut. 5:9; 6:15; Josh. 24:19) which denotes His personal, loving commitment to Israel, which is analogous to a marriage covenant (cf. Hosea 1-3). The covenant broken results in rejection (e.g. Josh. 24:19; Nahum 1:2). The word has a wide semantic field:
    1. passion ‒ Prov. 6:34; Song of Songs 8:6
    2. anger ‒ Prov. 14:30; 27:4
    3. jealousy ‒ Gen. 26:14; Num. 5:11-22; Ezek. 31:9
    4. competition ‒ Eccl. 4:4
    5. devotion ‒ Num. 11:29

(list from NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 938)

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN (anthropomorphism)

SPECIAL TOPIC: JEALOUS. . .ZEALOUS

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:25 "have remained long in the land"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:25 "have remained long in the land" This was not so much an individual promise of longevity, but a corporate promise to societies where parents teach the children about God and the children honor the parents. Stable families form stable societies (e.g. Deut. 4:9, 10,40 and 5:16,33).

▣ "act corruptly" The VERB (BDB 1007, KB 1469, Hiphil PERFECT with waw) means "to spoil" or "to ruin" and, by metaphorical extension, came to refer to covenant violations (i.e. idolatry, cf. Deut. 4:16,25; 9;12; 31:29).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

▣ "so as to provoke Him to anger" This phrase is a Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT (BDB 494, e.g. 32:21; 1 Kgs. 15:30; 16:13). Again, anthropomorphic language describes YHWH's reaction to human sin!

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROBLEMS AND LIMITATIONS OF HUMAN LANGUAGE

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:26 "I call heaven and earth to witness against you today"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:26 "I call heaven and earth to witness against you today" This was part of the Suzerain Hittite Treaties (need for powerful spiritual witnesses, cf. Intro. to Book, VII). These are the two most permanent things in physical creation. They are often called on by God to act as witnesses. It also reflects the Israeli legal system's need for two witnesses in a court case (cf. Num. 35:30; Deut. 17:6; 19:15). The phrase is used often in connection with the ratification of the covenant with YHWH (cf. Deut. 4:26; 30:19; 31:28).

▣ "you will surely perish quickly from the land" See Deuteronomy 27-29, but notice the theological balance of Deut. 4:31. D. Brent Sandy, Plowshares and Pruning Hooks, has helped me overcome my western literalism and come to understand the nature of biblical prophecy.

Unaided, fallen mankind has no hope of covenant obedience! (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-36).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:27 "scatter you among the peoples"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:27 "scatter you among the peoples" This seems to predict the exile of the covenant people by Assyria (722 B.C.) and Neo-Babylon (605, 597, 586, 582 B.C.), which is predicted in Deut. 28:64 and 29:28!

▣ "left few in number" This is a part of the consequences involved in breaking the covenant. It is opposite to the covenant blessing promised to Abraham in Gen. 15:5. See full note at Gen. 13:16.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:28 "you will serve gods, the work of man's hands"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:28 "you will serve gods, the work of man's hands" The VERB "serve" (BDB 712, KB 773, Qal PERFECT with waw) is used in the sense of worship or performance of cultic tasks:

  1. positively of YHWH ‒ Exod. 3:12; 4:23; Deut. 6:13; 1 Sam. 7:3
  2. negatively of other gods ‒ Exod. 23:33; Deut. 4:19,28; Josh. 23:7; Jdg. 2:10,19; 10:6,10; 1 Sam. 22:10; 1 Kgs. 16:31; 2 Kgs. 17:12

This Hebrew root becomes an honorific title of YHWH's servant (i.e. "My servant"):

  1. the Patriarchs ‒ Exod. 32:13; Deut. 9:27
  2. Caleb ‒ Num. 14:24
  3. Moses ‒ Exod. 14:31; Num. 12:7; Deut. 34:5; 1 Kgs. 8:53
  4. Joshua ‒ Josh. 24:29
  5. David ‒ 1 Sam. 23:10; 25:39
  6. Isaiah ‒ Isa. 20:3
  7. Messiah ‒ Isaiah 53; Zech. 3:8
  8. Nebuchadnezzar ‒ Jer. 25:9; 27:6; 43:10
  9. Cyrus ‒ Isa. 44:28; 45:1
  10. the nation of Israel ‒ Isa. 41:8; 44:1-2; 45:4

The references in Deut. 4:26,27,28 show the conditional nature of YHWH's promise and the folly of idolatry!

  1. Deut. 4:26, YHWH takes them out of the land
  2. Deut. 4:27, YHWH scatters them to other countries
  3. Deut. 4:28, they see idolatry firsthand

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:29 "you will seek the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:29 "you will seek the Lord" The VERB (BDB 134, KB 152, Piel PERFECT PLURAL) means "to seek" as in to restore the covenantal relationship with YHWH, broken by disobedience. The repentance demands total commitment (i.e. "with all of your heart and all of your soul," cf. Deut. 26:16; 30:2,10).

YHWH's forgiveness is always available upon true repentance (cf. Deut. 4:29-31; 30:1-3,10). True repentance is not lip service, but lifestyle change, not an emotion. We see examples of shallow, short-lived repentance in Hosea 6:1-3 and Jeremiah 3:21-25.

If they seek Him, they will find Him (cf. Jer. 24:7; 29:13). YHWH is not hard to find. He just expects His people to reflect His character!

SPECIAL TOPIC: Seek the Lord

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT REQUIREMENTS OF ISRAEL

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:30
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:30 Moses predicts Israel's rebellion, as does Joshua (cf. Josh. 24:19-28). The fall has spiritually damaged mankind's ability to obey God (cf. Romans 1-3; Galatians 3).

Notice that

  1. Deut. 4:26 seems to imply an immediate judgment
  2. Deut. 4:27 implies the Assyrian (722 B.C.) and Neo-Babylonian (605, 597, 586, 582 B.C.) exiles
  3. Deut. 4:30 speaks of an end-time setting ("in the latter days")

Israel must be covenantally related to YHWH. She can do this by covenant obedience (which Romans 1-3 and Galatians 3 say is impossible) or she can do it by new covenant faith/repentance in Jesus. All believers pray for an end-time revival among Jewish people (possibly Zech. 12:10 or Romans 11).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

▣ "in the latter days" See SPECIAL TOPIC: THE LAST DAYS  and   SPECIAL TOPIC: THIS AGE AND THE AGE TO COME

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:31 "the Lord your God is a compassionate God"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:31 "the Lord your God is a compassionate God" For the names of deity (El, YHWH, Elohim) see SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, A., C., D.

The ADJECTIVE "compassionate" (BDB 933) means "merciful" or "compassionate." It is one of several characteristics used to describe Israel's God (cf. Exod. 34:6 is the first list of YHWH's characteristics).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

▣ "He will not fail you nor destroy you nor forget the covenant with your fathers" There are three negated VERBS:

  1. fail ‒ BDB 951, KB 1276, Hiphil IMPERFECT (literally "let the hands fall"), which means abandon or forsake (cf. Deut. 31:6,8; Josh. 1:5; 10:6; 1 Chr. 28:20; Heb. 13:5)
  2. destroy ‒ BDB 1007, KB 1469, Hiphil IMPERFECT, which means "ruin," "spoil," and "destroy" (cf. Deut. 9:26; 10:10; Jer. 30:11)
  3. forget ‒ BDB 1013, KB 1489, Qal IMPERFECT (cf. Lev. 20:45, see SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

The difficult theological issue is how to take seriously God's promises in this verse in relation to the previous covenant demands. The inability of Israel to keep the covenant is documented in their history and in Paul's writings (cf. Romans 2-3; Galatians 3). The need for a "new covenant," based not on human performance but divine will and action is God's answer (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-36). God never changes, but neither does Israel! God's demand for a righteous people cannot be met in human effort or will! We need a new heart and a new spirit!

You must decide! Is the OT to be viewed through the NT or is the NT to be viewed through the OT? Is the focus on Israel or the world? Is the issue faith or race? If there is a "parenthesis" in God's eternal plan of redemption, it is not the church, but Israel (i.e. dispensationalism)!

I am becoming more and more uncomfortable with Dispensationalism. I think a good YouTube video on this subject is by Steve Gregg, "Deconstructing Dispensationalsim" (Deconstructing Dispensationalism).

SPECIAL TOPIC: Why OT Covenant Promises seem Different from NT Covenant Promises

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:32 "ask"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:32 "ask" The VERB (BDB 981, KB 1371, Qal IMPERATIVE) means inquire of YHWH about the uniqueness of Israel's relationship to Himself (cf. Deut. 4:32-40).

▣ "since the day that God created man on earth" This refers to Genesis 1-2; also see Psalm 104. The Hebrew "adam" is used in a generic sense.

4:33
NASB, NKJV, Peshitta  "the voice of God"
NRSV, REB, JPSOA  "the voice of a god"
TEV  "a god speaks"
NJB, LXX  "the voice of a living god"

The MT has no ARTICLE with Elohim. The UBS Text Project, p. 273, gives the NASB translation of the MT an "A" rating. The question comes, is it a generic reference or a specific reference? For Israel it surely refers to their covenant Deity (cf. v. 39, Elohim with the ARTICLE).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:34 "signs"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:34 "signs" See SPECIAL TOPIC: SIGN (OT)

▣ "by a mighty hand and by an outstretched arm" These are anthropomorphic idioms used to describe YHWH's power of deliverance on behalf of Israel (cf. Deut. 5:15; 6:21; 7:19; 9:29; 11:2; 26:8). In some texts the phrase is shortened to "mighty hand" (cf. Deut. 3:24; 6:21; 7:8; 9:26; Josh. 4:24) or "outstretched arm" (cf. Deut. 9:29; Exod. 6:6). This idiomatic terminology has a specific parallel in Egyptian texts related to the "king" (NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 92).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:35 "that you might know"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:35 "that you might know" The miracles of Deut. 4:34 were for the purpose of establishing Israel's faith (cf. Exod. 7:5,17; 10:2; 31:13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW (USING MOSTLY DEUTERONOMY AS A PARADIGM)

▣ "the Lord, He is God" See SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C. (Elohim) and D. (YHWH)

▣ "no other besides Him" There is no other spirit or god in YHWH's category (e.g. Deut. 4:39; 6:4; 32:39). See full note at Deut. 6:4.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANGELS AND DEMONS

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:36 "Out of the heavens He let you hear His voice"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 4:36 "Out of the heavens He let you hear His voice" This verse is referring to YHWH's physical manifestation of His presence on Mt. Horeb/Sinai, recorded in Exodus 19-20.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:37 "Because He loved your fathers"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:37 "Because He loved your fathers" This refers to YHWH's choice of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob (the Patriarchs of Genesis 12-50, cf. Deut. 7:7-8; 10:15).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S GRACE ACTS TO ISRAEL

▣ "He chose" Election (i.e. "chose," BDB 103, KB 119, Qal IMPERFECT with waw) in the OT is for service (e.g. Cyrus II, Isa. 44:24-45:7), not salvation as in the NT.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HE CHOSE US

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELECTION

▣ "He personally brought you from Egypt" The term "personally" (BDB 815) is literally "face," which denotes YHWH's personal presence (cf. Deut. 5:4; Gen. 32:30; Exod. 33:14-15; Isa. 63:9, "the angel of His presence"). This is also the root behind the Hebrew idiom "face to face" (cf. Exod. 33:11; Deut. 34:10 and same thought in "mouth to mouth" of Num. 12:8). Both speak of personal intimacy (e.g. John 1:1-2).

YHWH truly is the God who is with us (i.e. Immanuel of Isa. 7:14; 8:8,10). Sin breaks the intimacy and YHWH turns His face away (cf. Deut. 31:17; Lev. 17:10; 20:3,6; Isa. 59:2; Jer. 18:17; Ezek. 7:22; 39:23,24,29). I think this even happened to Jesus on the cross as He bore the sin of the world (cf. Mark 15:33-34).

4:38
NASB, NKJV, NRSV, Peshitta  "nations greater and mightier"
TEV, REB  "nations greater and more
  powerful"
NJB, JPSOA  "nations greater and more
  populous"

These nations can be seen (Deut. 4:38; 7:1; 11:23; Josh. 23:9) as"

  1. more numerous in population (cf. Deut. 7:7)
  2. inhabitants physically greater in size (i.e. giants, Num. 13:22,28,33; Deut. 1:28)

▣ "as it is today" This seems to be a textual marker of a later editor's statement, but it can refer to the kingdoms of Sihon and Og on the eastern side of Jordan. See note at Deut. 3:14.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:39
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:39 This is another strong statement of monotheism. See note at Deut. 6:4.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:40 "statutes. . .commandments"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:40 "statutes. . .commandments" See SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION.

▣ "that you may live long on the land" The VERB is literally "prolong" (BDB 73, KB 88, Hiphil IMPERFECT, cf. Exod. 20:12; Deut. 4:26,40; 5:16,33; 6:2; 11:9; 17:20; 22:7; 25:15; 30:18; 32:47). Notice the conditional element!

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOVERNMENT

▣ "which the Lord your God is giving you for all time" The VERB (BDB 678, KB 733, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE) must be interpreted in light of the meaning of "for all time." The Hebrew term and concept of "forever" must be interpreted

  1. in literary context
  2. in light of a conditional covenant

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam and aiōnios)

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:41 "Moses"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:41 "Moses" Notice the THIRD PERSON editor/scribe. YHWH spoke to Moses. Sometimes he wrote it down himself; sometimes he dictated it to another person, probably a Levitical priest.

▣ "three cities across the Jordan to the east" These cities are called "cities of refuge" (cf. Numbers 35; Deuteronomy 19; Joshua 20). There were six of them, three for each side of the Jordan. They were all Levitical cities (cf. Joshua 21), where the Levites, who had no land inheritance, lived.

They were part of the "eye for eye" justice system of Israel. If someone accidently killed a covenant partner then that family had the legal right to kill him (i.e. the blood avenger of Num. 35:12; Deut. 19:6,12; Josh. 20:3,5,9). If the one who accidentally killed another fled to one of these special cities, there was a trial by the elders; if he was found not to be a premeditated murderer, then he could live in the city safely (until the death of the High Priest). Then he could return to his home safely (in a legal sense).

Notice "across Jordan" is here qualified so as to refer to the eastern bank.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CITIES OF REFUGE

SPECIAL TOPIC: BLOOD AVENGER

SPECIAL TOPIC: MURDER

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:42 "unintentionally"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:42 "unintentionally" The negated term (BDB 395) refers to the death of a fellow Israelite accidentally, without premeditation or prejudice. We would call it manslaughter.

The lack of an evil motive is the key element. It becomes the theological heart of the sacrificial system. Any sin committed intentionally had no sacrifice available (cf. Exod. 21:12-14; Lev. 4:2,22,27; 5:15-18; 22:14; Num. 15:27,30; Deut. 17:12-13; Josh. 20:1-6). Even the national sacrifice by the High Priest on the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16) did not cover premeditated sin (cf. Ps: 51:14-17)! Are you not glad we are under the NT sacrifice of Jesus?!

At this point I would like to add a quote from NIDOTTE, vol. 2, discussing the concept of:

"'Unintentionally' or 'inadvertently' (Lev. 4:2) is both strategic and problematic (cf. Deut. 4:13,22,27; 5:15,18; 22:14; Num. 15:22,24-29). Because of it some scholars have concluded that the sin offering only treated inadvertent sin, that is, sins that were committed by mistake or sins which were done not knowing that the particular act was sinful (see Melgrom, 1991, 228-29). However, the word 'unintentionally' means basically 'in error' (the vb. means to commit an error, go astray). Although it can also mean that the error was unintentional or inadvertent (see e.g. Num. 35:11,15,22-23; Josh 20:39), this is not necessarily the case (see 1 Sam. 26:21; Eccl. 5:6)" (p. 94).

SPECIAL TOPIC: UNINTENTIONAL SINS

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:44-45 "Law. . .testimonies. . .statutes. . .ordinances"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 4:44-45 "Law. . .testimonies. . .statutes. . .ordinances" See SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:45 "these are the testimonies"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:45 "these are the testimonies" These are the words that Wisdom Literature used to describe the Torah, or the Law of God. The word "Torah" (BDB 435) means "teachings" of God. The Law was not given as a burden meant to break mankind. The oral traditions (i.e. Mishnah, Talmud) which grew up around the Law made it a great burden. The OT is nothing more than the loving, self-revelation of YHWH in the midst of human ignorance. The OT Law points up

  1. the seriousness of sin
  2. the frailty of mankind
  3. the need for a savior
  4. but it was given in love (cf. Ps. 19:7-9; Galatians 3)

▣ "which Moses spoke to the sons of Israel when they came out from Egypt" Moses is going over the Ten Commandments for the second time here. But the people who were hearing them this time were only children the first time they were given in Exodus 20 at Mt. Sinai. He is retelling it. Moses is doing for the children of Israel what he expects the fathers to do in their own homes (see full note at Deut. 4:10). Every generation has to tell the new generation about the acts and will of YHWH.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 4:46-49
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:46-49 These verses are an historical summary of the two victories on the eastern side of the Jordan River. The reason that God allowed two victories on the east side of Jordan is analogous to the concept of first fruits. The first fruits in Judaism are the sacrifice of a little bit of the harvest to prove that God is faithful and that the whole harvest is going to come. The defeat of the two Amorite kings on the east side of the Jordan said to Israel, "I love you. I promised to give you the land. You know that I mean it. Trust and obey me and I'll give you the rest" (i.e. conditional covenant)

This is another brief summary statement of the experience of Israel at the end of the wilderness wandering period in Moab.

4:48
NASB, NKJV, NJB, JPSOA  "Mount Sion"
NRSV, TEV, REB  "Mount Sirion"
LXX  "Mount Seon"
Peshitta  "Mount Serion"

The MT has "Sion," but from Deut. 3:9, we learn that the Sidonians called Mount Hermon "Sirion." The UBS Text Project, p. 274, gives "Sion" a "B" rating (some doubt). Both words refer to Mt. Hermon.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. Was OT faith basically a law to keep or a relationship with God?
  2. Why does the Bible stress parents teaching their own children about God?
  3. Why does God forbid man to make a physical representation of Him?
  4. How was Israel God's special treasure? And why?
  5. List the two prerequisites for a healthy lasting society.
  6. List the three consequences for breaking the covenant.
  7. Does this passage teach monotheism or henotheism?
  8. Why did God choose Israel?
  9. What was the purpose of the "eye for eye" revenge?
  10. Did the sacrificial system adequately deal with man's sin? Why or why not?
  11. How is Christ's sacrifice superior?

entries.title: Deuteronomy 5:1 "all Israel"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:1 "all Israel" The Law was for every Israelite (not an elite group), but Moses probably spoke to the elders who then told his words to all the people (i.e. families, tribes, clans).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name)

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELDERS

▣ "Hear" See note at Deut. 4:1.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (shema)

▣ "the statutes and the ordinances" See note at Deut. 4:1 and SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION.

▣ "learn them and observe them carefully" This phrase has three VERBALS:

  1. "learn them" (BDB 540, KB 531, Qal PERFECT with waw, cf. Deut. 4:10; 5:1; 14:23; 17:19; 18:9; 31:12,13
  2. "observe them" (BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal PERFECT with waw, cf. Deut. 4:2,6,9,40; 5:10,12,29,32; 6:2,3, 17 [twice], 25; 7:8,9[twice],11,12[twice], etc.
  3. "carefully," literally "do" (BDB 793, KB 889, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT)

These three VERBALS summarize the meaning of shema (BDB 1033, KB 1570, e.g. Deut. 4:1; 5:1,23,24,25,26, 27 [twice], 28 [twice]; 6:3,4; 9:1; 20:3; 27:9), which means "hear so as to do"! Spiritual knowledge and a godly obedient lifestyle are both crucial!

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel, vol. 1, pp. 143-144, lists the OT law codes:
    1. the Decalogue ‒ Exod. 20:2-17; Deut. 5:6-21
    2. the Code of the Covenant ‒ Exod. 20:22-23:33
    3. Deuteronomy ‒ Deuteronomy 12-26
    4. the Law of Holiness ‒ Leviticus 17-26
    5. the Priestly code ‒ Leviticus 11-16 (BDB 435)

      All of these are considered Torah (BDB 435). They are specific divine prescriptions on actions and attitudes.

  2. Types of Israeli laws
    1. Casuistic ‒ laws characterized by the "if. . .then" format. There are consequences to actions. These are usually guidelines for societies.
    2. Apodictic ‒ laws stated as general prohibitions (usually SECOND PERSON PLURAL statements ‒ "you shall not. . ."). These are usually guidelines for the spiritual life.

      SPECIAL TOPIC: LAWS IN THE ANE

  3. Cultural influences
    1. in content ‒ earlier law codes
      1. Lipit-Ishtar
      2. Code of Hammurabi
    2. in form ‒ Hittite treaties (Suzerain), which occur in several set patterns, but Deuteronomy and Joshua 24 follow the pattern of the 2000 B.C. period, which shows its historicity (cf. John H. Walton, Ancient Israelite Literature in Its Cultural Context, pp. 95-107; K. A. Kitchen, The Bible in Its World, pp. 80-95; see introduction to the book, VII.
      SPECIAL TOPIC: HITTITE (SUZERAIN) TREATIES

  4. The words of Exodus 20 have been slightly changed. These ten words were said to have been written by the finger of God. Therefore, which version, Exod. 20 or Deut. 20:5, is original?
     I think Moses modified lthe Exod. 20 version given to a nomadic desert community for a people about to enter and settle down in Canaan. For a good brief discussion, see Hard Sayings of the Bible, pp. 172-173.

  5. SPECIAL TOPIC: PAUL'S VIEWS OF THE MOSAIC LAW and SPECIAL TOPIC: MOSAIC LAW AND THE CHRISTIAN

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Deuteronomy 5:2 "The Lord our God"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:2 "The Lord our God" See SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C. and D.

▣ "made" This is literally "cut" (BDB 503, KB 500, Qal PERFECT [twice]). This was a method of OT covenant ratification (i.e. "to cut a covenant," cf. Gen. 15:18; 21:27,32; 31:44; Exod. 34:27; Deut. 5:3; 29:12; 31:16). Abraham took a goat, a bull, and other animals, cut them in half, laid the halves on each side, and walked through the middle of those halves as a sign of covenant. It possibly implies a curse on those who break the covenant (cf. Gen. 15:9-18; Jer. 34:18) or even a meal to seal the covenant.

▣ "covenant with us" See note at Deut. 4:13.

▣ "at Horeb" Horeb is the Hebrew word for Mt. Sinai.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOREB

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOCATION OF MT. SINAI

entries.title: Deuteronomy 5:3 "our fathers"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:3 "our fathers" Some scholars see this phrase referring to the Patriarchs, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, but others see it referring to the parents, the evil generation who died in the wilderness (cf. Num. 26:63-65). The next phrase seems to confirm the second option.

▣ "with all those of us alive here today" This refers to the children (i.e. under twenty years) of the evil generation. This clearly shows that the words of YHWH had relevance to this generation and every generation, including today.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 5:4 "face to face"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:4 "face to face" This refers to a personal encounter (not literally) at Mt. Horeb/Sinai in Exodus 19-20. It is a recurrent idiom (cf. Gen. 32:30; Exod. 33:11; Deut. 5:4; 34:10; Jdgs. 6:22; Ezek. 20:35).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FACE TO FACE

▣ "from the midst of the fire" This is a repeated reference to Exodus 19-20 (cf. Deut. 4:12,15,33,36; 5:4,22,24,26; 9:10; 10:4).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 5:5 "while I was standing between the Lord and you. . .for you were afraid"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 5:5 "while I was standing between the Lord and you. . .for you were afraid" The people were afraid of YHWH so Moses acted as a mediator between YHWH and the Israelites (cf. Exod. 19:16).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 5:6 "I am the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:6 "I am the Lord" This may be paraphrased: "I am the 'I Am.'" I am the ever living, only living God. I am the ever existing One. YHWH is a form of the Hebrew VERB "to be" (cf. Exod. 3:14).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "who brought you out of the land of Egypt" Notice that YHWH's grace and elective choice came before the Law was given. God chose Israel, she did not choose him. This choice was made plain to Abraham in the unconditional promise/covenant of Gen. 15:12-21. YHWH's redemptive plan is unconditional but how it impacts individuals and nations is conditional.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 5:7 "no other gods before Me"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:7 "no other gods before Me" "Before" (BDB 818 #7) is literally "before My Face," which is an idiom for "no other in My category" (cf. Exod. 20:3,23). YHWH is alone, unique, ever-existing! This is an assertion of monotheism (cf. Exod. 8:10; 9:14; Deut. 4:35,39; 33:26; 1 Sam. 2:2; 2 Sam. 7:22; 22:32; Isa. 46:9). This first assertion and command is the uniqueness of Israel's faith in a polytheistic Ancient Near East! See note at Deut. 6:4.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

entries.title: Deuteronomy 5:8 "an idol"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:8 "an idol" This is literally "graven image" (BDB 820). This can refer to

  1. any physical representation of YHWH (cf. Deut. 4:12,15-19,23,25). The golden calf of Exodus 32 was a representation of YHWH
  2. foreign idols (cf. Lev. 19:4; 26:1)

▣ "earth" See SPECIAL TOPIC: LAND, COUNTRY, EARTH (ארץ)

entries.title: Deuteronomy 5:9 "You shall not worship them or serve them"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:9 "You shall not worship them or serve them" These are two negated VERB forms:

  1. "worship" ‒ BDB 1005, KB 295 Hishtaphel IMPERFECT or Hithpael IMPERFECT, which means "bow down," "prostrate" (cf. Deut. 4:19; 8:19; 11:16; Exod. 20:5; 23:24; see SPECIAL TOPIC: WORSHIP)
  2. "serve" ‒ BDB 712, KB 773, Hophal IMPERFECT, which means "do" "serve as a slave," or "perform acts of worship (cf. Deut. 13:2; Exod. 20:5; 23:24

YHWH knew the "religious" and "superstitious" tendency of the fallen human heart and tried to protect the revelation of Himself and His purposes from the destructive influences of Near Eastern idolatry. Superstition is a terrible thing!

▣ "jealous" See note at Deut. 4:24.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: JEALOUS. . .ZEALOUS

▣ The VERB "visiting" (BDB 823, KB 955, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE) has several senses:

  1. visit to bless ‒ Gen. 21:1; 50:24,25; Exod. 13:19; Ruth 1:6; Ps. 65:9; 106:4; Jer. 27:22; 29:10; 32:5
  2. visit to punish ‒ Exod. 20:5; 34:7; Jer. 11:22; 13:21; 21:14; 24:25; Amos 3:2,14; Hosea 1:4; 2:15; 4:14; 12:2

Context, context, context; clarifies lexical options!

▣ "the iniquity of the fathers" The term "iniquity" (BDB 730) may be related to the similar root, "to twist" (BDB 730, e.g. 2 Sam. 19:20; 24:17; 1 Kgs. 8:47; Ps. 106:6). Israel is punished for her disobedience (e.g. Exod. 20:5; 34:7; Lev. 18:25; Num. 14:18; Deut. 19:15; Jer. 25:12; 36:31; Amos 3:2).

  1. iniquity ‒ עון
  2. twist ‒ עוה

SPECIAL TOPIC: SIN IN THE OT, A. 2.

▣ "on the children, and on the third and fourth generations of those who hate Me" Notice the punishment is not arbitrary or indiscriminate, but directed toward those who "hate" YHWH (BDB 971, KB 1338, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE). This implies that unbelief runs through families. The influence of the parents is crucial to the development of faith (see notes at Deut. 4:10). In the ANE several generations of families lived together. One generation's unbelief and/or disobedience affected the entire family. This is part of the Hebrew concept of corporality (i.e. one affects the whole—Adam, Achan, David, Jesus).

To this sense of corporality must be added the individual aspect of faith (cf. Deut. 24:16; 2 Kgs. 14:6; Jer. 31:29-30; Ezekiel 18)!

Just a personal note, all of us come from sinful families. All of us are affected by them. The sins of the parents are passed on to the children. But, thank God for

  1. Deut. 7:9, where the faith of the godly parents (not sinless) is passed on, not to the third and fourth generations but to the thousandth generations (note Deut. 5:10).
  2. Ezekiel 18. The sin of a parent does not necessarily affect the faith of the children.

Sin has consequences through time, but faith also has consequences through time and eternity.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 5:10 "showing"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:10 "showing" This VERB (BDB 793, KB 889) is a Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE, which matches the ongoing action of the VERB in Deut. 5:9.

▣ "lovingkindness" This refers to YHWH's covenant love and loyalty.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS (hesed)

▣ "to thousands" These two verses help me see the nature of YHWH. His basic nature is longsuffering love, but He does punish those who wilfully reject Him (especially those who have some knowledge of His revelation, i.e. the covenant people). The numbers in these two verses make my point.

  1. visiting iniquity to the third and fourth generations
  2. showing covenant love to the thousandth generation (cf. Deut. 7:9)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THOUSAND (eleph)

▣ "those who love Me and keep My commandments" It is a characteristic of Deuteronomy to link obedience to YHWH's covenant to love for YHWH (cf. Deut. 6:5; 7:9; 10:12; 11:1,13,22; 13:3; 19:9; 30:6,16,20).

YHWH's love is not capricious, but clearly defined. He shows no partiality. His initiating covenant love (i.e. unconditional promise of mankind's redemption) is maintained by covenant obedience (i.e. conditional covenant of YHWH's mandated human response).

"Keep" (BDB 1036, KB 1581) is the key concept in this chapter (cf. Deut. 5:1,10,12,29,32 and many more times in Deuteronomy). The OT was based on the grace of YHWH and lifetime human obedience/performance. YHWH wanted to show human's inability to respond appropriately (cf. Galatians 3). The NT (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-36) is based on God's gracious initiation and redemption in Christ. Believers are still destined to be righteous (cf. Eph. 1:14; 2:10), but they have been accepted and forgiven by grace through faith (cf. Eph. 2:8-9). Now they obey/perform out of a sense of gratitude and family love (i.e. "those who love Me"). The goal is the same, a righteous (Christlike) people, but the mechanism has changed from human performance to Christ's performance (cf. Isaiah 53; Mark 10:45; 2 Cor. 5:21).

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

entries.title: Deuteronomy 5:11 "You shall not take the name. . ."
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:11 "You shall not take the name. . ." The VERB (BDB 669, KB 724, Qal IMPERFECT) means "to lift," to carry," or "to take." It seems to imply an act of speech. The Israelites were called on to speak "the name" in worship (cf. Deut. 6:13; 10:20), but not the name of other gods!

This emphasis begins in Gen. 4:25-26, where the line of Seth "began to call upon the name of the Lord"; Abraham did the same (Gen. 12:8; 21:33); Isaac did the same (Gen. 26:25). This same concept is put in an eschatological setting by Joel 2:28-32. This is continued by the Apostle Peter on Pentecost and asserted to be fulfilled (cf. Acts 2:14-21); the Apostle Paul uses the phrase to offer universal salvation in Rom. 10:9-13.

The name represents the person and character of YHWH. The Israelites were to be a kingdom of priests to the world (cf. Exod. 19:5-6), but the tragedy is that their covenant disobedience, which caused YHWH to punish them (cf. Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 27-29), meant that the message to the world was distorted by:

  1. God's judgment of Israel instead of blessing
  2. God's people turning to idolatry
  3. God's people's developing arrogance, exclusiveness, and self-righteousness!

SPECIAL TOPIC: CALL ON HIS NAME

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF THE LORD

▣ "in vain" This term (BDB 996) means "empty," "non-existent," "vain" (cf. Exod. 20:7; Ps. 139:20). This is the same word used in Deut. 5:20 for a "false" witness. It is possible that this commandment does not refer to taking oaths in YHWH's name (cf. Deut. 6:13; 10:20), but in using His name in false legal testimony. Israel became a "false" witness to the character and purposes of YHWH because of their recurrent disobedience, which resulted in YHWH's judgment (cf. Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 27-29).

SPECIAL TOPIC: EMPTY, VAIN, FALSE, NOTHINGNESS

▣ "for the Lord will not leave him unpunished" The VERB (BDB 667, KB 720, Piel IMPERFECT which means "acquit") is imagery for something clean, thereby innocent or free from guilt (cf. Exod. 20:7; 34:7; Num. 14:18; Jer. 30:11; 46:28; Joel 3:21; Nah. 1:3). There are consequences to human sin. To misrepresent YHWH is a most serious sin, especially for those who know Him (cf. Luke 12:48; Heb. 10:26-31)!

entries.title: Deuteronomy 5:12 "Observe"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:12 "Observe" This VERB (BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE) means "keep" and is used repeatedly in Deuteronomy.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

▣ "the sabbath" See SPECIAL TOPIC: SABBATH (OT)

▣ "holy" This term (BDB 992) means "rest" or "cessation of activity." The usage as a day of worship starts with Gen. 2:2-3, where YHWH uses His rest as a pattern for animals (cf. Exod. 23:12) and mankind (humans need a regular schedule of work, rest, and worship). The first specialized use of this day by Israel was in Exod. 16:25-26 in the gathering of manna. It then becomes part of "the Ten Words" (cf. Exod. 20:8-11; Deut. 5:12-15). This is one example where the Ten Words in Exodus 20 are slightly different from the Ten Words in Deuteronomy 5. Deuteronomy is preparing Israel for the settled, agricultural life in Canaan, while Exodus 20 dealt with their desert wandering period.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY

entries.title: Deuteronomy 5:13 "work"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 5:13 "work" Laws like Deut. 5:13-14 caused the development of the Oral Traditions (i.e. Mishnah, Talmud, cf. Matt. 5:21-48) to be written because a question like, "What is work?" became crucial. The rabbis devised a definition so that the faithful Jew would not break the Law. The ambiguity of the written Law caused the legalistic Oral Law to be developed.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 5:14 "seventh day is a sabbath"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:14 "seventh day is a sabbath" The Sabbath was a day of rest (BDB 992). There are two origins given for the Sabbath: Exodus 20:11 orients it to Genesis 1-2, while Deuteronomy orients it to the Egyptian bondage (cf. Deut. 5:15). It became a covenant marker (like circumcision) of YHWH's people (cf. Exod. 31:13,17; Ezek. 20:12,20). Obedience was mandated (cf. Isa. 56:2; 58:13; Jer. 17:21-22).

Like the sun, moon (cf. Gen. 1:14), and seasons, the Sabbath provided a division of time for mankind's activities (cf. Ecclesiastes 3). The seven day week became a way to mark special days and years (cf. Exodus 23 and Leviticus 23). Specifically, the Sabbath begins on Friday evening and goes through Saturday evening, because Israelites marked the day in Genesis 1 categories ("evening and morning," cf. Gen. 1:5,8,13,19,23,31).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SABBATH (OT)

entries.title: Deuteronomy 5:15 "You shall remember"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:15 "You shall remember" See note at Deut. 7:18.

▣ "that you were a slave in the land of Egypt" Moses uses this experience of slavery to motivate the Israelites to compassionate action toward underprivileged people in their society:

  1. to allow servants (and animals) a day of rest ‒ Deut. 5:12-15; 16:12
  2. to freely release and empower Hebrew slaves ‒ Deut. 15:12-15
  3. to be fair and just with the underprivileged and disenfranchised ‒ Deut. 24:17-18
  4. to leave the corners of the field and the second gathering of crops for the poor ‒ Deut. 24:19-22 (i.e. gleaning)

This phrase is also used numerous times to warn Israel to act appropriately in light of YHWH's gracious gift of the land (e.g. Deut. 6:10-15) and to obey the covenant (e.g. Deut. 8:1-10) lest serious consequences come (e.g. Deut. 8:11-20)

SPECIAL TOPIC: GLEANINGS

▣ "hand" See SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN

entries.title: Deuteronomy 5:16 "Honor"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:16 "Honor" This VERB (BDB 457, KB 455, Piel IMPERATIVE) originally meant "to be heavy" and developed a metaphorical meaning of "give due weight to" or "honor." This honor is not based on agreement, but authority and respect. In a sense it models the relationship between God and mankind. A submissive attitude toward authority is crucial in religious life!

Jesus mentions these commandments several times as well as other portions of Deuteronomy:

  1. Deut. 5:16 ‒ Matt. 15:4; Mark 7:10
  2. Deut. 5:16-20 ‒ Matt. 19:18-19a; Mark 10:19; Luke 18:20
  3. Deut. 5:17 ‒ Matt. 5:21
  4. Deut. 6:4-5 ‒ Matt. 22:37; Mark 12:29-30; Luke 10:27
  5. Deut. 6:13 ‒ Matt. 4:10; Luke 4:8
  6. Deut. 6:16 ‒ Matt. 4:7; Luke 4:12
  7. Deut. 19:15 ‒ Matt. 18:16
  8. Deut. 19:15 ‒ Matt. 5:38

Paul also quotes Deuteronomy often:

  1. Deut. 5:16 ‒ Eph. 6:2-3
  2. Deut. 5:21 ‒ Rom. 7:7
  3. Deut. 19:15 ‒ 2 Cor. 13:1
  4. Deut. 21:23 ‒ Gal. 3:13
  5. Deut. 25:4 ‒ 2 Cor. 9:9; 1 Tim. 5:18
  6. Deut. 27:26 ‒ Gal. 3:10
  7. Deut. 30:12-14 ‒ Rom. 10:6-8
  8. Deut. 32:21 ‒ Rom. 11:8
  9. Deut. 32:35 ‒ Rom. 12:19-20
  10. Deut. 32:43 ‒ Rom. 15:10

(cf. Richard N. Longenecker, Biblical Exegesis in the Apostolic Period, pp. 42-43, 92-95). Apparently the NT writers used the OT extensively, but not legalistically!

SPECIAL TOPIC: HONOR FATHER AND MOTHER

▣ "and your mother" This shows high regard for motherhood even though in the Oriental society women were legally on the level of chattel or property. A Hebrew mother was honored in her own home. The authority of parents was strictly respected (cf. Exod. 21:17; Deut. 27:16). Both were to be respected and obeyed (cf. Prov. 1:8; 6:20; 15:20; 19:26; 20:20; 23:22-25; 30:11,17).

SPECIAL TOPIC: WOMEN IN THE BIBLE

▣ "your days may be prolonged" Verse 33; 4:40; 11:9 show that this was a promise to a society, not primarily to an individual. If a society is characterized by honor in the home and respect for family life, that society will be stable and last through time. See note at Deut. 4:40.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 5:17 "murder"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:17 "murder" The Hebrew VERB "murder" (BDB 953, KB 1283, Qal IMPERFECT) originally meant "to violently crush." Life belongs to God. This does not mean killing of any kind because Israel had both capital punishment (e.g. Num. 35:30) and Holy War (e.g. 20:13,16-17). The commandment is saying "Thou shalt not violently murder for selfish reasons or revenge" or "do not commit non-legal, premeditated murder." In my opinion this passage cannot be used as a biblical admonition against military service or capital punishment.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NOTES ON EXODUS 20 (MURDER)

SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE AND WAR

entries.title: Deuteronomy 5:17-21
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:17-21 These are laws that are common to all eastern societies. From archaeological discoveries we know of the Babylonian Law Codes of Lipit-Ishtar and Hammurabi which predate the Law of Moses by several hundred years. The Code of Hammurabi is similar to the Ten Commandments. This similarity shows

  1. that there are some things that are innately wrong in every situation and society
  2. that Moses was a child of his own day and culture as well as a prophet of God

SPECIAL TOPIC: LAWS IN THE ANE

entries.title: Deuteronomy 5:18 "adultery"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:18 "adultery" In the OT adultery (BDB 610, KB 658, Qal IMPERFECT) refers to only extramarital sexual activities. This was a serious crime because of OT views of the afterlife. They believed that in some sense a person lived on through his seed. Also, the importance of tribes inheriting and passing on land allotted to them by YHWH made adultery a significant issue.

Notice, the first law is faithfulness to parents; the second law is faithfulness in not taking your brother's life; the third idea is faithfulness within the home. Even betrothed women were treated as married (cf. Deut. 22:23ff). Mary was accused of unfaithfulness because she was betrothed to Joseph.

This idea of adultery is often used symbolically for idolatry (i.e. spiritual adultery). Ezekiel and Hosea analogously present YHWH as a husband to Israel, therefore, when Israel went after other gods, it was called "going a whoring" and was considered spiritual adultery or faithlessness.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ADULTERY

entries.title: Deuteronomy 5:19 "steal"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:19 "steal" This is probably a reference to kidnaping and selling (BDB 170, KB 198, Qal IMPERFECT, cf. Deut. 24:7; Exod. 21:16), because of the context of the surrounding laws. This expresses a faithfulness to one's covenant brother whose life belongs to God. All of the surrounding laws brought the death penalty. This seems harsh for petty theft.

SPECIAL TOPIC: STEALING

entries.title: Deuteronomy 5:20 "bear false witness"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:20 "bear false witness" In ancient societies, when accused of something, it was the responsibility of the accused to prove the accuser wrong rather than our modern American judicial practice of assuming one innocent until proven guilty. If you proved your accuser wrong he had to take the penalty for the crime he accused you of (cf. Deut. 19:16-21). Since disobedience to the Ten Words caused death, false witness was a serious crime! Bearing false witness reveals an unfaithfulness within the community of faith. Lies destroy the reputation and take an innocent life of a covenant brother or sister. God takes this lying seriously (cf. Job 17:5; Ps. 101:5; Prov. 11:9; Jer. 9:8-9).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FALSE WITNESS

entries.title: Deuteronomy 5:21 "shall not covet. . .shall not desire"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:21 "shall not covet. . .shall not desire" These two VERBS are synonymous:

  1. "covet" ‒ BDB 326, KB 325, Qal IMPERFECT, means "a strong desire" for material things, which can be positive or negative. In this context it is an uncontrollable, selfish desire for something which belongs to a covenant brother.
  2. "desire" ‒ BDB 16, KB 20, Hithpael IMPERFECT, means "desire" (cf. Deut. 14:26) or "lust" (often has a sexual context as in Deut. 5:21) for more and more for me at any cost (e.g. Num. 11:4; Ps. 106:14; Prov. 13:4; 21:26; 23:3,6; 24:1).

This relates to one's inner attitudes and motives. It is capstone to all the other commandments. This is the only commandment that deals with why, not how. This one says not only "don't do" but "don't think this." Jesus taught that we should not only not kill, we should not hate, or display an attitude that might result in murder. Jesus took this last commandment and raised the rest of the commandments to the level of inner motive and attitude as over against outer action (cf. Matt. 5:17-48). There is all the difference in the world in a man who does not steal because it is not pleasing to God and the man who does not steal because he is afraid of getting caught. One is acting on biblical principles and the other is acting on self-interest.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVETING

entries.title: Deuteronomy 5:22 "He added no more"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:22 "He added no more" The Ten Words (Decalog) and their explanations are from YHWH, not Moses (compare Exod. 31:18 & 34:27-28). This is revelation (from God), not human discovery or rationalization. The phrase "and He added no more" is a literary way of asserting a complete revelation (cf. Deut. 4:2; 12:32).

Verses 22-27 are referring to the experience of Israel at Mt. Horeb/Sinai and recorded in Exodus 19-20.

This revelation must be respected and untampered with (cf. Deut. 4:2; 12:32; Prov. 30:6; Eccl. 3:14).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 5:23 "all the heads of your tribes and your elders"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:23 "all the heads of your tribes and your elders" The elders came to Moses because they were frightened (cf. Deut. 5:25-26; Exod. 19:16,18; 20:18-20) by the physical manifestations connected to YHWH's personal presence on Mt. Horeb/Sinai.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELDERS

SPECIAL TOPIC: CAN HUMANS SEE GOD AND LIVE?

entries.title: Deuteronomy 5:24 "His glory and His greatness"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:24 "His glory and His greatness" The Hebrew root "glory" (BDB 458; see SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY [OT]) is the same root as "honor" (BDB 457) of Deut. 5:16. Both are commercial terms meaning "heavy" or "weighty," which came to denote honor. It is used often of God's

  1. name (e.g. Ps. 29:2; 66:2; 79:9; 96:8)
  2. person (e.g. Exod. 24:16-17; 33:18,22; 40:34-35; Num. 14:22)
  3. actions (e.g. Exod. 16:7,12)

The second term "greatness" (BDB 152) is often used of God in Deuteronomy (cf. Deut. 3:24; 5:24; 9:26; 11:2; 32:3; Ps. 150:2). See notes at Deut. 4:31 and 10:17.

▣ "that God speaks with man" God does reveal Himself and humanity can understand and relate to Him! This is the basis of our understanding of God's revelation and God's covenant requirements.

SPECIAL TOPIC: INSPIRATION

entries.title: Deuteronomy 5:27 "Go near and hear all that the Lord our God says"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:27 "Go near and hear all that the Lord our God says" This has two Qal IMPERATIVE VERBS:

  1. "go near" ‒ BDB 897, KB 1132, which means "come near" or "approach." Approaching YHWH often had dangerous consequences (cf. Exod. 16:7; Lev. 16:1; Num. 16:16).
  2. "hear" ‒ BDB 1033, KB 1570, this is the often repeated VERB shema (i.e. "we will hear and do it")

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (shema)

entries.title: Deuteronomy 5:28-33
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:28-33 Notice that God says "that it may be well for you." These commandments weren't given to burden the people. God gave them to give His people freedom. God gave His laws to give us a whole, healthy, and happy life. They are necessary because of the fall of humanity in Adam.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

entries.title: Deuteronomy 5:29 "Oh that they had such a heart. . .and would keep all My commandments"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:29 "Oh that they had such a heart. . .and would keep all My commandments" This introductory exclamation ("Oh that they had," BDB 566 plus BDB 678, KB 733, Qal IMPERFECT) is a common phrase in the OT used twenty-five times, mostly in Job (NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 209). Here it expresses a wish (cf. 2 Sam. 18:33; Ps. 55:6).

God longs for mankind's happiness and peace, but this involves responsibilities. If they would obey, it would be good for them, for their children, for their children's children and on and on (cf. Deut. 27-29).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART

entries.title: Deuteronomy 5:30,31
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:30,31 These two verses have a series of commands:

  1. "go" ‒ BDB 229, KB 246, Qal IMPERATIVE, Deut. 5:30
  2. "say" ‒ BDB 55, KB 65, Qal IMPERATIVE, Deut. 5:30
  3. "return" ‒ BDB 996, KB 1427, Qal  IMPERATIVE, Deut. 5:30
  4. "stand" ‒ BDB 763, KB 840, Qal IMPERATIVE, Deut. 5:31
  5. "speak" ‒ BDB 180, KB 210, Qal IMPERATIVE, Deut. 5:31
  6. "teach" ‒ BDB 540, KB 531, Piel IMPERFECT (possibly in this context COHORTATIVE in meaning), Deut. 5:31

entries.title: Deuteronomy 5:31 "all the commandments and the statutes and the judgments"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:31 "all the commandments and the statutes and the judgments" See SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION

▣ "which I give them to possess" There are two VERBALS in this phrase:

  1. "give" ‒ BDB, 678, KB 733, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE
  2. "to possess" ‒ BDB, 429, KB 441, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT

This statement is based on:

  1. God's promise to Abraham, Gen. 12:1-3; 15:18-21
  2. God's promise to Isaac, Gen. 26:3-5
  3. God's promise to Jacob, Gen. 28:13-15; 35:9-12
  4. God's promise to Israel, Gen. 15:16; Exod. 6:4,8; Deut. 4:38,40; 19:10; 20:16; 21:23; Josh. 1:2,3,6,11,13,15; 2:9,24; 18:3; 21:43; 24:13

God gave/promised a special land to Israel, but Israel had to

  1. take it
  2. settle it
  3. maintain covenant faithfulness in it (i.e. conditional covenant, cf. Deut. 4:40; 7:12-13; 8:1-20)

entries.title: Deuteronomy 5:32 "you shall not turn aside to the right or to the left"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:32 "you shall not turn aside to the right or to the left" This is an idiom related to God's word as a clearly defined path or road (cf. Ps. 119:105; Prov. 6:23). To deviate from God's clear path/road was sin (cf. Deut. 9:12,16; 17:11,20; 28:14; Josh. 1:7; 23:6; 31:29; 2 Kgs. 22:2; 2 Chr. 34:2; Prov. 4:27). See note at Deut. 2:27.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE WAY. . .THE PATH

entries.title: Deuteronomy 5:33 "You shall walk"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:33 "You shall walk" In this context "walk" means "lifestyle" (BDB 229, KB 246, Qal IMPERFECT). Biblical faith is not only laws to be kept, it is a daily lifestyle: 24 hours a day, 7 days-a-week relationship to YHWH by faith. This faith must issues in a godly life (i.e. Eph. 2:10; 4:1,17; 5:2,15). Obedience is the evidence of this faith relationship, not the basis or mechanism.

▣ "that it may be well with" The VERB (BDB 373, KB 370, Qal PERFECT with waw) is literally "pleasing" or "good." The ADJECTIVE is often used to describe the Promised Land (cf. Deut. 1:25,25; 3:25; 4:21,22, etc.). The VERB describes the good life God promises for covenant obedience (cf. Deut. 15:16; 19:13).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. What is the relationship between law and grace? Should Christians keep the Ten Commandments?
  2. What is the purpose of the Law?
  3. Why are the Ten Commandments different when comparing Exodus 20 and Deuteronomy 5?
  4. What is the purpose of the Sabbath? Why don't we worship on Saturday?
  5. What unifying theme do we see in Deut. 5:16-21?
