  9:22-24 9:22-24 9:22-24
9:25-29 9:25-29 9:25-29 9:25-29

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Deuteronomy 9:2 "the Anakim. . .sons of Anak"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:2 "the Anakim. . .sons of Anak" Etymologically this term means "long neck" and, therefore, refers to the giants.

  1. In Deut. 2:10-11 they are linked to the Rephaim
  2. in Num. 13:33 they are linked to the Nephilim

SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS USED FOR TALL/POWERFUL WARRIORS OR PEOPLE GROUPS (Giants)

SPECIAL TOPIC: "sons of God" in Genesis 6

▣ "know" See full note at Deut. 4:35.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 9:3 "Know"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:3 "Know" This VERB (BDB 393, KB 390, Qal PERFECT with waw) is used often and in several senses.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

▣ "a consuming fire" This is BDB 77 plus BDB 37, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPAL. This imagery is describing the judgment of God on the people of the land because of their wickedness (cf. v.4-5; Gen 15:16). See note at Deut. 4:24. For a good brief discussion of the imagery used to describe God see The Dictionary of Biblical Imagery, pp.332-336.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE

▣ "He will destroy them and He will subdue them before you" These two VERBS of conquest are parallel and denote YHWH's actions on Israel's behalf:

  1. "destroy" ‒ BDB 1029, KB 1552, Hiphil IMPERFECT
  2. "subdue" ‒ BDB 488, KB 484, Hiphil IMPERFECT

Also note that Israel must act in faith and attack:

  1. "you may drive them out" ‒ BDB 439, KB 441, Hiphil PERFECT with waw
  2. "destroy them quickly" ‒ BDB 1, KB 2, Hiphil PERFECT with waw plus the ADVERB (BDB 555 II)

Notice the theological and covenantal balance between the promised action of the sovereign YHWH and the mandated faithful response of the Israeli army and leaders. Both are crucial!

It is also to be noted that YHWH accomplished His task, but Israel did not complete the task of totally removing the indigenous inhabitants (cf. Judges 1-2). Israel should have acted quickly (cf. Deut. 7:22), but she did not!

entries.title: Deuteronomy 9:4-6 "Do not say in your heart when the Lord your God has driven them out before you, 'Because of my righteousness'"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:4-6 "Do not say in your heart when the Lord your God has driven them out before you, 'Because of my righteousness'" This is similar to Deut. 8:11-20. God is showing the people again that He is acting, not because they are good, but because of

  1. the wickedness of the people in the land (cf. Gen. 15:12-21; Lev. 18:24-25; 20:13-14)
  2. His promise to their Patriarchs beginning in Gen. 12:1-3

He wants them to remember that He is in full control.

The initial VERB "say" (BDB 55, KB 65) is a Qal IMPERFECT, used in a JUSSIVE sense. The fallen heart of humanity is still ever present and spiritually dangerous.

The second VERB "has driven" (BDB 213, KB 239, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) shows YHWH's active involvement in the Conquest (cf. Deut. 6:19; JosH. 23:5).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S GRACE ACTS TO ISRAEL

entries.title: Deuteronomy 9:5 "It is not for your righteousness or for the uprightness of your heart"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:5 "It is not for your righteousness or for the uprightness of your heart" These two NOUNS are parallel in this context:

  1. "righteousness" ‒ BDB 842, cf. Deut. 6:25; 9:4,5,6; 24:13; 33:21, see SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS
  2.  "uprightness" ‒ BDB 449, means integrity or moral lifestyle, cf. 1 Chr. 29:17; Ps. 119:7

Israel is not being given the land Canaan because of her godliness, but because of

  1. the Canaanite's ungodliness (cf. Deut. 9:4; Gen. 15:12-21; Lev. 18:24-28, see note at Deut. 3:6)
  2. YHWH's greater purpose for Israel

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "to confirm the oath the Lord swore to your fathers, to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob" Notice the VERBS:

  1. "to confirm the oath" ‒ BDB 877, KB 1086, Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT
  2. "the Lord swore" ‒ BDB 989, KB 1396, Niphal PERFECT

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

▣ "righteousness" See SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

entries.title: Deuteronomy 9:6, 13 "you are a stubborn people"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:6, 13 "you are a stubborn people" This was originally an agricultural phrase referring to unruly oxen. Literally this means "hard of neck" or "stiff-necked" (BDB 904 CONSTRUCT BDB 791, cf. Deut. 9:6,7,13,24,27; 10:16; 31:27; Exod. 32:9; 33:3,5; 34:9).

SPECIAL TOPIC: STUBBORNNESS (OT)

entries.title: Deuteronomy 9:7-22
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:7-22 These verses refer to the actions of Israel while Moses was on Mt. Horeb/Sinai receiving the Law (cf. Exodus 32).

▣ "Horeb" See SPECIAL TOPIC: LOCATION OF MT. SINAI  and   SPECIAL TOPIC: HOREB

entries.title: Deuteronomy 9:7 "Remember, do not forget"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:7 "Remember, do not forget" These two initial VERBS (BDB 269, KB 269, Qal IMPERATIVES, cf. Deut. 5:15; 7:18 [twice]; 8:2; 9:7,27; 15:15; 16:3,12; 24:9,18,22; 25:17; 32:7 and BDB 1013, KB 1489, Qal IMPERFECT, functioning as a JUSSIVE, cf. Deut. 4:9,23; 6:12; 8:11,14,19 [twice]; 9:7) are to help Israel remember (see note at Deut. 7:18) and not repeat her lack of faith in YHWH, His promises and His power as they did on several occasions during the exodus and wilderness wandering period.

Moses mentions their act of idolatry and rebellion at the foot of Mt. Horeb in Deut. 9:8, where Aaron fashioned a golden calf at the insistence of the people (cf. Exodus 32)!

entries.title: Deuteronomy 9:7-8 "how you provoked the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 9:7-8 "how you provoked the Lord" See Exodus 16; 32; and Numbers 13-14; 16:21,25 as some examples.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 9:9 "the tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant which the Lord had made with you"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:9 "the tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant which the Lord had made with you" Obviously the phrase "tablets of stone, and the tablets of the covenant" are parallel. These were YHWH's words, not Moses'. This is revelation, not human opinion or discovery.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TEN COMMANDMENTS

entries.title: Deuteronomy 9:9,11,18 "forty days"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:9,11,18 "forty days" This number is often symbolic of a long, indefinite period of time, longer than a lunar cycle (i.e. 28 days) but less than a seasonal change. The time from leaving Mt. Horeb/Sinai to entering Canaan was thirty eight years.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE, #7

entries.title: Deuteronomy 9:9, 18 "I neither ate bread nor drank water"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:9, 18 "I neither ate bread nor drank water" This refers to two separate 40 day fasts meaning either

  1. a miraculous preservation (cf. Exod. 24:18; 34:28)
  2. a hyperbolic idiom for a limited fast (no food, but water)

This same period of fasting is used of Jesus in Matt. 4; Luke 4. He is the "new" Moses!

entries.title: Deuteronomy 9:10 "the two tablets of stone"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:10 "the two tablets of stone" Because of Hittite Suzerain Treaties as a possible historical background, this may refer to two complete copies of the Law. See introduction to the book, VII.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HITTITE (SUZERAIN) TREATIES

▣ "written by the finger of God" This is imagery for the divine origin of the Ten Words and their explanations (cf. Exod. 31:18; 32:15-16; Deut. 4:13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN (Anthropomorphic Language)

▣ "the Lord had spoken with you at the mountain from the midst of the fire" This is a recurrent theme (cf. Deut. 4:12,15,33,36; 5:5,22,24,26; 9:10; 10:4). The phrase emphasizes God's acts and the content of the personal covenant revelation at Mt. Horeb/Sinai (i.e. Exod. 19-20).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 9:12-14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:12-14 Moses remembers his dialogue with YHWH in Exodus 32

  1. "arise," Deut. 9:12 ‒ BDB 877, KB 1086, Qal IMPERATIVE
  2. "go down," Deut. 9:12 ‒ BDB 432, KB 434, Qal IMPERATIVE
  3. "let Me alone," Deut. 9:14 ‒ BDB 951, KB 1276, Hiphil IMPERATIVE
  4. "I may destroy them," Deut. 9:14 ‒ BDB 1029, KB 1552, Hiphil IMPERFECT used in a COHORTATIVE sense
  5. "blot out their names," Deut. 9:14 ‒ BDB 562, KB 567, Qal IMPERFECT used in a COHORTATIVE sense

▣ "for your people whom you brought out of Egypt" This VERB (BDB 422, KB 425, Hiphil PERFECT) is used many times of YHWH, but only here of Moses.

▣ "turned aside" This VERB (BDB 693, KB747, Qal PERFECT) is theologically parallel to שׁוב (BDB 996, KB 1427). This Hebrew root can denote idolatry or repentance.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

▣ "molten image" This (BDB 651) does not refer to idolatry, but a physical representation of YHWH. This was a violation of the second commandment (i.e. Exod. 20:4) They wanted a god they could see and touch like the peoples of Egypt and Canaan.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 9:14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:14 Is this an example of the wrath of God or is it a test of Moses' leadership (cf. Deut. 9:25ff, Exod. 32:30-35)?

▣ "blot out their name from under heaven" This is Hebrew imagery (cf. Deut. 25:5; Ps. 41:5) for the complete extermination of the covenant people, except Moses.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TWO BOOKS OF GOD

entries.title: Deuteronomy 9:15 "mountain was burning with fire"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:15 "mountain was burning with fire" Burning fire or bright light was a symbol of God's presence (cf. Exod. 19:16,18; Deut. 1:32-33; 4:33; 5:4; Isa. 66:15; Heb. 12:18).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEKINAH

entries.title: Deuteronomy 9:16 "You had made for yourselves a molten calf"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:16 "You had made for yourselves a molten calf" This same VERB (BDB 793 I, KB 899, Qal PERFECT) is used in Deut. 9:12 and 21. Here this image is called:

  1. in Exod. 32:4,8, "molten calf" (BDB 722)
  2. in Deut. 9:21, "the calf"
  3. in Deut. 9:12, a "molten image" (cf. Exod. 34:17; Lev. 19:4)

entries.title: Deuteronomy 9:17 "smashed them before your eyes"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 9:17 "smashed them before your eyes" The very day the covenant was written by God it was broken (both literally and figuratively).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 9:18
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 9:18 See SPECIAL TOPIC: INTERCESSORY PRAYER

entries.title: Deuteronomy 9:19 "the Lord listened to me"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:19 "the Lord listened to me" See Exodus 34. Notice the source of Moses' fear (BDB 388, KB 386, Qal PERFECT, cf. Deut. 28:60):

  1. YHWH's anger ‒ BDB 60, cf. Exod. 32:12
  2. YHWH's hot displeasure ‒ BDB 404, cf. Deut. 29:23
  3. YHWH's wrath ‒ BDB 893, KB 1124, Qal PERFECT, cf. Deut. 1:34; Lev. 10:6; Num. 16:22
  4. YHWH's threat to destroy you ‒ BDB 1029, KB 1552, Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, cf. Deut. 6:15; 9:20

Numbers 1 and 2 may function as a hendiadys (cf. TEV, NET Bible).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 9:20 "for Aaron"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 9:20 "for Aaron" Moses praying for Aaron is not recorded in Exodus 32.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 9:21
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:21 See Exodus 32:20. Notice how many VERBS are used to describe what Moses did to the golden calf, the sinful thing:

  1. "burned it," BDB 976, KB 1358, Qal IMPERFECT with waw
  2. "crushed it," BDB 510, KB 507, Qal IMPERFECT with waw, cf. 2 Kgs. 18:4; Micah 1:7
  3. "grinding it very small," BDB 377, KB 374, Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE
  4. "it was as fine as dust," BDB 200, KB 229, Qal PERFECT
  5. "threw its dust into the brook," BDB 1020, KB 1527, Hiphil IMPERFECT with waw

entries.title: Deuteronomy 9:22 "Taberah"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:22 "Taberah" This was one of the campsites of Israel (mentioned in Numbers 33). The place name comes from a word play on the VERB "to burn" (BDB 129). This was the geographical location where YHWH answered their constant complaining with a judgment of fire (cf. Num. 11:1-3,34-35). It was about a three day journey north of Mt. Horeb/Sinai, but the exact location is uncertain.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE EXODUS, III.

▣ "Massah" This was another location of conflict between YHWH and Israel during the exodus (cf. Exod. 17:7). It is usually linked to Meribah (cf. Deut. 33:8), but not always (cf. Deut. 6:16; 9:2).

  1. Massah means "testing" (BDB 650 III, cf. Deut. 6:16; 9:22; 33:8; Exod. 17:7; Ps. 95:8)
  2. Meribah means "strife" (BDB 937 II, cf. Exod. 17:7)

▣ "Kibroth-Hattaavah" The name means "graves of lust" (BDB 869, cf. Num. 11:31-35). Numbers 11 mentions movement recorded between Taberah and Kibroth-Hattaavah, but here in Deuteronomy the two sites are separate.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 9:23 "Go up and possess this land"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:23 "Go up and possess this land" These are both Qal IMPERATIVES and reflect YHWH's direct speech through Moses to Israel:

  1. "go up" ‒ BDB 748, KB 828
  2. "possess" ‒ BDB 439, KB 441 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: POSSESS THE LAND)

Notice again YHWH's command for Israel to act on her belief in His sovereignty and promises. But instead of faith Israel demonstrated unbelief:

  1. "you rebelled against the command" ‒ BDB 598, KB 632 , Hiphil IMPERFECT with waw, cf. Num. 20:24; 27:14; Deut. 1:26,43; 9:23; Ps. 107:11
  2. "you neither believed Him" ‒ BDB 52, KB 63, Hiphil PERFECT
    SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS IN THE OT
  3. "nor listened to His voice" ‒ BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal PERFECT (these Qal PERFECTS reflect a settled condition). This is exactly opposite of covenant obedience and responsibility.
    SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (shema)

▣ "you rebelled" See note at Deut. 1:26.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 9:24
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 9:24 Israel had always been rebellious!

entries.title: Deuteronomy 9:25
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:25 Moses' intercessory prayer uses two VERBS:

  1. "I fell down" ‒ BDB 656, KB 709
    1. Hithpael IMPERFECT with waw, Deut. 9:25
    2. Hithpael PERFECT, Deut. 9:25
  2. "I prayed" ‒ Deut. 9:26 - BDB 813, KB 933, Hithpael IMPERFECT with waw

SPECIAL TOPIC: INTERCESSORY PRAYER

▣ "forty days and nights" See SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE, #7

entries.title: Deuteronomy 9:26
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:26 Notice how Moses' prayer reminds YHWH of His covenant relationship:

  1. "Lord God" (literally, "adon YHWH," cf. Deut. 3:24 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord [adon and kurios])
  2. "Thy people" ‒ covenant title, cf. Deut. 9:29
  3. "Thine inheritance" ‒ covenant gift, cf. Deut. 9:29
  4. "Thou has redeemed ‒ BDB 804, KB 911, Qal PERFECT (see SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM). YHWH delivered them from slavery to a national entity (cf. Deut. 7:8; 9:26; 13:5)
  5. "Thou hast brought out of Egypt" ‒ BDB 422, KB 425, Hiphil PERFECT; this fulfilled YHWH's covenant promise to Abraham (cf. Deut. 9:29; Gen. 15:16-21)

YHWH acts because of who He is! He follows the redemptive plan He has for all peoples! The great hope of all mankind is the unchanging, gracious, merciful, loving character of YHWH (e.g. Exod. 34:6; Mal. 3:6). See notes at Deut. 4:31 and 10:17.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

▣ "with a mighty hand" This phrase and "outstretched arm" of Deut. 9:29 have both been found in Egyptian texts referring to the Egyptian king. This is a recurrent idiom (cf. Exod. 32:11; Deut. 4:34; 5:15; 6:21; 7:8,19; 9:26; 11:2; 26:8; 34:12; 2 Chr. 6:32; Ps. 136:12; Dan. 9:15). Moses chose phrases that Israel had heard before in relationship to Pharaoh. YHWH was their true king!

entries.title: Deuteronomy 9:26-29
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:26-29 Verses 26-29 show three reasons Moses gave to YHWH in answer to His question, "Why should I spare Israel?":

  1. His promise to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob (cf. Exod. 32:13)
  2. Canaan will misunderstand YHWH's character
  3. Canaan will not understand YHWH's judgment on Israel

 The paragraph contains three prayer request VERBS:

  1. "do not destroy," Deut. 9:26 ‒ BDB 1007, KB 1469, Hiphil JUSSIVE
  2. "remember," Deut. 9:27 ‒ BDB 269, KB 269, Qal IMPERATIVE
  3. "do not look" (i.e. "turn"), Deut. 9:27 ‒ BDB 815, KB 937, Qal JUSSIVE

Moses appeals to YHWH's character and eternal redemptive plan for all people as the basis for not destroying His disobedient covenant people. More is at stake than just one people group!

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Deuteronomy 9:27
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:27 Notice the character of Israel:

  1. "the stubbornness of this people" ‒ BDB 904, cf. Deut. 9:6,7,13,24,27 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: STUBBORNNESS)
  2. "their wickedness" ‒ BDB 957, cf. Jer. 14:20; Ezek. 3:19; 33:12
  3. "their sin" ‒ BDB 308, cf. Exod. 32:30; Deut. 9:18; Ps. 32:5; 51:5; Prov. 5:22; 13:6; 14:34; 21:4; 24:9 (Deuteronomy shares the vocabulary of the sages)

▣ "Your servants" See SPECIAL TOPIC: SERVANT LEADERSHIP

entries.title: Deuteronomy 9:28 "Otherwise the land from which You brought us may say"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:28 "Otherwise the land from which You brought us may say" YHWH, because of Your reputation and worldwide purpose of redemption, spare Israel. Another phrase used in the same sense is, "for God's namesake" (cf. Isa. 48:9-11; Ezek. 20:9,14,22,44; 36:21-23; Dan. 9:17-19).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Deuteronomy 9:29 "Your great power and Your outstretched arm"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:29 "Your great power and Your outstretched arm" See full note at Deut. 4:34.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. Why did God choose Israel?
  2. Is Deut. 9:14 a true reflection of God's nature? If not, what is it?
  3. List and discuss the three reasons Moses gives as to why YHWH should not destroy Israel.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 10:1 "the mountain"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:1 "the mountain" This refers to Mt. Horeb/Mt. Sinai.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOREB

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOCATION OF MT. SINAI

▣ Moses is to prepare for his second encounter with YHWH:

  1. "cut out for yourself two tablets of stone" ‒ BDB 820, KB 949, Qal IMPERATIVE, cf. Exod. 34:1,4
  2. "come up to Me" ‒ BDB 748, KB 828, Qal IMPERATIVE
  3. "make an ark" ‒ BDB 793, KB 889, Qal PERFECT with waw, cf. Exod. 25:10

The Hittite Treaties also required two copies of the agreements. One was given to the lesser king to read every year and the other placed in the temple of the greater king's god. See Introduction to the book, VII.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HITTITE (SUZERAIN) TREATIES

▣ "ark of wood for yourself" Exodus 37:1 says Bezalel made the Ark of the Covenant. Rashi says details of the ark were not even given until Moses came down the second time from Mt. Sinai. Therefore, Moses must have made a crude ark first and then later Bezalel made another more elaborate one (cf. Exod. 25:10-22). This first ark, made quickly by Moses, held only the Ten Commandments (cf. 1 Kgs. 8:9). The later one contained: the Ten Commandments, a sample of manna, and Aaron's rod that budded . For a good brief discussion see Roland de Vaux, Ancient Israel, vol. 2, pp. 292-303.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ARK OF THE COVENANT

entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Deuteronomy 10:2 "I will write"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:2 "I will write" YHWH wrote the law, verse 4 and Exod. 34:1. However, Exod. 34:27 speaks of Moses writing. Possibly YHWH wrote the Ten Commandments, but Moses wrote the descriptive and declarative material, which explained and applied it. It was not Moses' mentality nor his cultural influence, but God who originated the Law. God used cultural examples and forms that Moses would have been familiar with. In many ways the form of the Law is similar to Babylonian law, but the content is different.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOSES' AUTHORSHIP OF THE PENTATEUCH

SPECIAL TOPIC: LAWS IN THE ANE

▣ "in the ark" This depositing of special documents before the national god is characteristic of the ANE. Compare Egyptian Book of the Dead (in a box under Thot's feet) and the Hittite Suzerain Treaties of the second millennium B.C. See Introduction to the book,VII.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 10:3 "acacia wood"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:3 "acacia wood" This was a hard, brownish-orange wood (BDB 1008) that grows in the desert. A member of the mimosa family (see UBS Fauna and Flora of the Bible, pp.87-88). It was a common evergreen desert tree (cf. Isa. 41:19). This wood is associated with all of the furniture of the tabernacle.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ACACIA WOOD

entries.title: Deuteronomy 10:4 "the Ten Commandments"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:4 "the Ten Commandments" This is literally "the ten words" (BDB 796 CONSTRUCT BDB 182). These basic characteristic, foundational laws are very brief and stated in general principles. They mandate an intimate, exclusive relationship with YHWH (cf. Deut. 10:20), which is reflected in exclusive worship and obedience, which in turn mandates an appropriate commiserate relationship with other covenant members (and also non-members, cf. Deut. 10:17-19). Knowing YHWH impacts all of life and its priorities!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TEN COMMANDMENTS

▣ "on the mountain from the midst of the fire" This refers to YHWH's presence on Mt. Horeb/Sinai, recorded in Exod. 19:16-20. His presence is described as a "consuming fire on the mountain" (cf. Exod. 24:17). This phrase if used several times Deuteronomy (cf. Deut. 4:12,15,33,36; 5:4,24,26).

The fire (BDB 77) was imagery of YHWH's glorious presence:

  1. a torch in Gen. 15:17
  2. the burning bush in Exod. 3:2
  3. fire on Mt. Horeb, Exod. 19:18; Deut. 4:11,12,15,33,36
  4. the Shekinah pillar of fire in Exod. 13:21,22; 14:24; Num. 9:15,16; 14:14; Ps. 78:14 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEKINAH)
  5. coals of fire in Ezekiel's vision of YHWH's portable throne chariot in Ezek. 1:13; 10:2

The Ten Commandments are repeatedly said to have been spoken from the midst of the fire (cf. Deut. 4:12,15,33; 5:4,22,24,26; 9:10; 10:4). The commandments were personal, covenantal revelations from YHWH, not the mind of Moses.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE

entries.title: Deuteronomy 10:6,7,9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 10:6,7,9 SPECIAL TOPIC: LATER ADDITIONS TO DEUTERONOMY

entries.title: Deuteronomy 10:6 "the sons of Israel"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:6 "the sons of Israel" See SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name)

▣ "Beeroth Bene-jaakan to Moserah" The first two words (BDB 91,122) translate literally, "the wells of the sons of Jaakan" (cf. Num. 33:31). Moserah means "chastisement" (BDB 64). Moserah (possibly a district), which may be synonymous with Mt. Hor (cf. Num. 20:22-29; 33:38), is the place where Aaron died. These both refer to geographical areas where the Israelites wandered.

▣ "Aaron died there" Numbers 20:27-28 says this happened at Mt. Hor. Aaron, like Moses, did not enter the Promised Land because of his disobedience (cf. Num. 20:8,12).

▣ "Eleazar" His name means "God has helped" (BDB 46). He was the third son of Aaron (cf. Exod. 6:23). The first two sons were killed because they took YHWH's commands lightly (cf. Lev. 10:1-7; Num. 3:4). The Rabbinical Midrash says that because Lev. 10:9 restricts alcohol to priests while they are on duty that these two sons, Nadab and Abihu, were drunk.

The High Priesthood was to pass on through Aaron's family (cf. Exod. 29:9; 40:15; Num. 3:5-10; 25:13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: AARON'S SONS

SPECIAL TOPIC: LEVITICAL PRIESTS

entries.title: Deuteronomy 10:7 "Gudgodah"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:7 "Gudgodah" The meaning of the name is uncertain (BDB 151). It is seemingly identified with Hor-haggidgad in Num. 32:32. They are both places where Israel camped in her journey from Mt. Horeb/Sinai to Kadesh-barnea. The JPSOA has "Gudgod."

▣ "Jotbathah" The word means "pleasantness" (BDB 406, probably because of the presence of water). It is also mentioned as a campsite in Num. 33:33-34. The JPSOA has "Jotbath."

entries.title: Deuteronomy 10:8 "the Lord set apart the tribe of Levi"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:8 "the Lord set apart the tribe of Levi" The VERB "set apart" (BDB 95, KB 110, Hiphil PERFECT, cf. Num. 8:14; 16:9; 1 Chr. 23:13) means "to divide." Here the separation is for

  1. special cultic service related to the tabernacle and later temple
  2. blessings of the people (cf. Deut. 10:8; Lev.9:22-23; Num. 6:22-27)
  3. judging the people's disputes (cf. Deut. 21:5)
  4. judging between clean and unclean (cf. Lev. 10:10)

This VERB is parallel to "choose" (BDB 103, KB 119, cf. Deut. 18:5; 21:5).

Israel was to be separate from the other nations (cf. Lev. 20:24-26; 1 Kgs. 8:53; i.e. "a holy nation," cf. Exod. 19:6), so the tribe of Levi was to be separated from the other tribes as YHWH's special cultic servants. They were chosen because:

  1. Levi was from the tribe of Moses and Aaron
  2. the Levites took the place of the "first born" from Hebrew families (cf. Exod.13; Num. 3:12; 8:14-19)
  3. the Levites faithfully responded to Moses' call to punish Israel (cf. Exod. 32:25-29). In Gen. 29:34, Leah called her third son Levi because her husband did not love her, but the child's name meant, "Jacob was attached (or joined) to me" (BDB 532).

 As the priestly tribe, some of them will

  1. carry the ark of the covenant
  2. stand before the Lord to serve Him (i.e. all the duties at the tabernacle and later, the temple, in Jerusalem, cf 18:5; Num. 18:1-7
  3. bless in His name (e.g. Num. 6:24-27)

Later there will develop specific tasks given to some families of Levi to be priests and others will function as Levites. However, in Deuteronomy all Levites can act as priests (compare Deut. 31:9 and 25). See Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel, vol. 2, pp. 358-371.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LEVITICAL PRIESTS

entries.title: Deuteronomy 10:9 "Levi does not have a portion or inheritance"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:9 "Levi does not have a portion or inheritance" The tribe of Levi was not given any land allotment, however, parts of forty-eight cities were given to them with their surrounding pasture land (cf. Num. 35:1-8; Joshua 21).

▣ "the Lord is his inheritance" This denoted their special place of service (cf. Num. 18:20; Deut. 10:9; 18:1,2; Josh. 13:33; Ezek. 44:28)! This wonderful promise to the tribe of Levi became a cry from the heart of every true believer (cf. Ps. 16:5; 73:23-28; 119:57; 142:5; Lam. 3:24).

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVERS' INHERITANCE

entries.title: Deuteronomy 10:10 "forty nights like the first time"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:10 "forty nights like the first time" See Exod. 34:28; Deut. 9:18.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE, #7

▣ "the Lord was not willing to destroy you" This was Moses' intercessory ministry (see SPECIAL TOPIC: INTERCESSORY PRAYER, cf. Deut. 9:25-29; Exod. 32:9-14).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 10:11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:11 YHWH commanded Israel to act on what He had already promised-the conquest of the Promised Land:

  1. "arise" ‒ BDB 877, KB 1086, Qal IMPERATIVE SINGULAR, cf. Deut. 2:13,24, which are PLURAL and refer to Israel. Here the SINGULAR refers to Moses.
  2. "proceed" ‒ BDB 229, KB 246, Qal IMPERATIVE SINGULAR, literally means "break camp and start the next stage of the journey" (cf. Exod. 17:1; 40:36,38;l Num. 10:2,12; 33:1,2). Moses was to lead the people onward.
  3. "they may go in" ‒ BDB 97, KB 112, Qal IMPERATIVE PLURAL, which may be functioning as a JUSSIVE
  4. "and possess the land" ‒ BDB 439, KB 441, Qal IMPERFECT PLURAL, which may be functioning as a JUSSIVE (see SPECIAL TOPIC: POSSESS THE LAND)

Israel is called on to fulfill YHWH's oath to the Patriarchs (cf. Deut. 1:8; Josh. 21:43). God uses human instrumentality (e.g. Exod. 3:7-12)! It is His power and purpose, but His covenant people must act in faith and trust!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

entries.title: Deuteronomy 10:12-13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:12-13 See the following three Special Topics.

  1. SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S COVENANT REQUIREMENTS OF ISRAEL
  2. SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR (OT)
  3. SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

entries.title: Deuteronomy 10:13 "for your good"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 10:13 "for your good" Obedience brings blessing; disobedience brings judgment (cf. Deuteronomy 27-29; Leviticus 26).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 10:14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:14 This verse implies monotheism. This refers to the atmosphere of this planet, the universe (starry canopy), and the throne of God (i.e. the three heavens).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HEAVENS AND THE THIRD HEAVEN

entries.title: Deuteronomy 10:15
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:15 Notice the parallel ways of describing YHWH's election of Israel as His special people (i.e. "even you above all peoples," cf. Exod. 19:5-6; Deut. 7:6; 14:2):

  1. "set His affection" ‒ BDB 365 I, KB 362, Qal PERFECT, cf. Deut. 7:7. In Deut. 4:37 the other word for love (BDB 12, KB 17) is used.
  2. "He chose their descendants" ‒ BDB 103, KB 119, Qal IMPERFECT with waw, cf. Deut. 4:37.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HE CHOSE US

▣ "as it is this day" This may be a textual marker of a later editor. Notice "until this day" in v. 11. See note at Deut. 3:14.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 10:16
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:16 Israel was to respond to YHWH's choice by:

  1. "circumcise your heart" ‒ BDB 557, KB 555, Qal PERFECT with waw. This is imagery of openness to God (cf. Lev. 26:41; Deut. 10:16; 30:6; Jer. 4:4; 9:25-26). It is expressed in several ways:
    1. circumcise your flesh ‒ Gen. 17:14 (covenant sign)
    2. circumcise your lips ‒ idiom in Exod. 6:12,30
    3. circumcise your ears ‒ Jer. 6:10
    4. refers to a true heart, not just body circumcision ‒ Deut. 30:6; Jer. 4:4; 9:25-26; Ezek. 44:9; Rom. 2:28-29
  2. "stiffen your neck no more" ‒ BDB 904, KB 1151, Hiphil IMPERFECT, cf. Deut. 9:6,7,13,24,27; 31:27. See note at Deut. 2:30.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CIRCUMCISION

SPECIAL TOPIC: STUBBORNNESS (OT)

entries.title: Deuteronomy 10:17
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:17 Notice the accolades used to describe YHWH:

  1. God of gods ‒ BDB 43, cf. Ps. 136:2
  2. Lord of lords ‒ BDB 10, cf. Ps. 136:3
  3. the great God ‒ BDB 152, cf. Deut. 3:24; 5:24; 9:26; 11:2; 32:3; Neh. 1:5; 9:32
  4. the mighty God ‒ BDB 150, cf. Neh. 9:32; Ps. 24:8; Isa. 10:21
  5. the awesome God ‒ BDB 431, KB 432, Niphal PARTICIPLE, cf. Deut. 7:21; Neh. 1:5; 9:32

Several of these titles come from the titles of pagan gods which Israel began to use for YHWH. Listing of several descriptive titles for deity is common in the ANE. In the Babylonian Creation Account (i.e. Enuma Elish), Marduk is given 50 different, magnificient titles.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (NT)

▣ "who does not show partiality" The Hebrew phrase means "who does not lift up faces" (BDB 669, KB 724, Qal IMPERFECT plus BDB 815). This is used often of judges (cf. Deut. 1:17; 16:19; 24:17; Lev. 19:15). This implies that YHWH is a God of fair judgment (cf. Deut. 10:17; 2 Chr. 19:7).

▣ "nor take a bribe" YHWH's character is described in human legal terms (cf. Deut. 10:18-19). This is often associated with the above phrase. YHWH does not need anything from humans. He cannot be bribed or manipulated.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 10:18-19
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:18-19 Notice how the legal characteristics of YHWH in Deut. 10:18 are put into practice:

  1. "He executes (BDB 793 I, KB 889, Qal PARTICIPLE) justice for":
    1. the orphan
    2. the widow (cf. Deut. 24:17; 26:12-13; 27:19; Ps. 68:4-5)
  2. "shows His love (BDB 12, KB 17, Qal PARTICIPLE) for the alien by giving him" (BDB 678, KB 733, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT):
    1. food
    2. clothing

 The Israelites are to do these things for two reasons:

  1. It reflects the character of their God (Deut. 10:17; Isa. 58:6-7,10; see SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD [OT]).
  2. They know how being treated unfairly feels (Deut. 10:19; 24:18,22; Exod. 22:21; 23:9).

 Exodus 22:22-23 also mentions that YHWH will hear the prayers of these socially powerless ones and act on their behalf (cf. Ps. 146:9; Mal. 3:5; as will the Messiah, cf. Isa. 11:4). This is what the human kings of the ANE were expected to do, but in reality, they catered to the rich and powerful.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 10:20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:20 As the requirements of YHWH were set out in Deut. 10:12-13 by several INFINITIVE CONSTRUCTS, here they are set our again in Qal IMPERFECT VERBS:

  1. "fear the Lord" ‒ BDB 431, KB 432, cf. Deut. 5:29; 6:13; 13:4 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR (OT)
  2. "serve Him" ‒ BDB 712, KB 773, cf. Deut. 13:4
  3. "cling to Him" ‒ BDB 179, KB 209, cf. Deut. 11:22; 13:4
  4. "swear by His name" ‒ BDB 989, KB 1396, cf. Deut. 5:11; 6:13. See full note at Deut. 5:11 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: CALL ON THE NAME).

All of these relate to proper motives and actions of worship (see SPECIAL TOPIC: WORSHIP).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 10:21 "He is your praise"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:21 "He is your praise" The language of Deuteronomy has much in common with Wisdom Literature (see SPECIAL TOPIC: WISDOM LITERATURE). This phrase is seen in Ps. 109:1. There is no VERB with this phrase or the next one. They are strong affirmations that YHWH's redemptive action during the exodus and wilderness wandering period are praiseworthy:

  1. their praise (BDB 239)
  2. their Elohim (BDB 43; see SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.)

▣ "who has done these great and awesome things for you which you have seen" This refers to YHWH's actions and provisions during the exodus from Egypt, the wilderness wandering period (cf. Deut. 11:2), and that which will be repeated during the conquest!

entries.title: Deuteronomy 10:22 "seventy persons in all"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:22 "seventy persons in all" Seventy is a round number used of people. See Genesis 46:27; Exod. 1:5.

One text of Exod. 1:5, found at Qumran (i.e. Dead Sea Scrolls) has the number 75, which matches Acts 7:14-15. For a good brief discussion of the different numbers, see Hard Sayings of the Bible, p. 521 or Gleason L. Archer, Encyclopedia of Bible Difficulties, pp. 378-379.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE, #8

▣ "as the stars of heaven" This is a fulfillment of YHWH's promise to Abraham. See full notes at Gen. 13:16 and Deut. 1:10.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. What is the purpose of God's law (OT sense)?
  2. Does this chapter reflect monotheism? Where and how?
  3. How does Deuteronomy express God's love for mankind?

entries.title: Deuteronomy 11:1
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:1 Notice how the two VERBS of this verse are related. They are theologically parallel. One should result in the other!

  1. "love the Lord" ‒ BDB 12, KB 17, Qal PERFECT with waw, cf. Deut. 11:13,22. See full note at Deut. 5:10.
  2. "keep His charge" ‒ BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal PERFECT with waw (see SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP)

This is a repeat of Deut. 6:2,4-5; 10:12. Love is both an action (obedience) and a feeling ("with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your might," cf. Deut. 6:5; 13:3)

▣ "His charge, His statutes, His ordinances and His commandments" See SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Deuteronomy 11:2 "And know this day that I am not speaking with your sons who have not known and who have not seen"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:2 "And know this day that I am not speaking with your sons who have not known and who have not seen" Moses is appealing to those who were eye witnesses ( as Levites and children under the age of military service, below 20 years old, cf. Deut. 1:6,9,14; 5:2,5; 11:2,7) to the events of the Exodus and wilderness wanderings (cf. Deut. 4:34; 7:19).

▣ "Know" See full note at Deut. 4:35 and SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW.

▣ "the discipline of the Lord" YHWH's discipline (BDB 416) is positive, Deut. 11:3; and negative, Deut. 11:6. Child training is a characteristic of our father God (cf. Heb. 12:5-13). This is another wisdom term used so often in Proverbs.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FATHERHOOD OF GOD

▣ "His greatness" See notes at Deut. 10:17 and 4:31.

▣ "His mighty hand, and His outstretched arm" This is an anthropomorphic phrase used for God's power (cf. Deut. 4:34; 5:15; 6:21; 9:29). See note at Deut. 4:34 and SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 11:4 "horses and chariots"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:4 "horses and chariots" See SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARIOTS

▣ "Red Sea to engulf them" The Hebrew word here is "Reed Sea" (BDB 410 CONSTRUCT BDB 693 I).

"Engulf" is literally "flow over their faces" (BDB 847, KB 1012, Hiphil PERFECT, cf. Exod. 14:23-31), which is imagery for drowning.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE RED SEA

▣
NASB  "completely destroyed them"
NKJV, NJB, Peshitta  "destroyed them to this day"
NRSV, JPSOA  "destroyed them once and for all"
REB  "destroyed them, and so things remain to this day"
LXX  "destroyed them to this very day"

The MT has the VERB "destroyed" (BDB 1, KB 2, Piel IMPERFECT with waw plus the idiomatic phrase "to this day," which denotes a compete destruction whose consequences remain.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 11:5
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 11:5 This is a reminder of YHWH's supernatural provisions during the wilderness wanderings. See full note at Deut. 8:4.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 11:6 "Dathan and Abiram"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:6 "Dathan and Abiram" See Numbers 16:1-35; 26:9-10; Ps. 106:16-18.

▣ "among all Israel" See SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 11:8 "therefore"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:8 "therefore" This refers to all preceding historical allusions of chapter 11 or possibly even farther back. Much of Deuteronomy, up to this point, has rehearsed again and again the same admonitions.

▣ "possess the land" See SPECIAL TOPIC: POSSESS THE LAND

entries.title: Deuteronomy 11:9 "so that you may prolong your days on the land"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:9 "so that you may prolong your days on the land" Compare Deut. 11:21 with Deut. 5:16. This is not an individual promise of longevity but a cultural promise of stability to a society which honors the Law of God (cf. Deut. 4:1; 8:1) and thereby honors the family (cf. Deut. 4:40; 5:16,33; 6:2). See full note at Deut. 4:40.

▣ "the Lord swore to your fathers to give to them" See SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS.

▣ "a land flowing with milk and honey" This is not only a physical description but a technical designation for the land of Palestine in Ugaritic, Assyrian, and Egyptian documents. See full note at Deut. 6:3.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 11:10 "not like the land of Egypt"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:10 "not like the land of Egypt" The cultivation of crops was quite different in Egypt than Palestine. Palestine had seasonal rain (cf. v. 11), Egypt had to depend on irrigation from the Nile and its annual flood.

▣ "water it with your foot" This probably refers to

  1. an irrigation system in which a field was flooded and then the foot was used to punch a hole in the dike to let water out
  2. a treadmill used to lift water for irrigation

entries.title: Deuteronomy 11:11 "the land. . .drinks water from the rain of heaven"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:11 "the land. . .drinks water from the rain of heaven" For desert peoples there is no greater blessing than adequate, regular water (cf. Deut. 8:7-9). This good land is conditional on covenant obedience (cf. Deut. 11:16-17; Lev. 26:14-20; Deut. 28:12,23-24; 1 Kgs. 8:35; 17:1; 2 Chr. 7:11-14; Isa. 5:6; Jer. 14; Amos 4:7-8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: WATERS

entries.title: Deuteronomy 11:12 "the eyes of the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:12 "the eyes of the Lord" This is an anthropomorphic description of the Lord like Deut. 11:2. It expresses His special care and presence in the Promised Land.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN (anthropomorphism).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 11:13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:13 Notice the conditional ("if" BDB 49, cf. Deut. 11:22; and "obey" BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and Qal IMPERFECT from the same root, which shows emphasis and means "to hear so as to do!") nature of YHWH's blessing is:

  1. "to love" ‒ BDB 12, KB 17, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT
  2. "to serve" ‒ BDB 712, KB 773, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT. In Arabic this root means to worship and obey God, cf. Exod. 3:12; 4:3; 7:16; 8:1
  3. "with all your heart and all your soul," cf. Deut. 4:29; 6:5; and especially 10:12.

Moses is repeating this exhortation which he heard from YHWH again and again for emphasis.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S COVENANT REQUIREMENTS OF ISRAEL

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (shema)

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

▣ "heart" For the ancient Hebrew the "heart" stood for the mind and intent, the intellect and motive of an individual.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART

▣ "soul" This word means "the life force given by God" (BDB 659). It can refer to humans or animals in Genesis. See note online at Gen. 35:18 and Lev. 17:11.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH

entries.title: Deuteronomy 11:14 "He will give the rain"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:14 "He will give the rain" "He will give" (BDB 678, KB 733) describes YHWH's covenant blessings and cursings (i.e. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28):

  1. Deut. 11:9  ‒ Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT (blessing)
  2. Deut. 11:14 ‒ Qal PERFECT (blessing)
  3. Deut. 11:15 ‒ Qal PERFECT (blessing)
  4. Deut. 11:17 ‒ Qal IMPERFECT (curse)
  5. Deut. 11:17 ‒ Qal PARTICIIPLE (curse)
  6. Deut. 11:21 ‒ Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT (blessing)
  7. Deut. 11:25 ‒ Qal IMPERFECT (blessing)
  8. Deut. 11:26 ‒ Qal PARTICIPLE (blessing/curse)
  9. Deut. 11:29 ‒ Qal  PERFECT with waw (blessing/curse)
  10. Deut. 11:31 ‒ Qal PARTICIPLE (blessing)
  11. Deut. 11:32 ‒ Qal PARTICIPLE (blessing/curse)

YHWH wants to bless, but Israel's covenant obedience determines which response (blessing or cursing, cf. chapters 27-29) she receives (cf. Leviticus 26).

YHWH is separate from nature yet is in control of it. He uses it to reveal Himself to mankind (cf. Deut. 27-28; Ps. 19:1-6; Rom. 1:19-25; 2:14-15).

SPECIAL TOPIC: WATERS

▣ "early" Palestine has two annual times of rainfall. The early rains (for planting) come in October ‒ November (BDB 435, cf. Jer. 5:24; Hosea 6:2; Joel 2:23).

▣ "late rains" The late rains (for maturing crops) come in February ‒ April (BDB 545, cf. Jer. 3:3; Joel 2:23). At other times heavy dew is the only source of moisture. Hosea 6:3 uses this as imagery for end-time spiritual renewal.

▣ "your grain and your new wine and your oil" These were staples of their diet (cf. Deut. 7:13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: BIBLICAL ATTITUDES TOWARD ALCOHOL AND ALCOHOLISM

entries.title: Deuteronomy 11:15 "for your cattle"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:15 "for your cattle" This term "cattle" (BDB 96) refers to:

  1. all living creatures other than humans, Gen. 8:1; Exod. 9:9,10,22
  2. domestic animals, Gen. 47:17; Exod. 20:10; Lev. 19:19; 26:22; Num. 3:41,45; Deut. 2:35

▣ "you shall eat and be satisfied" This VERB is a recurrent promise in Deuteronomy (cf. Deut. 6:11; 8:10; 11:15; 14:29). It is made up of two VERBS:

  1. "eat" ‒ BDB 37, KB 46, Qal PERFECT with waw
  2. "be satisfied" ‒ BDB 959, KB 1302, Qal PERFECT with waw

entries.title: Deuteronomy 11:16-17
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:16-17 These verses are a warning ("beware," BDB 1036, KB 1581, Niphal IMPERATIVE, cf. Deut. 4:9,15,23; 6:12; 8:11; 11:16; 12:13,19,28,30; 15:9; 24:8, see note at Deut. 6:12) about idolatry and its consequences.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

entries.title: Deuteronomy 11:18-20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:18-20 These verses are a recapitulation of Deut. 6:6-9. They are meant to impress on the faithful the need to live life in light of God's words!

▣ "You shall therefore impress these words" This is imagery, BDB 962, KB 1321, Qal PERFECT with waw, cf. Deut. 32:46. This is what the imagery of Deut. 6:8 and Exod. 13:9,16 means. Always keep God's word in the forefront of your thoughts. Review every action in light of them!

entries.title: Deuteronomy 11:19 "teach them to your sons"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 11:19 "teach them to your sons" This is a recurrent theme of Deuteronomy. See full note at Deut. 4:9.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 11:20 "write"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:20 "write" In the past some scholars have questioned the ability of Moses and the early Israelites to write. As the archaeological evidence has grown, no one today would deny this. See "The Question of Israelite Literacy" in Approaches to the Bible, vol. 2, pp. 142-53 (from Biblical Archaeology Society, 1995).

Here. it refers to the mezuza of Deut. 6:9, which was put on the front doorpost of the home. It contained several texts from the Pentateuch.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOSES' AUTHORSHIP OF THE PENTATEUCH

11:21
NASB  "as long as the heavens remain above the
  earth"
NKJV  "like the days of the heavens are above the
  earth"
NRSV  "as long as the heavens are above the earth"
TEV, NJB  "as long as there is sky above the earth"
Peshitta  "as the days of heaven upon earth"
JPSOA, LXX  "as long as there is a heaven over the earth"

This is a parallel statement to "perpetual ordinance" (e.g. Exod. 12:14,17,24,25; 13:10). This is imagery of the permanence of the natural order. This is the basis of modern western scientific research..

entries.title: Deuteronomy 11:22
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:22 The conditional nature of the covenant (cf. Deut. 11:13; see SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT) and its requirements are recurrent:

  1. the condition is similar to Deut. 11:13, but slightly different:
    1. "for if" and, BDB 49
    2. "to keep" BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and Qal IMPERFECT VERB (grammatical construction used to bring emphasis; see SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP)
  2. the requirements (series of Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCTS, like Deut. 11:13):
    1. "to do" ‒ BDB 793, KB 889
    2. "to love" ‒ BDB 12, KB 17
    3. "to walk" ‒ BDB 229, KB 246, cf. Deut. 8:6 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY)
    4. "to hold fast to" ‒ BDB 179, KB 209, cf. Deut. 10:20; 13:4

entries.title: Deuteronomy 11:23-25
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:23-25 These are the promised results (i.e. "as He has spoken to you," Deut. 11:25) of the conditional covenant:

  1. "The Lord will drive out all the nations before you," Deut. 11:23, BDB 439, KB 441, Hiphil PERFECT with waw, cf. Exod. 34:24; Num. 32:21; Deut. 4:37-38; 9:4-5; Josh. 23:5,13
  2. "You will dispossess nations greater and mightier than you," Deut. 11:23, BDB 439, KB 441, Qal PERFECT with waw, cf. Deut. 7:17; 9:3; Num. 33:52
  3. "Every place on which the sole of your foot treads shall be yours," Deut. 11:24, BDB 201, KB 231, Qal IMPERFECT, cf Josh. 1:3. Their borders are described in Gen. 15:18; Exod. 23:31; Deut. 1:7; 3:12-17; Josh. 1:1-4; 13:8-12
  4. "No man will be able to stand before you," Deut. 11:25, BDB 426, KB 427, Hithpael IMPERFECT, cf. Deut. 7:24; Josh. 1:5; 10:8; 23:9
  5. "The Lord your God will lay," BDB 678, KB 733, Qal IMPERFECT
    1. "fear" ‒ BDB 808, cf. Deut. 2:25
    2. "dread" ‒ BDB 432, cf. Gen. 9:2

This same truth, but in different terms is in Exod. 23:27 and Josh. 2:9.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 11:24
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 11:24 For full notes on the boundaries of the Promised Land see Deut. 1:8.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 11:26-28
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:26-28 These verses continue the consequences of the conditional covenant between YHWH and His people. They are expanded in Deuteronomy 27-29 (cf. Leviticus 26). These verses explain much of the history of the Jews.

This paragraph starts out with a common call for attention, "See" ‒ BDB 906, KB 1157, Qal IMPERATIVE, cf. Deut. 1:8,21; 2:24; 4:5; 11:26; 30:15; 32:39. The term "today" (BDB 398) is a way of urging decisive, immediate action (cf. Deut. 4:39).

  1. "blessing" ‒ BDB 139
    1. "if you listen" ‒ BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERFECT, "hear so as to do," cf. commanded in Deut. 4:1; 5:1; 6:3,4; 9:1; 20:3; 27:10; 33:7; conditioned in Deut. 7:12; 11:13 (twice); 15:5 (twice); 28:1(twice),13; 30:10,17
  2. "curse" ‒ BDB 887
    1. "if you do not listen," same as above, Qal IMPERFECT
    2. "turn aside" ‒ BDB 693, KB 747, Qal PERFECT with waw
    3. "following other gods" ‒ BDB 229, KB 246, literally, "walking," cf. Deut. 6:14; 8:19; 11:28; 13:2; 28:14; Jdg. 2:12; Jer. 7:6,9; 11:10; 13:10

This contrast of destinies is often called "the two ways" (cf. Deut. 28 and 30:1,15-20; Ps. 1; Jer. 21:8; Matt. 7:13-14).

▣ "a blessing" See SPECIAL TOPIC: BLESSING (OT)

entries.title: Deuteronomy 11:28 "which you have not known"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 11:28 "which you have not known" This is literally "know." See full note at Deut. 4:35 and SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 11:29 "the blessing. . .the curse"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:29 "the blessing. . .the curse" This verse describes the covenant renewal ceremony conducted by Joshua at Shechem (cf. Deuteronomy 27-28 and Josh. 8:30-35). Apparently two groups of Levitical singers sang or chanted the blessing from Mt. Gerezim and the curses from Mr. Ebal. These two mountains flank Shechem (i.e. meaning shoulder blades, BDB 1014). Archaeology has found a large stone altar on Mt. Ebal which matches the description of this altar in the Talmud. See Introduction to the book VII.

This follows the Suzerain Hittite Treaties, which relate to the king and his vassal subjects (cf. Deuteronomy 27; Joshua 24 for the same pattern).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HITTITE (SUZERAIN) TREATIES

entries.title: Deuteronomy 11:30 "Arabah"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:30 "Arabah" This is the Jordan Valley south of the Dead Sea. See note at Deut. 1:1.

▣ "Gilgal" This means a "circle of stones" (BDB 166 II), which was the name of the Israelites' first camp site in Canaan (cf. Josh. 4:19). However, this one is farther north near Shechem (see The IVP Bible Background Commentary, OT, p. 181). See full note at Gen. 13:18 online at www.freebiblecommentary.org.

▣ "oaks of Moreh" This was a sacred tree or grove near Shechem (cf. Gen. 12:6 and 35:4). The UBS Text Project, p. 281, gives the PLURAL "oaks" an "A" rating (high probability).

Moreh means "teacher" (BDB 435).

SPECIAL TOPIC: TREES

entries.title: Deuteronomy 11:31-32
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:31-32 These are summary verses recounting what has been stated many times before.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. Why does Deuteronomy repeat the same phrases and historical incidents so much?
  2. How are the conditional or volitional elements of the Covenant emphasized?
  3. How is the sovereignty of YHWH emphasized?

 

Copyright © 2014 Bible Lessons International

entries.title: Deuteronomy 12:1 "the statutes and judgments"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:1 "the statutes and judgments" See SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION.

▣ "you shall carefully observe" This is a combination of a VERB, "keep watch" (BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal IMPERFECT) and a Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, (BDB 793, KB 889). This is a recurrent theme (e.g. Exod. 23:13,21; 34:11-12; Lev. 18:4-5,26,30; Deut. 4:6,9,15,23,40; and many more especially in Deuteronomy and Wisdom Literature).

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

▣ "which the Lord, the God of your fathers, has given you" The VERB shows completed action (BDB 678, KB 733, Qal PERFECT), yet the events are future. It is a Hebrew way of showing certainty (i.e. PROPHETIC PERFECT). This is a recurrent theme in Deuteronomy (cf. Deut. 1:8,20,21,25,35,36,39; 2:29; 3:18,20; 4:1,21,38,40; 5:16,31; 6:10,23; 7:13,16; 8:10; 9:6,23; 10:11; 11:9,17,21,31; 12:1,9; 15:4; 17:14; 18:9; 19:1,2,8,14; 21:23; 24:4; 25:15,19; 26:1,2,3,6,9,10,15; 27:3; 28:8,11,52; 31:7; 32:49; 34:4). It shows YHWH's gracious choice and provision for Israel.

▣ "to possess" The VERB (BDB 439, KB 441, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) is a recurrent promise.

SPECIAL TOPIC: POSSESS THE LAND

▣ "on the earth" "On the earth" is another way of saying "in the Land" (cf. Deut. 12:19). As long as the Israelites kept God's commandments, they could live in the Promised Land. See note at Deut. 4:40.

This verse has two different words for "land":

  1. "in the land" ‒ BDB 75
  2. "on the earth" ‒ BDB 9

They both refer to the whole earth or to the land of Canaan. They are usually synonyms (cf. Deut. 4:38-40; 11:8-9; 12:1; 26:2,15).

SPECIAL TOPIC: LAND, COUNTRY, EARTH

SPECIAL TOPIC: WORLD (several terms)

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. This starts the amplification of the Ten Words into daily regulations (i.e. Deuteronomy 12-26), which cover Israel's secular and sacred life. If one follows the outline of the Hittite Treaties, then (1) 4:1-11:32 contains the foundational laws and (2) Deut. 12:1-26:19 is the characteristic expansion and explanation of those laws.   Scholars have delineated four "Law Codes" in the Pentateuch:
    1. Book of the covenant, Exod. 20:22-23:33
    2. Priestly Code, Exodus 25-31 and 34:29 through Leviticus 16
    3. Holiness Code, Leviticus 17-26
    4. Deuteronomic Code, Deut. 12-26 and 28

      However, this listing is more effected by Julius Wellhausen's source critical approach (i.e. J=YHWH; E=Elohim; D=Deuteronomy; and P=priestly writers) to the Pentateuch than contemporary, second millennium B.C. parallels (cf. R. K. Harrison, Old Testament times and John H. Walton, Ancient Israelite Literature In Its Cultural Context).

  2. This is the chapter where the controversy concerning the date of Deuteronomy rages. It centers around Deut. 12:1-7 which call for one central worship altar (later Jerusalem).

  3. It seems that this text relates to two separate periods and purposes: (1) in the wilderness (i.e. tabernacle) and (2) in the Promised Land. The purpose of all laws is proper worship of YHWH in place, motive and form. Idolatry and its worship sites are rejected. The tension seems to be between legitimate local places of worship (Exod. 20:24; Deut. 16:21) and a central place of Israeli worship. Local and special altars (cf. Deuteronomy 27) were allowed (e.g. 1 Kgs. 3:3-5), but the Ark, tabernacle, and later the temple are emphasized (i.e. one central cultic site).

  4. Historically it is to be noted that Hezekiah's reform was more oriented toward a central worship site than was Josiah's reform, which is usually used as the supposed historical occasion for the writing of Deuteronomy (i.e. 621 B.C., cf. 2 Kgs. 18:22; 2 Chr. 32:12 and Isa. 36:7). Josiah's reform primarily dealt with idolatry not centralized worship! I personally reject the JEDP theory of Pentateuch source criticism (cf. Josh McDowell More Evidence That Demands A Verdict).
    SPECIAL TOPIC: PENTATEUCH SOURCE CRITICISM

  5. See SPECIAL TOPIC: LAWS IN THE ANCIENT NEAR EAST

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Deuteronomy 12:2 "utterly destroy all the places"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:2 "utterly destroy all the places" "Utterly destroy" comes from a Hebrew word that means "cause to perish" (BDB 1, KB 2, Piel INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and Piel IMPERFECT VERB, which show intensity, cf. Deut. 12:3; Num. 33:52 [twice]; 2 Kgs. 21:3). YHWH was admonishing the Israelites to destroy the pagan altars so as not to become a part of their fertility worship (cf. Exod. 23:24; 34:13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: UTTERLY DESTROY

▣ "on the high mountains and on the hills and under every green tree" These are the locations of local Ba'al and Asherah altars where fertility rites were practiced (cf. Jer. 2:20; 3:2,6; 17:2; Isa. 57:5,7; Hosea 4:13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP OF THE ANE

entries.title: Deuteronomy 12:3 "their altars. . .sacred pillars. . .Asherim"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:3 "their altars. . .sacred pillars. . .Asherim" See SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL'S MANDATED RESPONSE TO CANAANITE FERTILITY WORSHIP

▣ "you shall obliterate their name from this place" The VERB (BDB 1, KB, 2; Piel PERFECT with waw) means "destroy." It is used several times in this context (i.e. Deut. 11:4,17; 12:2 [twice], 3).

YHWH's name is to be "established" (BDB 1014, KB 1496, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT), but Ba'al and Asherah destroyed!

Israel either destroys the pagan idols or she will be destroyed by YHWH (i.e. Deut. 8:19,20; 11:17; 28:15-19, 63). This reflects the "two ways" (i.e. blessings or cursings, your choice confirmed by your actions, cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28; 30; Psalm 1).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 12:5 "the place which the Lord your God shall choose"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:5 "the place which the Lord your God shall choose" God chose (BDB 103, KB 119, Qal IMPERFECT, cf. Deut. 12:11,14,18,21,26; 14:23-25; 15:20; 16:2,6,11,15; 17:8,10; 18:6; 26:2; 31:11) the worship site (cf. Exod. 20:24).

The tabernacle (ark) traveled with Israel:

  1. Gilgal, Josh. 4:19; 10:6,15
  2. Shechem, Josh. 8:33
  3. Shiloh, Josh 18:1; Jdgs. 18:31; 1 Sam. 1:3
  4. Bethel, (possible) Jdg. 20:18,26-28; 21:2
  5. Kiriath-jearim, ark, 1 Sam. 6:21; 7:1-2 (priests at Nob, cf. 1 Samuel 21-22)
  6. Jerusalem
    1. David captures the citadel of Jebus (cf. 2 Sam. 5:1-10)
    2. David brings the ark to Jerusalem (cf. 2 Samuel 6)
    3. David purchases the site of the temple (2 Sam. 24:15-25; 2 Chr. 3:1)

Many modern scholars have tried to assert that Deuteronomy was written late to accommodate Hezekiah and Josiah's reforms of centralizing Israel's worship. However, Deuteronomy does not name Jerusalem as the specific site that YHWH will choose. In context the theological contrast is between:

  1. the local Ba'al shrines and the one shrine of Israel
  2. the monotheism of Israel versus the polytheism of Canaan (and the rest of the Ancient Near East)
▣
NASB  "to establish His name there for His dwelling"
NKJV  "to put His name for His habitation"
NRSV  "as his habitation to put his name there"
TEV  "where the people are to come into his presence"
NJB  "there to set his name and give it a home"
REB  "to receive his name that it may dwell there"
LXX  "to designate that his name be called there"
Peshitta  "to put His name there"
JPSOA  "to establish His name there"

The translation of this verse is influenced by Deut. 12:11. Verse 5 has "for his dwelling" (BDB 1015), while Deut. 12:11 has "to make dwell" (BDB 1014, KB 1496, Piel INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT). In meaning they are very similar and have no theological difference or connotation.

The Israelites substituted YHWH's name for His presence. This is a direct reference to the Tabernacle in the early days.

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

entries.title: Deuteronomy 12:6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:6 This verse lists several kinds of offerings:

  1. "burnt offerings" This meant wholly burnt offerings (BDB 750 II; see SPECIAL TOPIC: BURNT OFFERINGS). This was a way of showing total, complete dedication to God. It was a voluntary sacrifice (cf. Leviticus 1).
  2. "sacrifices" This refers to partially burnt, partially consumed offering (BDB 257). These were sin offerings, peace offerings, thanksgiving offerings, etc. These were any offerings which had blood involved (cf. Leviticus 7; see SPECIAL TOPIC: SIN OFFERING).
  3. "tithes" The tithe was Israel's way of supporting the priests, who were given no land inheritance (see SPECIAL TOPIC: TITHING IN THE MOSAIC LEGISLATION). There seem to be three tithes (BDB 798):
    1. for the central sanctuary
    2. for the local Levites, with the possibility of "a"
    3. every three years for the local poor (Lev. 27:30-33; Num. 18:21-22)
  4. "contributions of your hand" This is the Hebrew word for "heave-offerings" (BDB 929, cf. Lev. 7:32). This refers to a sacrifice where some part of the animal is lifted off for the priests to eat.
  5. "votive offerings" This (BDB 623) is an example of a conditional vow to YHWH, "I'll do this, if You will do that." This is the Jews keeping their part of the vow (Lev. 7:16-18).
  6. "freewill offerings" This (BDB 621) refers to an offering in thanks or praise from one who was overwhelmed with the goodness of YHWH (cf. Lev. 22:18ff).
  7. "first-born" This (BDB 114) is a reference to the Death Angel going through Egypt killing the firstborn of cattle and mankind. In light of this event all the first born of cattle and humans belonged uniquely to YHWH (cf. Exod.13; Lev. 27:26-27)!

entries.title: Deuteronomy 12:7 "you and your household shall eat before the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:7 "you and your household shall eat before the Lord" This refers to a fellowship meal, which is a theological precursor of both Passover and Eucharist (cf. Deut. 12:12,18; 14:26; Rev. 3:20). YHWH's people were created to rejoice (BDB 970, KB 1333, Qal PERFECT with waw) with Him in the physicalness of creation and the intimacy of worship (cf. Lev. 23:40; Num. 10:10; Deut. 12:7,12,18; 14:26; 16:11; 26:11; 27:7; 28:47).

SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE OFFERING

entries.title: Deuteronomy 12:8 "You shall not do at all what we are doing here today"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:8 "You shall not do at all what we are doing here today" Things will be more uniform in the Promised Land. The religious practices during the wilderness wanderings period were simpler than the more organized practices in the Promised Land and, especially at the temple, later located in Jerusalem.

▣ "every man doing whatever is right in his own eyes" This phrase has a neutral connotation here, but in Judges it takes on a sinister connotation of an individual asserting freedom from covenant obligations either through sinful choice or covenant ignorance (cf. Deut. 17:6; 21:25).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 12:9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:9 See note at Deut. 12:1

entries.title: Deuteronomy 12:10 "He gives you rest. . .security"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:10 "He gives you rest. . .security" YHWH gives you rest (BDB 628, KB 679, Hiphil PERFECT with waw) from your enemies. This security (BDB 442, KB 444, Qal PERFECT with waw) was not achieved because of Israel's great military might, but because of the presence of YHWH.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 12:11 "the place in which the Lord your God shall choose"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:11 "the place in which the Lord your God shall choose" This is a reference to the centralized place of worship (i.e. the tabernacle and the ark, cf. Deut. 12:5,14), which was first at Shiloh. See full note at Deut. 12:5.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 12:12 "you shall rejoice"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:12 "you shall rejoice" This is the purpose of YHWH's laws (cf. Deut. 12:7,18; 14:26; 28:47).

▣ "you and" Notice how everyone in the family including servants and the local Levites (cf. Deut. 12:19) were to be included! In a sense these were all extended family members. They were loved and provided for, both in life's necessities and for the next life (i.e. worship).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 12:12, 19 "Levite who is within your gates"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:12, 19 "Levite who is within your gates" All priests were Levites, but not all Levites were priests. Here "Levite" refers to the non-priests of the family of Levi who symbolized the poor and needy (cf. Deut. 12:18,19; 14:27,29; 16:11,14; 26:12-13), because the Levites had been given no land. They were respected local teachers of the Law.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LEVITICAL PRIESTS

entries.title: Deuteronomy 12:13 "Be careful that you do not offer your burnt offerings in every cultic place you see"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:13 "Be careful that you do not offer your burnt offerings in every cultic place you see" YHWH will show you the special places for offering (cf. Deut. 12:5,11,14). Do not use the many local Canaanite altars just because they are there. Don't offer a sacrifice to YHWH on altars erected for Ba'al. However, there were some local altars made for YHWH (cf. Deut. 16:21; 1 Kgs. 3:4).

This verse has three VERBS:

  1. "be careful" ‒ BDB 1036, KB 1581, Niphal IMPERATIVE
  2. "do not offer" ‒ BDB 748, KB 828, Hiphil IMPERFECT used as an IMPERATIVE
  3. "see" ‒ BDB 906, KB 1157, Qal IMPERFECT

entries.title: Deuteronomy 12:15, 20-24 "you may slaughter"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:15, 20-24 "you may slaughter" This shows a widening of the Law (cf. Lev. 17:1ff). If an animal was killed (BDB 256, KB 261, Qal IMPERFECT) for food and not sacrifice, it could be killed anywhere.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 12:15 "blessing"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:15 "blessing" See SPECIAL TOPIC: BLESSING

▣ "unclean and the clean" This does not refer to unclean animals as far as food (cf. Deut. 12:20-22; Leviticus 11), but unclean animals as far as sacrifice. A blemished sheep could be eaten by humans as could some wild animals like deer, but not pigs, etc.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOOD LAWS (OT)

entries.title: Deuteronomy 12:16 "you shall not eat the blood"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:16 "you shall not eat the blood" This relates to the Hebrew reverence for blood as the symbol for life. Even when they killed animals, whether for eating or sacrifice, they poured the blood out (cf. Deut. 15:23; Lev. 17:13) and did not eat it, because life belonged to God. The blood represented life, life belongs to God (cf. Deut. 12:23-25; Gen. 9:4; Lev. 7:11-12; 17:10-11,14)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: BLOOD

entries.title: Deuteronomy 12:17 "the tithe"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:17 "the tithe" This verse lists several things that were to be tithed (BDB 798 cf. Deut. 14:23; 18:4; Num. 18:12):

  1. "grain" ‒ BDB 186
  2. "wine" ‒ BDB 440
  3. "oil" ‒ BDB 850

This was an agricultural society.

SPECIAL TOPIC: TITHES IN THE MOSAIC LEGISLATION

entries.title: Deuteronomy 12:17-18
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:17-18 This is another warning about only using the central shrine for worship (cf. Deut. 12:26).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 12:19
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:19 See note at Deut. 12:12.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 12:20 "I will eat meat"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:20 "I will eat meat" This VERB (BDB 37, KB 46) is repeated three times:

  1. Qal COHORTATIVE
  2. Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT
  3. Qal IMPERFECT

If they desire to eat meat in the Promised Land they may surely do it:

  1. right kind of meat (Deut. 12:17,22)
  2. killed at the right place (Deut. 12:15,18,21,27)
  3. killed in the right way (Deut. 12:16,23-25)

entries.title: Deuteronomy 12:23 "be sure"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:23 "be sure" This VERB (BDB 304, KB 302, Qal IMPERATIVE) means "be strong" (cf. Deut. 31:6,7,23) in the sense of firmly refrain from something (cf. 1 Chr. 28:7).

▣ "not to eat blood" See note at Deut. 12:16.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BLOOD

▣
NASB, NKJV, NJB,
 REB, JPSOA, Peshitta 		 "for the blood is the life"
NRSV  "since blood is life"
TEV  "for the life is in the blood"
LXX  "because its blood is life"

The MT has "for the blood is the life." The word "life" is literally the Hebrew nephesh (BDB 659). This term refers to air-breathing life on the planet, human and animal. The root itself is connected to the throat (i.e. airway).

  1. life is in the blood, Lev. 17:11
  2. blood is nephesh, Deut. 12:23

See John H. Walton, ANE Thought and the OT: Introducing the Conceptual World of the Hebrew Bible, pp. 213,214; also see my notes online at Gen. 35:18 and lev. 17:11.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH

entries.title: Deuteronomy 12:26 "holy things"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:26 "holy things" This refers to the things mentioned in Deut. 12:17.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 12:28 "Be careful"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:28 "Be careful" This VERB (BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal IMPERATIVE) is used repeatedly in Deuteronomy (cf. Deut. 4:9,15,23; 6:12; 8:11; 11:16; 12:13,19,28,30; 15:9; 24:8) to encourage obedience to YHWH's covenant.

▣ "in order that it may be well with you and your sons after you forever" The VERB (BDB 405, KB 408, Qal IMPERFECT) is used several times in Deuteronomy (cf. Deut. 4:40; 5:16,29,33; 6:3,18; 12:25,28; 22:7) and in Jeremiah (cf. Deut. 7:23; 38:20; 42:6) and refers to the blessed, happy, wholesome life of YHWH's people. Again, covenant obedience is linked to blessing and longevity in the land. This total obedience is admonished to successive generations i.e. forever).

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam and aiōnios)

▣ "for you will be doing what is good and right"

  1. "good" BDB 373 II
    1. in God's eyes, 6:18; 13:18; 2 Chr. 14:2
    2. in man's eyes, Josh. 9:25; Jdg. 19:24; Jer. 26:14
  2. "right" BDB 449, same as above, but also Deut. 12:25; 13:18; 1 Kgs. 11:38; 14:8; 15:11; 22:43; 2 Kgs. 12:2 (for a parallel to 1. b. above, see 12:8).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 12:29 "before the Lord your God cuts off before you the nations"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 12:29 "before the Lord your God cuts off before you the nations" The VERB (BDB 503, KB 500, Hiphil IMPERFECT) means YHWH eliminated people by killing them (cf. Deut. 19:1; Josh. 23:4; 2 Sam. 7:9; Jer. 44:8). This indicates that YHWH is fighting Israel's battles.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 12:30 "beware"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:30 "beware" See note at Deut. 12:28.

▣ "that you are not ensnared" The VERB (BDB 669, KB 723, Niphal IMPERFECT), in its Qal stem, literally means, "to bring down with a stick" (cf. Ps. 9:16). The Niphal stem, used only here, is a metaphorical extension implying "throw a stick at a target."

▣ "do not inquire after their gods" The VERB (BDB 205, KB 233, Qal IMPERFECT) means "to seek after":

  1. YHWH in Deut. 12:5; 4:29; Jer. 10:21; 29:13
  2. Canaanite gods in Deut. 12:30; 2 Chr. 25:15,20; Jer. 8:2

entries.title: Deuteronomy 12:31
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:31 YHWH is clearly saying to Israel that if they practice the same abominable fertility rites, He will remove them from the land (cf. Deut. 7:4; Lev. 18:24-30) as He did the Canaanites (cf. Gen. 15:16-21). YHWH "hates" (BDB 971, KB 1338, Qal PERFECT) idolatry (cf. Deut. 12:31; 16:22).

SPECIAL TOPIC: IDOLATRY

▣ "every abominable act" See SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOMINATION

entries.title: Deuteronomy 12:32 "you shall not add nor take away from it"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:32 "you shall not add nor take away from it" God is serious about obedience to His word (see note at Deut. 4:2). However, Deuteronomy shows some adaptation of the laws of the desert period. We must apply the truths of the Bible for every new age and culture. God revealed Himself to a particular culture at a particular time. Some of it is related only to that time and people (e.g. holy war, polygamy, slavery, subjugation of women), but much of it is timeless truth to be applied to every age (for a discussion of how to distinguish between the eternal and the cultural, see Fee and Stuart, How To Read the Bible For All Its Worth, pp. 149-164 and Gordon Fee, Gospel and Spirit, pp. 1-36).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. Why is there so much emphasis on a central worship site?
  2. Why did some of the laws change?
  3. Why is the blood so important to the Hebrews?
  4. Why are these rules so detailed?
