READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. This is part of a literary unit, Deut. 27-28, which is often referred to as "the cursing and blessing" section of the Covenant.

  2. I think the whole OT can be seen as a consequence of Israel's inability to perform the Covenant stipulations, and thereby was visited with the curses of Deut. 27:15-26; 28:15-68 (also note Leviticus 26).

  3. YHWH wanted Israel to be a revelatory channel for all the world to come to know Him. He wanted to bless Israel to gain the attention of the nations and thereby to attract the nations unto Himself.
    SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN.

  4. The curses for disobedience are more numerous than the promised blessings.

    This same structure is paralleled in the treaties of the ANE.

    1. Meredith G. Kline, Treaty of the Great Kings: The Covenant Structure of Deuteronomy
    2. D. Brent Sandy and Ronald L. Giese, Jr., Cracking Old Testament Codes, pp. 125-128.
    3. SPECIAL TOPIC: HITTITE (Suzerain) TREATIES

  5. This cursing and blessing section is parallel to Leviticus 26. This form of covenant consequences is often called "the two ways" (cf. Deut. 30:15,19; Psalm 1).

  6. This is the second sermon of Moses (i.e. Deut. 5-28). The first sermon looked back to YHWH's gracious, powerful extraction of Israel from Egypt and His presence and provision through the wilderness wandering period.

    The second sermon focuses on YHWH's will for national Israel in the Promised Land. He establishes Israel's distinctiveness so as to reveal Himself to the world.

    The third sermon (Deuteronomy 29-32) deal with covenant renewal and affirmation of Israel's loyalty and obedience to YHWH alone.

    See full outline of Deuteronomy by sermons in Introduction to Deuteronomy, VIII.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:2 "blessings"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
28:2 "blessings" The term (BDB 139) is related to the root "to kneel" (BDB 138). YHWH offers Israel the choice (cf. Deut. 11:26-31; 30:1,19). This conformity to YHWH's covenant requirements determines their destiny!

SPECIAL TOPIC: BLESSING (OT)

▣ "will come upon you" This idiomatic phrase (BDB 97, KB 112, Qal PERFECT with waw) is used here for blessing, but in Deut. 28:15 for the curses.

▣ "overtake" The VERB (BDB 673, KB 727, Hiphil PERFECT with waw) is used of:

  1.  blessing, pursuing, and overtaking Israel because of her obedience, Deut. 28:2
  2.  cursing, pursuing, and overtaking Israel because of her disobedience, Deut. 28:15,45

▣ "obey" In Deut. 28:1 this term (BDB 1033, KB 1570) was an intensified Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and a Qal IMPERFECT. Here it is a Qal IMPERFECT (cf. Deut. 28:15,49; 30:10,12,13,17; 31:12) and in Deut. 28:45, 62 a Qal PERFECT (cf. Deut. 30:8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:3 "Blessed shall you be in the city. . .in the country"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 28:3 "Blessed shall you be in the city. . .in the country" This is imagery of expressing a nation wide blessing (cf. Deut. 28:4-6, 8).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:4 "Blessed. . .offspring of your body. . .the herd. . .crops. . .flock"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 28:4 "Blessed. . .offspring of your body. . .the herd. . .crops. . .flock" Many and healthy cattle and children were a sign of covenant prosperity and wealth. The man with large families, large herds, was one who was blessed by God (cf. Deut. 7:13; 28:4,11; 30:9). These were physical signs of God's blessings to obedient covenant members (cf. Gen. 1:22,28).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:5 "Blessed. . .basket"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
28:5 "Blessed. . .basket" This basket was used to carry fruit or grain (cf. Deut. 26:2). This speaks of prosperity in agriculture.

▣ "Blessed. . .kneading bowl" This was a bowl used to prepare family meals (i.e. daily bread). This was a way of saying, "there will always be food on the table." The opposite is stated in Deut. 28:17.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:6 "Blessed. . .when you come in. . .when you go out"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 28:6 "Blessed. . .when you come in. . .when you go out" This is a Hebraic idiom (cf. Deut. 31:2; Ps. 121:8; Isa. 37:28) for a blessed life in all areas (cf. contrast in Deut. 28:19).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:7 "Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
28:7 "Lord" This is the Hebrew word "Lord" (Adon).

SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord (Adon and Kurios)

▣ "enemies" This PARTICIPLE (BDB 33, KB 38 Qal PARTICIPLE) is used eight times in this chapter (cf. Deut. 28:7,25,31,48,53,55,57,68). It refers to the active hostility of a person or group against a person or group. YHWH promised to be an enemy to Israel's enemies (cf. Exod. 23:22), but because of covenant disobedience He is now an enemy to Israel!

If Israel is obedient, YHWH will fight her enemies (i.e. Divine Warrior, "holy war" terminology, cf. Deut. 30:7; 33:27-29).

▣ "will flee before you seven ways" This idiom refers to the fearful, unorganized retreat of Israel's enemies (cf. Deut. 28:20, 25).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE, #4

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:8 "blessing upon. . .barns"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
28:8 "blessing upon. . .barns" This refers to grain storehouses (cf. Prov. 3:10). Later Judaism says this refers to YHWH blessing one in secret.

▣ "in the land which the Lord your God gives you" This goes back to the promise to Abraham in Gen. 12:1-3. The land was YHWH's special promise fulfilled in the exodus/conquest.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:9 "the Lord will establish you"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
28:9 "the Lord will establish you" This VERB (BDB 877, KB 1086, Hiphil IMPERFECT) basically means "to raise up." It is used in several different senses in Deuteronomy in the Hiphil.

  1. confirm a covenant, cf. Deut. 8:18
  2. being on the scene, cf. Deut. 18:15,18
  3. raise up fallen livestock, cf. Deut. 22:4
  4. to set up memorial stones, cf. Deut. 27:3)

Here it is used as imagery in the sense of "establish," as in Deut. 25:7 and 29:13.

▣ "Lord" See SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "a holy people" The word "holy" means "set apart for God's service" (BDB 871 and 872). Israel was meant to be a kingdom of priests to bring all the nations to YHWH (i.e. Ezod. 19:5-6).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "walk" This is a biblical imagery for lifestyle faith and obedience (cf. Deut. 5:33; 8:6; 10:12; 11:22; 19:9; 26:17; 30:16).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:10 "So all the peoples of the earth will see that you are called by the name of the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
28:10 "So all the peoples of the earth will see that you are called by the name of the Lord" The phrase "called by the name of the Lord" (BDB 894, KB 1128, Niphal PERFECT) denotes YHWH's ownership of Israel (cf. 2 Sam. 6:2; Isa. 43:7; Jer. 7:10-12; 14:9; 15:16; 32:34; Dan. 9:18,19; Amos 9:12).

YHWH wanted Israel to be a revelatory channel for all the world to come to know Him. He wanted to bless Israel to gain the attention of the nations and thereby to attract the nations unto Himself (cf. Deut. 28:25, 37).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

▣ "afraid of you" The blessings of YHWH, both in domestic and military areas, will cause fear/reverence (BDB 431, KB 432, Qal PERFECT with waw, cf. Deut. 7:19; 17:13) on the part of superstitious pagans of the surrounding nations.

Israel was not to fear (BDB 431, KB 432) because YHWH was with them, for them, and fought on their behalf (e.g. Deut. 1:21,29; 3:2,22; 7:18; 20:1,3; 31:6,8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR (OT)

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 28:11 This is a summary verse of YHWH's blessing to an obedient covenant people (e.g. Deut. 11:14).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:12 "His good storehouse"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
28:12 "His good storehouse" This (BDB 373 II and 69) was a symbol of heaven and rain (cf. Deut. 28:23-24; Ps. 85:12; Mal. 3:10). It is possibly a sarcastic reference to Ba'al worship. Ba'al was the Canaanite god of prosperity (i.e. rain, cf. 1 Kings 17-18). Yet, it was YHWH who provided all blessings to His people (cf. Deut. 28:47; 11:14; Lev. 26:4).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVEN

▣ "to give rain to your land in its season" This VERB (BDB 678, KB 733) is used regularly in this chapter for YHWH's covenant gifts of blessing (cf. Deut. 28:1,7,8,11,12,13).

Not only will YHWH open the windows of heaven and send rain, but He will do it at the appropriate time (i.e. early and later rains, the time of planting and the time of maturing crops).

SPECIAL TOPIC: WATERS

▣ "you shall lend to many nations but you shall not borrow" This was another sign of God's blessing that they had surplus to loan (cf. Deut. 23:20)! The results of disobedience are sharply contrasted in Deut. 28:44!

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
28:13 This verse has two idioms of prosperity and power:

  1.  the head and not the tail
  2.  you only shall be above, not be underneath

But note the conditional element. The same idiom was used in Deut. 28:1, "being careful to do" (two INFINITIVE CONSTRUCTS). The reversal caused by disobedience is seen in Deut. 28:44.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:14 "do not turn aside. . .to the right or to the left"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
28:14 "do not turn aside. . .to the right or to the left" It is used literally in Num. 20:17; 22:26; Deut. 2:27, but usually it is a Hebrew idiom for "any deviation from the standard or clearly marked path is sin" (cf. Deut. 5:32; 17:11,20; Josh. 1:7; 23:6; 2 Kgs. 22:2). Notice here, idolatry is specifically referenced (cf. Deut. 5:7-9; 27:15; Exod. 20:23; 34:17).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

▣
NASB, NRSV, LXX  "which I command you today"
NKJV, REB, Peshitta  "which I command you this day"
TEV      ———
NJB  "the words which I am laying down for
  you today"
JPSOA  "that I enjoin upon you this day"

This phrase seems to imply a special day of giving the law (cf. Deut. 28:1,13,14,15). However, 'olam can refer to a period of time. The reason for the question is exactly to what does "the book" of Deut. 28:58 and 61 refer?

  1. all of Deuteronomy
  2. one of Moses' sermons in Deuteronomy
  3. larger body of legislation including parts of Exodus, Leviticus, and Numbers

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam and aiōnios)

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:15 "to observe to do"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
28:15 "to observe to do" This is the exact terminology and grammatical form found in Deut. 28:1,13; 32:46. Similar forms of the same terms are found in Deut. 28:58 and 29:8. Obedience is crucial. Obedience is not the foundation of the covenant, but its natural outflow! The covenant is established in the love and sovereignty of YHWH, but its continuance and fruitfulness is maintained by obedience.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

▣ "His commandments and His statutes" See SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION.

▣ "curses" This is a NOUN form from the root "to be small" (BDB 886-887, cf. Deut. 27:15-26, 28:15-68). These curses were meant to cause Israel to return to YHWH.

▣ "overtake" This is a personification of curses. See note at Deut. 28:2.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:15-37
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 28:15-37 This section of cursings does not demand a literal interpretation. Rather, they were to build up an impression of disaster. These kinds of blights will follow if disobedience occurs. It was a way of building up a mindset on what will happen if Israel violates YHWH's law.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:16-19
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
28:16-19 These verses parallel completely. Verses 3-6 are the blessings; Deut. 28:16-19 are the cursings.

28:18
NASB, NJB  "offspring of your body"
NKJV, Peshitta  "fruit of your body"
NRSV  "fruit of your womb"
TEV  "children"
LXX  "the progeny of your belly"
JPSOA  "the issue of your womb"

The literal phrase is, "the fruit of your womb." Many healthy, happy children were one of the blessings (cf. Deut. 28:4,11), but disobedience brought covenant promise reversal!

This is imagery for one's entire life (cf. v. 6).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:20 "confusion"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
28:20 "confusion" This is a word (BDB 223) that is used of defeat in battle (cf. Deut. 7:23). It is opposite of Deut. 28:7 and 25. The confusion will be upon Israel if she disobeys God's word.

▣
NASB, NKJV, REB, Peshitta  "rebuke"
NRSV, JPSOA  "frustration"
TEV  "trouble"
LXX  "exhaustion"
KB 546  "threat"

This root, מגערת (BDB 172, KB 546) is found only here. It is similar to the root for "rebuke," גערה, found mostly in Job and Psalms. It relates to YHWH's destruction of disobedient Israel in battle. For these rare words, modern interpreters look at

  1. context
  2. related Hebrew roots
  3. cognate roots
  4. if poetry, parallelism

▣ "until you are destroyed and until you perish quickly" Notice the parallelism:

  1. "destroyed" ‒ BDB 1029, KB 1552, Niphal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, cf. Deut. 4:26; 6:15
  2. "perish" ‒ BDB 1, KB 2, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, cf. Lev. 26:38; Deut. 4:26; 8:19-20; 11:17; 30:18-20; Josh. 23:13,16 plus the ADVERB "quickly" (BDB 555 II)

▣ "on account of the evil of your deeds, because you have forsaken Me" Notice that deviation from the commandments is seen as forsaking YHWH!

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:21 "pestilence"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
28:21 "pestilence" This (BDB 184) refers to a plague (cf. Lev. 26:25; Num. 14:12) like YHWH sent on Egypt (cf. Exod. 5:3; 9:15).

▣ "cling" The VERB (BDB 179, KB 209, Hiphil) is JUSSIVE in form. YHWH's judgment will stick close to them until it has finished its task (i.e. "consumed you," BDB 477, KB 476, Piel INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT).

The same term is used for what Israel should do to YHWH (i.e. cling to Him, cf. Deut. 10:20; 11:22; 30:20). What irony!

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:22
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
28:22 Note the list of things YHWH will send against a disobedient Israel:

  1. consumption (BDB 1006, cf. Lev. 26:16), a disease of the lungs
  2. fever (BDB 869, cf. Lev. 26:16)
  3. inflamation (BDB 196)
  4. fiery heat (BDB 359, #2,3, and 4 all involve heat; this one seems to imply drought conditions, cf. NRSV)
  5. sword (BDB 352; see note below)
  6. blight (BDB 995, smut on crops, cf. 1 Kgs. 8:37; 2 Chr. 6:28; Amos 4:9)
  7. mildew (BDB 439, cf. 1 Kgs. 8:37; 2 Chr. 6:28; Amos 4:9; Hag. 2:17; the word means "green," therefore, a "green mildew")

Both humans and agriculture will suffer and die! Notice the symbolic number of afflictions (i.e. seven; there are also seven blessings listed in this chapter).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE, #4

▣
NASB, NKJV, Peshitta  "sword"
NRSV, NJB, TEV, JPSOA, REB  "drought"
LXX  "murder"

The Hebrew root, חרב, has several meanings

  1. drought ‒ BDB 351 I
  2. desolation ‒ BDB 351 II
  3. sword ‒ BDB 352

Number 3 has the Masoretic vowel marks, but UBS Text Project, p. 295, gives "drought" a "C" rating (considerable doubt). The list itself suggests an agricultural judgment.

Remember, the Masoretic notes are not inspired. They were added to a Hebrew consonantal text much later in Israel's history (i.e. started in A.D. 70 and finished in A.D. 900). They codify Israel's ancient traditions.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:23 "iron"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
28:23 "iron" Iron is often imagery for difficulties:

  1. the land will not produce, because of no rain it turns as hard as metal, Deut. 28:23, cf. Lev. 26:19
  2. the yoke of iron is placed on Israel's neck, Deut. 28:48
  3. Egypt as an iron furnace of affliction, cf. Deut. 4:20

SPECIAL TOPIC: MASORETIC TEXT

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:25 "you will go out one way against them, but you will flee seven ways before them"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
28:25 "you will go out one way against them, but you will flee seven ways before them" This is imagery describing Israel's military planning as being totally useless. Seven is a numerical symbol for "perfection." Israel will be in total retreat. The promises of "holy war" have been reversed!

▣ "you will be an example of terror to all the kingdoms of the earth" Israel will be used by YHWH to reveal Himself to the world; either positively (i.e. the blessings) or negatively (i.e. the curses, cf. Deut. 28:37; 2 Chr. 29:8; Jer. 15:4). YHWH wanted to use Israel to reach all mankind. This is a reversal of His purposes!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:26 "Your carcasses shall be food"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 28:26 "Your carcasses shall be food" For Israel it was a great tragedy to be unburied and thus able to be picked apart by animals (cf. 1 Sam. 17:44-46). Because of the mentioning of "birds," many see this as an eschatological reference (cf. Isa. 18:14; Jer. 7:33; 16:4; 19:7; 34:20; Ezek. 29:5; 32:4; 39:4).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:27 "with the boils of Egypt"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
28:27 "with the boils of Egypt" Notice the list of plagues and problems (plagues of Egypt now on Israel are a reversal of covenant blessings) YHWH will visit on Israel if they do not obey His covenant. To whom much is given, much is required (e.g. Luke 12:48).

1. NASB, NKJV, NRSV, TEV, NET "boils," cf. Deut. 28:27,35
NJB "Egyptian ulcers"
JPSOA "inflamation"
BDB 1006, cf. Exod. 9:9-11. It refers to some kind of abscess.
 
2. NASB, JPSOA, NET "tumors," Deut. 28:27
NKJV "emerods"
NRSV "ulcers"
TEV "sores"
NJB "swelling in the groin"
BDB 779 II, cf. 1 Sam. 5:6,9,12. Many scholars have interpreted this as the symptoms of plague (i.e. buboes, large darkened, swollen areas, cf. 1 Sam. 5:9-6:17, which, by implication, associates it with mice)
 
3. NASB, NKJV "the scab," Deut. 28:27
NRSV, NJB "scurvy"
JPSOA "boil-scars"
NET "eczema"
BDB 173, cf. Lev. 21:20; 22:22
 
4. NASB, NKJV, NRSV, TEV, NJB "the itch," Deut. 28:27
NET "scabies"
BDB 360 III. This term is found only here in the OT and refers to skin irritation caused by mites (cf. NIDOTTE, vol. 2, p. 278).
 
5. NASB, NKJV, NRSV, NJB, NET "madness," Deut. 28:28,35
TEV "lose your mind"
BDB 993, cf. Zech. 12:4
 
6. NASB, NKJV, NRSV, TEV, NJB, NET "blindness, Deut. 28:28,29
BDB 734, cf. Lam. 4:14; Zeph. 1:17
 
7. NASB "bewilderment of heart," Deut. 28:28
NKJV "confusion of heart"
NRSV, NET "confusion of mind"
TEV "confusion"
NJB "distraction of mind"
BDB 1069, cf. Zech. 12:4
 
8. NASB, NKJV "oppressed. . .continually," Deut. 28:29
NRSV "continually abused"
TEV, NET "constantly oppressed"
NJB "exploited"
NET "confusion of mind", Deut. 28:28
BDB 798, Qal passive participle, cf. Lev. 6:2
 
9. NASB, TEV "robbed continually," Deut. 28:29
NKJV "plundered continually"
NRSV, NET "continually robbed"
NJB "plundered"
BDB 159, Qal passive participle, cf. Lev. 6:2
 
10. NASB "wife. . .violated," Deut. 28:30
NKJV, NRSV "lie with her"
NET "rape"
  BDB 993, KB 1415, Qal imperfect
 
11. your home lived in by another, Deut. 28:30
 
12. your vineyard enjoyed by another, Deut. 28:30
 
13. your livestock taken by another, Deut. 28:31
 
14. your children taken, Deut. 28:32
 
15. your crops given to another, Deut. 28:33
 
16. your labors enjoyed by another, Deut. 28:33
 
17. NASB, NKJV "oppressed," Deut. 28:33
NRSV "abused"
TEV "oppression"
NJB "exploited"
BDB 798, KB 897, Qal passive participle, cf. Deut. 28:29; 1 Sam. 12:4; Amos 4:1
 
18. NASB, NKJV, NRSV, NJB "crushed," Deut. 28:33
TEV "harsh treatment"
BDB 954, KB 1285, Qal passive participle, cf. 1 Sam. 12:3-4; Amos 4:1
 
19. NASB, NKJV, NRSV, NJB "driven mad," Deut. 28:34
TEV "make you lose your mind"
BDB 993, KB 1415, Pual participle, cf. Deut. 28:30
 
20. NASB "strike you. . .with sore boils," Deut. 28:35
NKJV "strike you. . .with severe boils"
NRSV "strike you. . .with grievous boils"
TEV "will cover you. . .painful sores, boils"
NJB "strike you down with foul ulcers"
BDB 645, KB 697, Hiphil imperfect and two objects, BDB 1006 and 948
 
21. your king removed and replaced by pagan rulers, Deut. 28:36
 
22. you shall serve foreign gods, Deut. 28:36
 
23. you will become:
a.
NASB "a horror," Deut. 28:37
NKJV "an astonishment"
NRSV "object of horror"
NJB "the astonishment"
BDB 1031 I, cf. 2 Kgs. 22:19; Jer. 5:30; 25:9,11,18,38; 29:18; 42:18; 44:12,22; 49:13,17; 50:23; 51:37,41
b.
NASB, NKJV, NRSV "a proverb," Deut. 28:37
NJB "the byword"
BDB 605, cf. 1 Kgs. 9:7; Jer. 24:9
c.
NASB "a taunt," Deut. 28:37
NKJV, NRSV "a byword"
NJB "the laughing-stock"
BDB 1042, cf. 1 Kgs. 9:7; Jer. 24:9
 
24. NASB "the Lord will drive you"
NKJV, NRSV "the Lord will lead you"
NJB "Yahweh is taking you"

This VERB (BDB 624 I, KB 675, Piel IMPERFECT) is used of leading livestock (e.g. Exod. 3:1). It became imagery of

  1. leading people in judgment (e.g. 4:27; 1 Sam. 30:2,22; Isa. 20:4)
  2. YHWH leading as a caring shepherd (cf. Ps. 48:14; 78:26,52; 80:1)

Humans will be led (shepherd) or driven (judge) by their faith obedience.

This list reminds Israel of the YHWH's plagues on the Egyptians. These plagues are now visited on disobedient Israel (cf. Deut. 7:15; 28:60,61).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:32
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
28:32 Notice the plight of these Israeli parents:

  1. children given to other people (BDB 678, KB 733, Qal PASSIVE PARTICIPLE)
  2. they see it happening (BDB 906, KB 1157, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE)
  3. their eyes fail with longing all the day (the term, BDB 479, is found only here in the OT)
  4. they have no power to stop it (BDB 34 II, CONSTRUCT BDB 43)

I can only imagine the horror and pain!

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:33 "oppressed"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 28:33 "oppressed" This term was used regularly of the wealthy taking advantage of the poor and socially ostracized, but here it is used of YHWH breaking His disobedient people.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:35 "from the sole of your foot to the crown of your head"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 28:35 "from the sole of your foot to the crown of your head" This is imagery for widespread sickness of which one cannot be healed (cf. Job 2:7; in Isa. 1:5-6 it is a symbol of sin).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:36 "your king"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 28:36 "your king" Moses recognized that there would be a king someday (cf. Deut. 17:14-20). The Israelites were a tribal society. There was no king until Saul (cf. 1 Samuel 8).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:38-42
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
28:38-42 Again notice the list of Israel's attempts at prosperity, which will be thwarted by YHWH:

Their Actions Results
1. much seed, Deut. 28:38 locusts destroy
2. plant vineyards, Deut. 28:39 worms destroy
3. plant olive trees, Deut. 28:40 olives drop off
4. have children, Deut. 28:41 children taken captive
5. trees and produce, Deut. 28:42 crickets destroy

The promised prosperity of YHWH is negated by the covenant disobedience of Israel!

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:40 "anoint yourself"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
28:40 "anoint yourself" The people of the ANE put olive oil on their faces as a symbol of prosperity and joy (e.g. Ruth 3:3; 2 Sam. 12:20; 14:2).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANOINTING IN THE BIBLE

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:43-44
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
28:43-44 These two verses describe the role reversal of Israelites and resident aliens (sojourners, BDB 158):

  1.  aliens shall rise above you
    1. they higher and higher (BDB 751)
    2. you lower and lower (BDB 641) [the reversal of Deut. 28:13]
  2. alien shall lend to you [the reversal of Deut. 28:12]
  3. alien shall be the head [the reversal of Deut. 28:13]

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:45-48
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
28:45-48 Notice the cause and effect of YHWH's covenant judgments:

  1.  the cause
    1. Israel would not listen (BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal PERFECT) and keep (BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUST) YHWH's commandments and statutes, Deut. 28:45; SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (shema)
    2. Israel did not serve (BDB 712, KB 773, Qal PERFECT [twice]) YHWH, Deut. 28:47:
      (1) with joy
      (2) with a glad heart
      (3) thankfully for the abundance of all things
  2. the effect
    1. curses (personified)
      (1) shall come on you, Deut. 28:45, BDB 97, KB 112, Qal PERFECT with waw
      (2) pursue you, Deut. 28:45, BDB 922, KB 1191, Qal PERFECT with waw
      (3) overtake you, Deut. 28:45, BDB 673, KB 727, Hiphil PERFECT with waw
      (4) until you are destroyed, Deut. 28:45, BDB 1029, KB 1552, Niphal INFINITIVE CONSTRUST, cf. Deut. 4:25-26
    2. enemies
      you shall serve your enemies, Deut. 28:48
      (a) in hunger (BDB 944)
      (b) in thirst (BDB 854)
      (c) in nakedness (BDB 735)
      (d) lack of all things
      (e) put iron yoke on you
      (f) until destroyed (BDB 1029, KB 1552, Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUST, cf. Deut. 4:25-26)

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:46 "forever"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 28:46 "forever" See SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam and aiōnios).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:49 "The Lord will bring a nation against you"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 28:49 "The Lord will bring a nation against you" This refers to Assyria (cf. Hosea 8:1) and/or Neo-Babylon (cf. Jer. 5:15).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:49-57
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
28:49-57 The consequences of disobedience are continued. This paragraph lists the problems related to siege warfare in the Ancient Near East:

  1. The invaded described:
    1. invader brought by YHWH, Deut. 28:49
    2. a nation from afar, Deut. 28:49
    3. a nation with a strong and swift army, Deut. 28:49
    4. a nation with an unknown language, Deut. 28:49
    5. a nation with no respect for those whom they invade, Deut. 28:50
    6. a nation that will consume all the produce and livestock of Israel for food, Deut. 28:51
    7. a nation who will besiege every fortified city in Israel, Deut. 28:52
  2. The consequences for Israel:
    1. they will perish for lack of food, Deut. 28:51
    2. Israel shall eat her own young, Deut. 28:53 (cf. Lev. 26:29) and not share even this food (cf. Deut. 28:57)
    3. gentle (BDB 940) men and women will lose their natural and family affections and turn hostile, Deut. 28:54,56
    4. they will not share their children as food, Deut. 28:57

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:50 "no respect for the old; nor show favor to the young"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
28:50 "no respect for the old; nor show favor to the young" The Assyrians especially, but also the Neo-Babylonians, would kill the elderly (opposite of Lev. 19:32) and the very young children as a way of demoralizing the population before they were deported to a distant region and resettled in someone else's houses.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HUMAN AGING

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:51
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 28:51 In this verse the invading nations are described in terms of a total devastation of resources similar to the locust plagues of Joel, Amos, and Micah.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:52 "high and fortified walls in which you trusted"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 28:52 "high and fortified walls in which you trusted" Israel would be trusting (BDB 105, KB 120, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE) in her military preparations (cf. 2 Chr. 32:7-8)!

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:53-57 "you shall eat the offspring of your own body"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 28:53-57 "you shall eat the offspring of your own body" This shows the desperate nature of a siege (i.e. cannibalism, cf. Lev. 26:29; 2 Kgs. 6:24-30; Jer. 19:9; Lam. 2:20; 4:10; Ezek. 5:10).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:58-68 "if. . .then"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
28:58-68 "if. . .then" Notice the covenant obligations and the consequences for disobedience (i.e. conditional covenant):

  1. "if you"
    1. "are not careful to observe all the words of this law" (BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal IMPERFECT and BDB 793, KB 889, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT)
    2. "to fear this honored and awesome name, the Lord your God" (BDB 431, KB 432, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, cf. Deut. 4:10; 5:29; 6:2,13,24; 10:12,20; 13:4; 14:23; 17:19; 28:58; 31:12,13); see SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH
    3. note Deut. 28:1,13,15,58; 29:9; 31:12; 32:46. Obedience is crucial; see SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP
  2. "then"
    1. YHWH will bring plagues, Deut. 28:59
      (1) extraordinary (BDB 810, KB 927, Hiphil PERFECT with waw)
      (2) severe (BDB 152)
      (3) lasting (BDB 52, KB 63, Niphal PARTICIPLE with waw)
      (4) miserable, (BDB 948)
      (5) chronic (BDB 52, KB 63, Niphal PARTICIPLE with waw)
    2. YHWH will bring back the plagues (BDB 188, cf. Deut. 7:15), of which the Israelites were afraid (BDB 388, KB 386, Qal PERFECT), of Egypt to cling (BDB 179, KB 209, Qal PERFECT with waw) to them, Deut. 28:60
    3. YHWH will bring every sickness (BDB 315) and every plague (BDB 646, cf. Lev. 26:21) not mentioned in the book of the law, Deut. 28:61
    4. YHWH will reverse His promise of prosperity and abundance, Deut. 28:62-63
    5. YHWH will reverse the exodus from Egypt to the Promised Land and scatter (BDB 806, KB 918, Hiphil PERFECT with waw) His covenant people, Deut. 28:64
      (1) serve other gods, Deut. 28:64
      (2) find no rest, Deut. 28:65
      (3) have trembling heart, Deut. 28:65
      (4) failing eyes, Deut. 28:65
      (5) despair of soul, Deut. 28:65
      (6) be in dread night and day, Deut. 28:66,67
      (7) no assurance of life, Deut. 28:66
      (8) slavery, Deut. 28:68
28:58
NASB  "this honored and awesome name"
NKJV, NRSV  "the glorious and awesome name"
TEV  "this wonderful and awesome name"
NJB  "this glorious and awe-inspiring name"

The "name" stands for the person and character of YHWH (see SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH, e.g. Job 1:21; Isa. 48:9-11; Ezek. 20:44; Amos 2:7). He is described by the two Niphal PARTICIPLE:

  1. BDB 457, KB 455, from the VERB, "to be heavy or weighty," used as imagery for honorable or glorious (cf. Isa. 26:15; 66:5; Ezek. 28:22; 39:13)
  2. BDB 431, KB 432, from the VERB, "to fear," used in the sense of reverential awe of YHWH and His redemptive acts (e.g. Deut. 7:21; 10:17,21; Neh. 1:5; 4:14; 9:32; Ps. 145:6)

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:61 "the words of this law which are written in this book"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
28:61 "the words of this law which are written in this book" It is uncertain what this refers to specifically:

  1. the entire Torah
  2. the laws of Exodus ‒ Numbers
  3. all of Deuteronomy (cf. Deut. 31:24)
  4. parts of Deuteronomy
    1. law codes
    2. cursing and blessing

Of course "book" means scroll, but this does assert that Moses wrote or had someone record YHWH's law dictated through him (cf. Deut. 27:3,8; 28:58; 29:21,29; 30:10).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOSAIC AUTHORSHIP OF THE PENTATEUCH

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:62 "few in number"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
28:62 "few in number" This was a reversal of the Abrahamic promises. God promised that they would be

  1. the "stars of heaven" (cf. Gen. 15:5; 22:17; 26:4)
  2. like "the sand" (cf. Gen. 22:17; 32:12)
  3. like "the dust" (cf. Gen. 13:16; 28:14; Num. 23:10)
  4. The full list can be seen at Gen. 13:16.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:63 "the Lord delighted over you"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
28:63 "the Lord delighted over you" This VERB (BDB 965, KB 1314) is used in two ways:

  1. to bless (Qal PERFECT, cf. Deut. 30:9)
    1. prosper you (BDB 405, KB 408, Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT)
    2. multiply you (BDB 915 I, KB 1176, Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT)
  2. to curse (Qal IMPERFECT)
    1. perish (BDB 1, KB 2, Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT)
    2. destroy (BDB 1029, KB 1552, Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT)
    3. torn from the land (BDB 650, KB 702, Niphal PERFECT)

YHWH both rewards and disciplines His children (i.e. Hebrews 12). The discipline is for the purpose of restoration and inclusion.

▣ "you will be torn from the land" The VERB (BDB 650, KB 702, Niphal PERFECT with waw) is often used of YHWH's judgment (cf. Ps. 52:5; Prov. 15:25). This was a total reversal of the Abrahamic promises (cf. Gen. 12:1-3).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:64 "the Lord will scatter you among all peoples"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
28:64 "the Lord will scatter you among all peoples" This refers to exile, a reverse exodus (cf. Deut. 28:68.)

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

▣ "no resting place" This (BDB 629 I) was also used twice for the Genesis 8 account of the flood of Noah's day:

  1. the Ark rested on the mountains of Ararat, Deut. 28:4
  2. the dove sent out to find dry land could not find a place to rest, Deut. 28:9

YHWH wants His people to have a place of rest (i.e. the Promised Land, cf. Deut. 3:20; 12:9-10; 25:19; Josh. 1:13,15; 21:44), but their willful covenant disobedience brought a reverse exodus (i.e. exile, cf. Ps. 95:11).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:65 "failing of eyes"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
28:65 "failing of eyes" This chapter mentions loss of sight several times:

  1. blindness as YHWH's judgment on covenant disobedience, Deut. 28:28-29
  2. judgment seen before your eyes, Deut. 28:30-33
  3. what you see will drive you mad, Deut. 28:34
  4. imagery for premeditated violence against another family member (i.e. "eye shall be evil toward"), Deut. 28:54-56
  5. Egyptian plagues, one of which was utter darkness, Deut. 28:60-61
  6. "failing eyes," a metaphor for fear and despair, utter hopelessness, Deut. 28:65-66
  7. sight caused further dread, Deut. 28:67
28:66-67
NASB, NRSV  "dread"
NKJV, LXX  "fear"
TEV  "terror. . .fear"
NJB  "afraid. . .terror"
JPSOA  "terror. . .dread"

This term (BDB 808 I) means "trembling," or "shaking," caused by fear or joy! Here it is fear (cf. Isa. 33:14). YHWH wanted to cause "dread" in Israel's enemies (cf. Deut. 2:25; 11:25), but because of their disobedience they were the fearful ones!

entries.title: Deuteronomy 28:68 "the Lord will bring you back to Egypt"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
28:68 "the Lord will bring you back to Egypt" The reversal of the Exodus. The re-captivity of Israel! Here it denotes the exiles of Assyria and Neo-Babylon.

▣ "by the way about which I spoke to you" The reference to this statement by YHWH is uncertain.

▣ "there will be no buyer" The VERB "to buy" (BDB 888, KB 1111, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE) was often imagery of YHWH purchasing Israel out of Egyptian bondage (cf. Exod. 15:16; Ps. 74:2), but here it is used of the fate of Israel whereby even Egypt would not buy them back as slaves. They were totally rejected by God and man.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. Why is the cursing section so much longer than the blessing?
  2. What is the purpose of this chapter?
  3. How is works-righteousness related to the blessing enjoined here?
  4. Why is God's judgment so severe?
  5. Have these things occurred in Israel's history?

entries.title: Deuteronomy 29:1 "the words of the covenant which the Lord commanded Moses"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
29:1 "the words of the covenant which the Lord commanded Moses" This is Moses' third address in Deuteronomy (chapters 29-30). He reminds Israel that these laws are from YHWH, not himself. See outline of Moses' sermons in Introduction to Deuteronomy, VIII.

▣ "besides the covenant" This refers to two covenants

  1. at Mt. Sinai/Horeb (Exodus 19-24)
  2. on the plains of Moab (cf. Deut. 1:5; 5:1,3,5-26). It was spelled out clearly in Exodus 20-31.

It was renewed in Exodus 34; Deuteronomy 29-30; and Joshua 24.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Deuteronomy 29:2 "all Israel"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
29:2 "all Israel" This usually refers to only the elders, but because of Deut. 29:1-13, it seems to refer to the entire nation.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name)

entries.title: Deuteronomy 29:2-3 "You have seen. . .your eyes have seen"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
29:2-3 "You have seen. . .your eyes have seen" This is a figure of speech (cf. Deut. 4:34; 7:19) because these people were the children of those who had seen (cf. Num. 14:29; Deut. 5:2-4). Verses 2-8 form a historical review like chapters 1-4, which was a common element of Near Eastern treaties.

▣ "sign and wonders" These terms "signs" (BDB 16) and "wonders" (BDB 68) are mentioned often in Deuteronomy (cf. Deut. 4:34; 6:22; 7:19; 11:3; 26:8; 28:46; 29:2; 34:11) to help the current generation of Israelis to remember YHWH's powerful, gracious acts of deliverance and provisions (cf. Deut. 29:5-7) during the Exodus and Wilderness Wandering Period.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SIGN (OT)

entries.title: Deuteronomy 29:4 "to this day"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
29:4 "to this day" This recurrent phrase may denote a later editor. See full note at Deut. 3:14.

The blindness of Israel to their special place in YHWH's eternal redemptive plan was not just an ancient problem (i.e. Deut. 29:4), but also a current problem (cf. Matt. 13:14-17; Mark 4:10-12; Luke 8:9-10; John 12:36b-43; Acts 28:26-27; and especially Rom. 11:25-32).

The gospel is described as the predetermined plan and foreknowledge of God (cf. Acts 2:23; also note 3:18; 4:28; 13:29).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREKNOWLEDGE

▣ "the Lord has not given you a heart to know, nor eyes to see, nor ears to hear" The Israelites of the exodus and wilderness wanderings saw the physical, but did not comprehend the spiritual dimension of YHWH's actions (i.e. they were a special covenant people who were part of an eternal redemptive plan). This phrase becomes imagery for spiritual blindness and hardness (cf. Isa. 6:9-10; Acts 28:26-27; Rom. 11:8).

There is a word play between Deut. 29:2, "you have seen" and Deut. 29:4, where it is stated they cannot see! This may refer to Israel's rebellions mentioned in Deut. 9:7-24. Without faith God is invisible in history, but with faith history becomes God's track record. It takes a gift (i.e. "given," BDB 678, KB 733, Qal PERFECT) of YHWH's grace for fallen humans to sense and understand His presence!

entries.title: Deuteronomy 29:5 "clothes have not worn out. . .sandal has not worn out"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 29:5 "clothes have not worn out. . .sandal has not worn out" The Jewish commentator, Rashi, says clothes and shoes grew as the children grew (cf. Deut. 8:4; Neh. 9:21).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 29:6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
29:6 Verses 5 and 6 show God's providential care during the entire period of judgment known as the Wilderness Wandering Period (cf. Num. 14:26-35; Deut. 8:2-3). The Israelites were to help maintain the relationship by focusing on YHWH (not food, drink produced by human hands, but on His provision). But these verses also show the continual spiritual blindness of YHWH's people (cf. Isa. 6:9-10).

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

entries.title: Deuteronomy 29:7
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 29:7 This shows YHWH's military presence on behalf of Israel (cf. Num. 21:21-24, 33-35; and Deut. 2:26-3:17).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 29:8
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 29:8 These are the tribes that settled on the eastern side of Jordan (cf. Deut. 3:12-13; Num. 32:28-32).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 29:9 "So keep the words. . .do them"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
29:9 "So keep the words. . .do them" The conditional nature of the covenant (i.e. "keep," BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal PERFECT with waw and "do," BDB 793, KB 889, Qal PERFECT with waw) is recurrent in Deuteronomy (cf. Deut. 4:2,6,9,15,23,40;  5:1,10,12,29,32;  6:2,3,12,17,25;  7:9,11,12;  8:1,2,6,11;  10:13;  11:1,8,16,22,32;  12:1,28,32;  15:5;  16:12;  17:19;  19:9;  24:8;  26:16,17,18;  27:1;  28:1,9,13,15,45,58;  29:9;  30:10,16;  31:12;  32:46). Obedience is a visible measure of the spiritual faithfulness of Israel. To love YHWH is to obey YHWH!

This verse was later read by the rabbis when some of the people were publicly whipped (cf. Deut. 25:3). It contains 13 words to correspond to 13 stripes. Psalm 78:38 was also read.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

▣ "that you may prosper in all that you do" This VERB (BDB 968, KB 1328, Hiphil IMPERFECT) usually means "be prudent" or "circumspect," but in the Hiphil stem it can mean "prosper," "have success" (cf. Josh. 1:7-8; 1 Sam. 18:5,14,15; 1 Kgs. 2:3; 2 Kgs. 18:7; 1 Chr. 22:13). Notice that success and prosperity are contingent on obedience!

entries.title: Deuteronomy 29:10 "You stand"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
29:10 "You stand" Notice the different groupings of Israeli society mentioned in Deut. 29:10-11:

  1.  chiefs, BDB 910
  2.  tribal members, BDB 986
  3.  tribal elders, BDB 278
  4.  tribal officers, BDB 1009, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE
  5.  all the men of Israel, BDB 481, 35, 975 (same as #2)
  6.  children, BDB 381
  7.  wives, BDB 61
  8.  resident aliens, BDB 158
  9.  servants, described in their servant tasks

All these different groups are called upon to attest to their commitment to the covenant (cf. Deut. 29:14-15). This was a formal covenant renewal ceremony!

The number of groups mentioned varies from translation to translation. Some translations (REB) assume that #1 and #2 should be combined (e.g. KJV, "your captains of your tribes," JPSOA, "your tribal leaders"). The ASV, NASB, NIV all have #1-4.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 29:12-13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
29:12-13 This is a covenant renewal text. Notice how "the covenant" (BDB 136) and "the oath" (BDB 46) are parallel (i.e. Gen. 26:28). YHWH's regulations are linked to His promises!

YHWH wants to culminate the promises made to the Patriarchs in Genesis by establishing a people (cf. Deut. 28:9), a people who reflect His character!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

29:12
NASB, NKJV, NRSV, TEV, LXX, JPSOA  "that you may enter
  into the covenant"
NJB  "and you are about
  to pass into the
  covenant
Peshitta  "that you may not
  transgress the
  covenant"

The VERBAL (BDB 716, KB 778, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) literally means "pass over." It is used only in the sense of entering into a covenant here. It is possibly connected to the idea of "cutting" a covenant by passing between the parts of the sacrificial animal as in Gen. 15:17-18. The inference is that the fate of the animal will pass on to the one making the covenant if they disobey the stipulations.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

entries.title: Deuteronomy 29:15 "and with those who are not with us here today"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 29:15 "and with those who are not with us here today" This refers to future generations (cf. Deut. 29:22,29; 5:3-5; 12:25,28).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 29:16-17
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
29:16-17 These verses form a summary parenthesis about the pagan nations Israel encountered in its pilgrimage to the Promised Land.

▣ "their abominations" See SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOMINATION

▣ "their idols" See SPECIAL TOPIC: IDOLATRY

entries.title: Deuteronomy 29:18
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
29:18 The warnings against covenant disobedience (esp. idolatry) is clearly spelled out for each and every member and social group in Israeli society (i.e. individuals, families, tribes).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MAGIC

▣ "a root bearing poisonous fruit and wormwood" This phrase is parallel to "whose heart turns away" (BDB 815, KB 937, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE). The poison is disobedience and the consequences are severe!

  1. YHWH will never be willing to forgive him (Deut. 29:20, negated Qal IMPERFECT, BDB 2, KB 3) and a Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT (BDB 699, KB 757).
  2. YHWH's anger and jealousy will burn against him (Deut. 29:20, BDB 798, KB 896, Qal IMPERFECT).
  3. Every curse will rest on him (Deut. 29:20, BDB 918, KB 1181, Qal PERFECT with waw). This same VERB describes sin as a crouching animal in Gen. 4:7.
  4. YHWH will blot out his name from under heaven (Deut. 29:20, BDB 562, KB 567, Qal PERFECT with waw).
  5. YHWH will single him out for adversity (Deut. 29:21, BDB 95, KB 110, Hiphil PERFECT with waw).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 29:19 "he will boast, saying, 'I have peace though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
29:19 "he will boast, saying, 'I have peace though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart" This is the recurrent attitude of sinners who take God's patience as an excuse to continue to rebel. God's judgment, though often seemingly delayed, will call every stubborn covenant violation into account (i.e. we reap what we sow, cf. Job 34:11; Ps. 28:4; 62:12; Prov. 24:12; Eccl. 12:14; Jer. 17:10; 32:19; Matt. 16:27; 25:31-46; Rom. 2:6; 14:12; 1 Cor. 3:8; 2 Cor. 5:10; Gal. 6:7-10; 2 Tim. 4:14; 1 Pet. 1:17; Rev. 2:23; 20:12; 22:12).

SPECIAL TOPIC: STUBBORNNESS

▣
NASB  "to destroy the watered land with the dry"
NKJV  "as though the drunkard could be included with the
  the sober"
NRSV  "(thus bringing disaster on moist and dry alike)"
TEV  "That would destroy all of you, good and evil alike"
NJB  "much water drives away thirst"
JPSOA  "to the utter ruin of moist and dry alike"
NET Bible  "This will destroy the watered ground with the
  parched"

This is a proverb whose exact meaning is unsure, but the context demands an idiom of complete destruction. Because of one stubborn violator of YHWH's covenant all Israel would suffer (i.e. Hebrew corporality, e.g. Adam, Achan, Jesus). Today we might say, "one bad apple spoils the barrel" or "one bad egg spoils the omelet."

SPECIAL TOPIC: BIBLICAL FAITH IS CORPORATE

entries.title: Deuteronomy 29:20 "The Lord shall never be willing to forgive him"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
29:20 "The Lord shall never be willing to forgive him" This hyperbole must be seen against the background of YHWH's willingness to forgive and accept any repentant believer (i.e. Deut. 30:1-10).

Some Bible teachers link this verse with Ps. 103:9 and assert that there is a limit or threshold to YHWH's grace. I do not accept this. Psalm 103:9 in context (i.e. Deut. 29:8-14) shows He will forgive! The problem is not God's forgiveness, but fallen, rebellious mankind's continual sin! The relationship is broken from mankind's side and it remains broken from mankind's side. Unbelief and rebellion issue in destruction, both temporally and eternally!

▣ "jealousy" This term (BDB 888) is derived from something dyed an intense red (i.e. when anger or zeal caused the blood to flush the face). Human emotions are used to describe YHWH's emotions (anthropomorphism, see SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN). He is zealous for His people (cf. Isa. 26:11). This zealousness can turn to jealousy (cf. Ezek. 5:13; 16:38,42; 23:25; 36:5,6; 38:19; Zeph. 1:18; 3:8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: JEALOUS. . .ZEALOUS

▣
NASB  "will rest on him"
NKJV  "would settle on him"
NRSV  "will descend on them"
TEV, NJB  "will fall on him"
REB  "will fall heavily on him"
LXX  "will attach themselves to him"
Peshitta, NASB margin  "shall lie upon him"
Jewish Study Bible note  "will crouch down upon him"

The MT has the VERB (BDB 918, KB 1181, Qal PERFECT with waw), which means "stretch oneself out," "lie down." This same VERB is used as imagery for sin crouching at Cain's door in Gen. 4:7. It is a personification of sin and evil, as an animal lying in wait to destroy.

▣ "will blot out his name from under heaven" This idiom means (1) no children or (2) death (cf. Gen. 7:4; Exod. 17:14; 32:32; Deut. 9:14; 2 Kgs. 14:27; Ps. 9:5-6).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TWO BOOKS OF GOD

entries.title: Deuteronomy 29:21 "all the curses of the covenant"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 29:21 "all the curses of the covenant" See Deut. 29:27-28; 27:15-26; 28:15-19,20-26,27-37,38-48,49-57; also note Leviticus 26.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 29:22 "Now the generation to come. . .will say"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 29:22 "Now the generation to come. . .will say" This literary form (i.e. children asking questions) is seen earlier in Deut. 6:20, which reflects Exod. 13:8,14; 10:2; 12:26,27. Deuteronomy often speaks of teaching the children (e.g. Deut. 4:10; 6:7).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 29:22-23
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
29:22-23 YHWH's blessing, which was meant to attract those who did not know Him, will be turned into a mocking questioning by foreigners:

  1. plagues of the land, Deut. 29:22
  2. diseases, Deut. 29:22
  3. land is brimstone, Deut. 29:23
  4. land is salt, Deut. 29:23
  5. land is a burning waste, Deut. 29:23
  6. land is sown, and no germination, Deut. 29:23
  7. land is unproductive, Deut. 29:23
  8. land has no grass, Deut. 29:23
  9. land like the cities of the Plain (cf. Gen. 19:24)

All of these YHWH sent (cf. Deut. 29:22-28).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 29:23 "All its land is brimstone and salt"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 29:23 "All its land is brimstone and salt" The land will be as the southern Dead Sea area, which was the site of Sodom and Gomorrah (cf. Gen. 19:24-26).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 29:24 "And all nations will say"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 29:24 "And all nations will say" Israel was a sign to all nations concerning YHWH (i.e. Ezek. 36:22-36). It was meant to be a blessing sign but even if judgment, still a sign!

entries.title: Deuteronomy 29:25 "Because they forsook the covenant"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 29:25 "Because they forsook the covenant" This was and is the basic reason for the divine curses (cf. 2 Kgs. 17:9-23; 2 Chr. 36:13-21).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 29:26 "gods. . .gods"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
29:26 "gods. . .gods" Literally this is Elohim. This term is PLURAL. It usually is translated "God" (i.e. when combined with a SINGULAR VERB). It can also refer to angelic beings and judges.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVENLY COUNCIL OF ANGELIC BEINGS

▣ "have not known" This denotes both information and an intimate, personal relationship. See SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

▣
NASB, NRSV, JPSOA, LXX  "He had not allotted to them"
NKJV  "He has not given to them"
NJB  "no part of their heritage from him"
REB  "whom the Lord had not assigned
  to them"
Peshitta  "nor had they divided spoils among
  them"

The question is "Who does 'them' refer to?"

  1. Israel (LXX)
  2. pagan gods

Number 2 may refer to national angels (cf. Deut. 32:8 in the LXX; also Isa. 24:21; Dan. 10:13,20; see Jewish Study Bible, p. 435).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANGELS AND DEMONS

entries.title: Deuteronomy 29:27 "the anger of the Lord burned against the land"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
29:27 "the anger of the Lord burned against the land" The land is effected by Israel's sin (cf. Gen. 3:17) and human sin in general (cf. Rom. 8:18-22). God uses natural phenomena to redirect mankind's thoughts and priorities.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROBLEMS AND LIMITATIONS OF HUMAN LANGUAGE

entries.title: Deuteronomy 29:28 "the Lord uprooted them"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
29:28 "the Lord uprooted them" This VERB (BDB 684, KB 737, Qal IMPERFECT with waw, cf. 1 Kgs. 14:15; 2 Chr. 7:20; Jer. 12:14) is the opposite of "planted"! The covenant has been reversed!

Notice how YHWH's actions are described:

  1.  in anger ‒ BDB 60 I
  2.  in fury ‒ BDB 404
  3.  in great wrath ‒ BDB 893 and 152
  4.  cast them into another land (i.e. exile, BDB 1020, KB 1527, Hiphil IMPERFECT with waw)

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

▣ "as it is this day" See full note at Deut. 3:14. This may denote a later editor.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 29:29 "The secret things belong to the Lord our God"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
29:29 "The secret things belong to the Lord our God" This refers to

  1. the destiny of humans (cf. Deut. 29:19-20
  2. complete knowledge of YHWH
  3. to His future plans

▣ "but the things revealed belong to us" Humans are responsible for the light they have. If they have no contact with the Bible or the gospel, they are responsible for the revelation in nature (cf. Ps. 19:1-6; Romans 1; see full note at John 14:6) and an inner moral nature (cf. Romans 2). If they have been exposed to Scripture, they are responsible for its content! Believers can know truth and are responsible for it!

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. Why did God have the covenant renewed so often (Deut. 29:1)?
  2. Why did God blind the eyes of the Jews to His purposes (Deut. 29:4-6)?
  3. Does God ever become unwilling to forgive man (Deut. 29:20)?
  4. Why does the land suffer for man's sins (Deut. 29:27)?
  5. What is Deut. 29:29 referring to?

entries.title: Deuteronomy 30:1 "when all of these things have come upon you
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
30:1 "when all of these things have come upon you" Israel's future will be one of two realities based on their covenant obedience (i.e. Deut. 30:15,19; Psalm 1). YHWH desires "blessings," but their choices will determine which of the realities (i.e. blessings or cursings, cf. Leviticus 26) comes into being. Human choices are crucial!

▣ "the blessing and the curse" This is known in Wisdom Literature as "the two ways" (Psalm 1). They are described in Deut. 27; 28; 30:15,19.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BLESSING (OT)

▣ "I have set before you" This VERB (BDB 678, KB 723, Qal PERFECT, cf. Deut. 30:15,19 and note at Deut. 11:26) is imagery for Israel's need to choose one of the two divine consequences related to His covenant.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELECTION/PREDESTINATION vs. HUMAN FREE WILL

▣ "and you call them to mind" This is an idiom meaning "cause to return to your heart" (BDB 996, KB 1427, Hiphil PERFECT with waw, cf. Deut. 4:39; 1 Kgs. 8:47; Isa. 44:19; 46:8).

▣ "in all nations where the Lord your God has banished you" This is predictive prophecy of the choices Israel would make which would result in exile. Notice YHWH did this because of Israel's continual covenant violations and imitations of the Canaanite practices.

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing \ is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Deuteronomy 30:2 "return"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
30:2 "return" This same VERB (BDB 996, KB 1427, Qal PERFECT with waw) was used in Deut. 30:1 (Hiphil PERFECT with waw) in reference to Israel recalling YHWH's covenant. Here it is used in the sense of repentance. There is hope even for covenant violators!

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

entries.title: Deuteronomy 30:2-3
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
30:2-3 This context brings a needed theological balance to the stark judgment of Deut. 29:19. The problem is not rebellion, but sustained, continual rebellion (i.e. generation after generation). Repentance is always possible from God's side, but humans harden their own hearts with willful rebellion and disobedience!

For "heart" see SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART

For "soul" see SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH

▣ "Lord" YHWH is the covenant name of God that the rabbis say reflects His mercy (cf. Gen. 2:4; Exod. 3:13-14).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "God" Elohim is the general name for God which conveys power, might and strength (i.e. God as Creator, Provider, and Sustainer, Genesis 1). The rabbis say it is used of God's justice and righteousness. This distinction between these two names can be seen in Psalm 103, YHWH, and Psalm 104, Elohim.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.

▣ "obey" Notice that "returns to the Lord" is parallel to "obey Him" (BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal PERFECT with waw). Obedience is described in personal terms:

  1. obey his voice ‒ BDB 876 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP)
  2. with all your heart ‒ BDB 523
  3. with all your soul ‒ BDB 659

This is parallel to Deut. 4:29-30; 6:5; 10:12

Notice the number of times and the different senses of the term shub (BDB 996, KB 1427): It is a key term in this chapter for hope and restoration.

  1. "call them to mind" is literally "cause them to return to your heart, Deut. 30:1
  2. "you return to the Lord," Deut. 30:2 (i.e. repentance)
  3. "God will restore you from captivity," Deut. 30:3
  4. "again," Deut. 30:3,8,9
  5. "if you turn to the Lord," Deut. 30:10

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

▣ "with all your heart and soul" This is an idiom of one's whole being (cf. Deut. 30:2,6,10; 4:29; 6:5; 10:12; 11:13; 13:3; 26:16).

▣ "you and your sons" The ancient covenant is being renewed with the current generation (cf. Deut. 29:1). Israel was to educate the children as to the historical bases of their faith (cf. Deut. 4:9,10; 6:7,20-25; 11:19; 32:46) so that each new generation would be part of the ancient covenant.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 30:3-4 "God will restore. . .God has scattered"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 30:3-4 "God will restore. . .God has scattered" Notice YHWH is in control of history. He uses nations and individuals but He is sovereign (cf. Isa. 10:5; 44:28-45:1).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 30:3-9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
30:3-9 Notice what YHWH promised to do for Israel (if they obey, Deut. 30:8,10):

  1. He will restore (Deut. 30:3, BDB 996, KB 1427, Qal PERFECT with waw)
  2. He will have compassion (Deut. 30:3, BDB 933, KB 1216, Piel PERFECT with waw)
  3. He will gather you (BDB 867, KB 1062, Piel PERFECT with waw, twice, Deut. 30:3 and 4)
  4. He will bring you back (Deut. 30:4, BDB 542, KB 534, Qal IMPERFECT with waw)
  5. He will bring you into the land (Deut. 30:5, BDB 97, KB 112, Hiphil PERFECT with waw)
  6. He will prosper you (Deut. 30:5, BDB 405, KB 408, Hiphil PERFECT with waw)
  7. He will multiply you (Deut. 30:5, BDB 915 I, KB 1176, Hiphil PERFECT with waw)
  8. He will circumcise your heart (Deut. 30:6, BDB 557 II, KB 555, Qal PERFECT with waw)
  9. He will inflict all the curses on your enemies (Deut. 30:7, BDB 678, KB 733, Qal PERFECT with waw)
  10. He will prosper you abundantly (Deut. 30:9, BDB 451, KB 451, Hiphil PERFECT with waw)
    1. the work of your hand
    2. the offspring of your body
    3. the offspring of your cattle
    4. the produce of your land (the opposite is in Deut. 28:38-42)
  11. He will again rejoice over you for good (Deut. 30:9, BDB 965, KB 1314 [twice], Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT and Qal PERFECT)
30:4
NASB  "at the ends of the earth"
NKJV  "to the farthest parts under heaven"
NRSV, JPSOA, REB  "to the ends of the world"
TEV  "to the farthest corners of the earth"
NJB, LXX  "to the very sky's end"
Peshitta  "in the outmost parts of heaven"

This is literally "to the end of the heavens," which is a hyperbole (cf. Deut. 4:32; 28:64; Jer. 31:8). It refers to the farthest civilizations they knew (i.e. the ANE and Mediterranean cultures).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE CIRCLE OF THE EARTH

entries.title: Deuteronomy 30:5 "which your fathers possessed"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
30:5 "which your fathers possessed" This could refer to:

  1. the Patriarchs (Moses' day)
  2. the return from the exile (post-exilic editor)

From my study #1 seems best. Verse 9 speaks of the same group.

▣ "He will prosper you and multiply you" This is part of YHWH's promise to Abraham (cf. Genesis 12; 15; 17, etc).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 30:6 "God will circumcise your heart"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
30:6 "God will circumcise your heart" This is imagery for an open and accessible hearing of God's word. The opposite is stated in Deut. 30:17. In Deut. 10:16 and Jer. 4:4; 9:25-26, the Israelite is called upon to perform this spiritual act (cf. Rom. 2:28-29), yet here God must do it. This same tension between God's sovereignty and human action is seen in Ezek. 18:31 vs. Ezek. 36:26. Here, circumcision is imagery for a proper spiritual attitude. See full note at Deut. 10:16.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PREDESTINATION (Calvinism) VS. HUMAN FREE WILL (Arminianism)

▣ "heart" For the Hebrews this was the center of intellectual activity.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART

▣ "descendants" This is literally "seed" (BDB 282). This term is used in this figurative sense several times in Deuteronomy (cf. Deut. 1:8; 4:37; 10:15; 11:9; 28:46,59; 30:6,19; 31:21; 34:4).

▣ "soul" This is the Hebrew word nephesh (BDB659). See notes at Deut. 11:13 and Gen. 35:18; Lev. 17:11 online.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH

entries.title: Deuteronomy 30:8-9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
30:8-9 This reflects what YHWH wanted to do for Israel and for the whole world!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Deuteronomy 30:10 "if. . .if"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
30:10 "if. . .if" This shows the conditional nature of the covenant. Notice that obedience (listen and keep) are paralleled with sincere and total commitment (with all your heart and soul).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S COVENANT REQUIREMENTS OF ISRAEL

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

entries.title: Deuteronomy 30:11-14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
30:11-14 YHWH's will for Israel was not impossible (cf. Deut. 28:29). This verse seems to depreciate the reformers doctrine of "total depravity." There are several places in the OT where human resistence to sin is possible (e.g. Gen. 4:7; Deut. 30:15,19).

The church (i.e. Paul) picks up on Genesis 3 as the origin of sin in mankind, while Rabbinical Midrash picks up on Genesis 6 as the source of the conflict. As Christianity asserts the fallenness of all creation (i.e. Rom. 8:18-19), including humanity (Rom. 3:23), Judaism asserts the basic goodness of humanity. For them the evil is in the choice (i.e. yetzer), not the basic nature.

However, it seems to me that moral accountability is based on the real possibility of comprehending God's will and the ability to act on it. Without the possibility of appropriate action, divine accountability is inappropriate! Can I be held responsible for that which I cannot do?

entries.title: Deuteronomy 30:12 "'Who will go up to heaven'"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
30:12 "'Who will go up to heaven'" Paul uses this in Rom. 10:6-9. It possibly reflects the Sumerian legend of Etana, but probably relates to the Hebrew view of God's sovereignty.

There are several VERBS used in an imperatival sense in this verse (according to OT Parsing Guide):

  1. "to get it" ‒ BDB 542, KB 534, Qal IMPERFECT, but JUSSIVE in meaning
  2. "make us hear" ‒ BDB 1033, KB 1570, Hiphil IMPERFECT, but JUSSIVE in meaning
  3. "we may observe it" ‒ BDB 793, KB 889, Qal IMPERFECT, but COHORTATIVE in meaning

entries.title: Deuteronomy 30:13 "beyond the sea"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
30:13 "beyond the sea" Some see this as related to the Babylonian flood account called the Gilgamesh Epic, but it probably relates to the Jewish fears of sailing or imagery of the ends of the earth.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANE CREATION ACCOUNTS AND FLOOD TEXTS

entries.title: Deuteronomy 30:14 "But the word is very near you, in your mouth and in your heart"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
30:14 "But the word is very near you, in your mouth and in your heart" This refers to YHWH's revealed covenant. The ancients read Scripture aloud! They had to appropriately respond inwardly to what they had heard (i.e. read themselves or read aloud).

▣ "that you may observe it" Humans must make the decision. It is in his ability to do so. God initiates but mankind must respond and continue to respond in repentance, faith, obedience, worship, and perseverance! This is the nature of "covenant."

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

entries.title: Deuteronomy 30:15 "See"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
30:15 "See" This (BDB 906, KB 1157, Qal IMPERATIVE) VERB is used as an idiom for "pay close attention to" (cf. Gen. 27:27; 31:50). It is used several times in Deuteronomy (cf. Deut. 1:8,21,35; 2:24,31; 4:5; 11:26; 30:15; 32:39.

▣ "I have set before you today life and prosperity, and death and adversity" Even covenant Israel had to choose (i.e. conditional covenant)! This is referring to covenant blessing and cursing (cf. Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 27-28).

Remember, the choice is set in a covenant of grace. This is very similar to Wisdom Literature's idiom of the "two ways" (cf. Psalm 1; Prov. 4:10-19; Jer. 21:8; Matt. 7:13-14). Our choices show who we are! How we respond to life's inexplicable "in and outs" reveals our spiritual orientation! Eternal life has observable characteristics!

entries.title: Deuteronomy 30:16-18
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
30:16-18 These verses are a summary of covenant conditions and consequences:

  1. the responsibility (cf. Deut. 8:6; 19:9; 26:17; 28:9)
    1. "to love the Lord," Deut. 30:16 (BDB 12, KB 17, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT)
    2. "walk in His ways," Deut. 30:16 (BDB 229, KB 246, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT; see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY)
    3. "keep His commandments," Deut. 30:16 (BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal INFINITIVE; see SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP)
  2. the consequences of obedience
    1. "you may live," Deut. 30:16 (BDB 310, KB 309, Qal PERFECT with waw)
    2. "you may multiply," Deut. 30:16 (BDB 915, KB 1156, Qal PERFECT with waw)
    3. "your God may bless you," Deut. 30:16 (BDB 138, KB 159, Piel PERFECT with waw)
  3. the conditions and consequences of disobedience
    1. if your heart turns away," Deut. 30:17 (BDB 815, KB 937, Qal IMPERFECT with waw)
    2. "if you will not obey," Deut. 30:17; (BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERFECT with waw)
    3. idolatry
      (1) drawn away (BDB 623, KB 673, Niphil PERFECT with waw)
      (2) worship (BDB 1005, KB 295, Hishtaphel PERFECT with waw)
      (3) serve (BDB 712, KB 773, Qal PERFECT with waw; see SPECIAL TOPIC: WORSHIP)
    4. "you shall surely perish," Deut. 30:18 (BDB 1, KB 2, Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and Qal IMPERFECT of the same root, which expresses intensity)
    5. "you shall not prolong your days," Deut. 30:18 (BDB 73, KB 88, Hiphil IMPERFECT)

Notice how Deut. 30:20 reinforces these covenant responsibilities so that the Patriarchal blessing can be fulfilled! This terminology is characteristic of Deuteronomy.

SPECIAL TOPIC: DEGREES OF REWARDS AND PUNISHMENT

entries.title: Deuteronomy 30:19 "I call heaven and earth to witness"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
30:19 "I call heaven and earth to witness" These witnesses were not unique to Israel's covenant, but are found in several ANE texts. These two permanent aspects of God's creation (cf. Gen. 1:1) function as God's two required witnesses (cf. Deut. 17:6; 19:15; Num. 35:30). This legal emphasis occurs several times in Deuteronomy (cf. Deut. 4:26; 30:19; 31:28; 32:1).

For "Earth" see SPECIAL TOPIC: LAND, COUNTRY, EARTH.

▣ "So choose life in order that you may live" God has given humans the right and responsibility to make moral choices. It is part of His image and likeness in mankind (i.e. Gen.1:26-27)! The Hebrew VERB, "to choose" or "to elect," is used 70% of the time for mankind's choice (cf. NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 639). We must choose (cf. Ezek. 18:30-32)!

▣ "you and your descendants" Deuteronomy characteristically emphasizes the need to pass on the covenant history and responsibilities to the succeeding generations (cf. Deut. 4:9,10; 6:7,20-25; 11:19; 32:46).

Our children are affected by our lifestyle choices and instruction (cf. Exod. 20:5-6; Deut. 5:9-10; 7:9).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 30:20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
30:20 There is a series of Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCTS which summarize the covenant:

  1. responsibilities
    1. loving
    2. obeying
    3. holding fast
  2. consequences ‒ that you may dwell in the land

See note at Deut. 30:16-18. YHWH's covenant demanded an initial and a continual faith, love, obedience, and perseverance.

YHWH promised the land to Israel's patriarchs (cf. Gen. 12:7; 13:14-17; Deut. 9:4-6), but Israel must obey His covenant requirements or the land would be forfeited (cf. Deut. 11:31-32; 28:36,63-68; 30:19-20). The grace gift (unconditional covenant) must be responded to and maintained (conditional covenant)!

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. What is the central truth of this chapter?
  2. Is this chapter speaking about someone becoming a believer or believers being faithful?
  3. Does this chapter contradict Paul's theology about mankind's inability to keep the law (i.e. Galatians 3; Romans 3)?

entries.title: Deuteronomy 31:1 "spoke these words"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:1 "spoke these words" Possibly this should be "finished speaking," following the Septuagint and some manuscripts of the Dead Sea Scrolls (cf. NRSV, REB). This is the end of Moses' three sermons. The UBS Text Project, p. 299, gives the MT a "C" rating (considerable doubt).
