READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Deuteronomy 31:2 "I am a hundred and twenty"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:2 "I am a hundred and twenty" Moses' life of 120 years (cf. Deut. 34:7) can be divided into three 40 year segments. Moses was

  1. 40 years being prepared at the royal academies of Egypt
  2. 40 years in the desert training for his call
  3. 40 years from the time of the burning bush to the present (cf. Exod. 7:7 and Acts 7:23ff)

 Why mention his age? These are possible reasons:

  1. in Egyptian literature 110 years was the age of wise men, but in Syria it was 120 years
  2. age limit of Gen. 6:3
  3. another excuse of Moses for why he will not lead them into the Promised Land (see note below)

▣ "I am no longer able to come and go" This is a Hebrew idiom for

  1. vitality (Josh. 14:11; NRSV, TEV, NJB, JPSOA)
  2. military activity (Jewish Study Bible, p. 438)

However, old age had not taken away Moses' strength, cf. Deut. 34. Possibly this was an excuse (cf. Deut. 1:37) related to Moses' public disobedience recorded in Num. 20:11-12. Deuteronomy 3:23-29 records Moses' pleading with God to let him enter the Promised Land (cf. Deut. 32:48-52).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 31:3 "the Lord your God who will cross ahead of you"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:3 "the Lord your God who will cross ahead of you" YHWH fights for them, though they must prepare for battle and participate (cf. Deut. 31:3-6, i.e. holy war terminology). Moses was a tool used by God. God, Himself, was the one who delivered the people. In reality it is YHWH, not Joshua, who goes into battle ahead of His people!

▣ "Joshua is the one who will cross ahead of you" A new leader was needed because of Moses' disobedience. God will be with Joshua, but he too must perform his covenant obligations (cf. Deut. 1:38; 3:28).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 31:6 "Be strong and courageous"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:6 "Be strong and courageous" This verse has several imperatival forms:

  1. "be strong" ‒ BDB 304, KB 302, Qal IMPERATIVE, cf. Deut. 31:7,23
  2. "be courageous" ‒ BDB 54, KB 65, Qal IMPERATIVE, cf. Deut. 31:7,23
  3. "do not be afraid" ‒ BDB 431, KB 432, negated Qal IMPERFECT, used in a JUSSIVE sense
  4. "do not tremble" ‒ BDB 791, KB 888, negated Qal IMPERFECT, used in a JUSSIVE sense, cf. Deut. 1:29; 7:21; 20:3; Josh. 1:9

Numbers 1 and 2 are repeated by Moses to Joshua in Deut. 31:7 and numbers 3 and 4 are repeated in Deut. 31:8 (#4 is parallel, but a different VERB, "be dismayed," BDB 369, KB 365, Qal IMPERFECT).

A proper attitude and faith are essential! There are giants in the land, but YHWH is with His people (cf. Deut. 31:3,4,5,6).

▣ "He will not fail you or forsake you"

  1. YHWH goes with them (i.e. "walks," BDB 229, KB 246, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE)
  2. YHWH will not fail them (i.e. "abandon," BDB 951, KB 1276, Hiphil IMPERFECT)
  3. YHWH will not forsake them ("leave," BDB 736 I, KB 806, Qal IMPERFECT, cf. Gen. 28:15)

This promise is repeated to Joshua in Josh. 1:5 and is repeated as a promise to NT believers in Heb. 13:5! Our hope is in the unchanging gracious character of YHWH (e.g. Exod. 34:6; Neh. 9:17; Ps. 103:8; 145:8; Joel 2:13; Mal. 3:6)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

entries.title: Deuteronomy 31:7
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:7 This is a public transfer of power! This is the fulfillment of Deut. 1:38 and 3:28!

▣
NASB, JPSOA  "for you shall go with this people"
NKJV  "for you must go with this people"
NRSV  "for you are the one who will go with this
  people"
TEV  "You are the one who will lead these
  people"
LXX  "For you will go before this people"
Peshitta  "For you shall bring this people"

The MT is reflected in the NASB. The UBS Text Project, pp. 299-300, gives this a "D" rating (i.e. highly doubtful). It suggests the translation of the Peshitta (Vulgate).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 31:8 "He will be with you"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 31:8 "He will be with you" This is restated, "I will be with you," in Deut. 31:23! The promise of YHWH's personal presence is the greatest blessing that can be given (cf. Exod. 3:12; 4:12,15; 33:14-16; Deut. 4:37; Josh. 1:5). It is the reason why His leaders and people should not be fearful of anyone or anything!

entries.title: Deuteronomy 31:9 "Moses wrote this law"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:9 "Moses wrote this law" Several times in the Pentateuch it says, "Moses wrote" (cf. Exod. 17:14; 24:4,22; 34:1,27,28; Num. 17:2,3; 33:2; Deut. 4:13; 5:22; 31:9,22). Moses gave the Law to Israel to standardize the will of YHWH for future generations.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOSES' AUTHORSHIP OF THE PENTATEUCH

▣ "to the priests, the sons of Levi" It is interesting that there is some divergency in exactly who are "priests":

  1. tribe of Levi (always)
  2. sons of Aaron (often)

All priests are Levites, but not all Levites are priests. In Deuteronomy the distinction between priests and Levites is removed (i.e. Deut. 18:1).

SPECIAL TOPIC: LEVITICAL PRIESTS

▣ "to the elders" This refers to tribal elders. In this verse Moses entrusts the law to Israel's religious and secular (i.e. tribal) leaders (cf. Deut. 27:1). However, in reality, all of Israel's leaders and laws were seen as religious (i.e. YHWH's will). There was no secular versus sacred in Israel. All was sacred because all belonged to YHWH! There were special days and special places, but all of life was regulated by divine decrees!

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELDERS

entries.title: Deuteronomy 31:10
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:10 There are two dates referred to in this verse:

  1. one was every year, the Feast of Booths
    1. Exod. 23:16-17; 34:22
    2. Lev. 23:33-43
    3. Deut. 16:13-15
  2. one was every seventh year (i.e. the Sabbatical year)
    1. Exod. 23:10,11
    2. Lev. 25:1-7
    3. Deut. 15:1-6

Here, Moses adds to the regular rituals the annual reading of the covenant.

The Feast of the Booths (i.e. #1) was an annual event meant to remind Israel of YHWH's gracious and powerful acts of deliverance from Egypt and His provision and presence during the wilderness wanderings.

This festival of thanksgiving for deliverance/freedom, as well as the freedom from debt ceremony, occurred every seventh year (i.e. #2, Sabbath year, cf. Leviticus 25).

The combination of these two freedom events was a perfect time to review the Mosaic law covenant with this gracious, covenant-making God (i.e. YHWH)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FEASTS OF ISRAEL

entries.title: Deuteronomy 31:11 "the place which He will choose"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:11 "the place which He will choose" This verse in Moses' day referred to the gathering of all males three times a year (cf. Leviticus 23) at the tabernacle (cf. Exod. 20:24; Deut. 12:5,11,13; 14:25; 15:20; 16:7,16; 17:8,10; 18:6; 26:2).

Later it would refer to the central shrine located in Jerusalem.

▣ "you shall read this law in front of all Israel" This was a covenant renewal event. The Law was clearly revealed (i.e. read) and Israel committed herself to its keeping! Everyone in Israel's society was present (cf. Deut. 31:12-13), even the newest generation (i.e. of Bar Mitzvah at age 13, e.g. Isa. 7:16; see SPECIAL TOPIC: AGE OF ACCOUNTABILITY).

The law was not only for a later king nor current leaders, but for all the people through their generation and even resident aliens!

entries.title: Deuteronomy 31:12 "may hear. . .learn. . .fear"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:12 "may hear. . .learn. . .fear" Notice the progression of VERBS:

  1. "hear" ‒ BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERFECT, common in Deuteronomy, meaning "to hear so as to do"; see SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (shema)
  2. "learn" ‒ BDB 540, KB 531, Qal IMPERFECT
  3. "fear" ‒ BDB 431, KB 432, Qal IMPERFECT with waw (see last paragraph below; see SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR)
  4. "be careful to observe" (see SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP)
    1. BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal PERFECT with waw
    2. BDB 793, KB 889, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT

Notice that #1,2,3 are repeated in Deut. 31:13 to relate to the new generation, which did not as yet know (BDB 393, KB 390, Qal PERFECT). This law was meant to be known and kept through multiple generations of Israelis.

In some ways this progression reminds me of Ezra (cf. Ezra 7:10). Israel is to fear or revere (BDB 431) YHWH (cf. Deut. 4:10; 14:23; 17:19), but not fear anyone or anything else!

entries.title: Deuteronomy 31:14 "call. . .present"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:14 "call. . .present" These are two IMPERATIVES.

  1. "call" ‒ BDB 894, KB 1128, Qal IMPERATIVE
  2. "present" ‒ BDB 426, KB 427, Hithpael IMPERATIVE (this refers to an official commissioning by YHWH, cf. 1 Sam. 10:19, or covenant renewal, cf. Josh. 24:1)

▣ "the tent of meeting" There seems to have been two special tents connected to YHWH:

  1. the tabernacle described in Exodus 25-27, which housed the Ark of the Covenant and was positioned at the center of the Israelite camp (see SPECIAL TOPIC: TABERNACLE OF THE WILDERNESS)
  2. the tent of meeting described in Exod. 33:7-11, erected outside of the camp of Israel, where Moses went to meet with YHWH
  3. usually the cloud (i.e. which the rabbis call the Shekinah Cloud of Glory), which symbolized YHWH's personal presence, manifested itself at #1, but here at #2 (cf. Deut. 31:15; Exod. 33:9; see SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEKINAH)
  4. It is possible that several other references relate to #2-Exod. 18:7-16; Num. 11:16,24,26; 12:4

▣ "that I may commission him" In Deut. 31:7 Moses calls Joshua before the people. Here YHWH calls Moses and Joshua before Himself.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 31:15 "a pillar of cloud"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:15 "a pillar of cloud" This same pillar of cloud was what separated the children of Israel from the army of Egypt in Exod. 13:21-22; 14:19-20. This pillar is what filled the temple when Isaiah saw God "high and lifted up" in Isaiah 6. This was a physical symbol of the presence of God. It stayed with the Israelites throughout their wilderness wandering. It functioned in several ways:

  1. it showed YHWH's presence
  2. it led the Israelites from place to place
  3. it shaded them by day
  4. it lit up their camp by night

Once they crossed Jordan, YHWH's presence was manifested over the Ark of the Covenant, but the cloud disappeared.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CLOUD. . .PILLAR

SPECIAL TOPIC: ARK OF THE COVENANT

entries.title: Deuteronomy 31:16 "this people will arise and play the harlot"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:16 "this people will arise and play the harlot" This reveals YHWH's foreknowledge of Israel's continuing sin of idolatry (cf. Deut. 4:15-28; 31:29). Notice the progression of the idolatry in the VERBS:

  1. "will arise" ‒ BDB 877, KB 1086, Qal PERFECT with waw, e.g. Exod. 32:6
  2. "play the harlot" ‒ BDB 275, KB 275, Qal PERFECT with waw
    1. act as a harlot
      (1) Lev. 21:7,9,14
      (2) Deut. 22:21; 23:18
    2. imagery of the Promised Land, Lev. 19:29
    3. imagery of foreign alliances
      (1) Isa. 23:17
      (2) Jer. 3:1
      (3) Ezek. 16:26,28
    4. imagery of fertility idolatry
      (1) Exod. 34:15,16
      (2) Lev. 17:7; 20:5
      (3) Deut. 31:16
  3. "will forsake Me" ‒ BDB 736, KB 806, Qal PERFECT with waw, cf. Deut. 28:20; Jdg. 10:6,10; Jer. 1:16
  4. "break My covenant" ‒ BDB 830, KB 974, Hiphil PERFECT with waw, cf. Deut. 31:20; Lev. 26:15; Jer. 11:10

SPECIAL TOPIC: IDOLATRY

entries.title: Deuteronomy 31:17 "My anger will be kindled"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:17 "My anger will be kindled" This VERB (BDB 354, KB 351, Qal PERFECT with waw) is often used of YHWH's anger: (see SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN)

  1. against Moses, Exod. 4:14
  2. against Israel, Exod. 22:24; 32:10; Num. 11:1,10; 32:10; Deut. 6:15; 7:4; 11:17; 31:17
  3. against the spies, Num. 12:9
  4. against Balaam, Num. 22:22
  5. against the land, Deut. 29:27

▣ "I will forsake them and hide My face from them" These two VERBS describe anthropomorphically YHWH's nullification of the covenant. YHWH does to them what they did to Him (cf. Deut. 31:16).

  1. "I will forsake them" ‒ BDB 736, KB 806, Qal PERFECT with waw
  2. "hide My face from them" ‒ BDB 711, KB 771, Hiphil PERFECT with waw, cf. Deut. 31:18; 32:20; Isa. 59:2; 64:7). This is an idiom for the removal of covenant fellowship and blessing.

The consequences are:

  1. they shall be consumed
    1. VERB, "to be" ‒ BDB 224, KB 243, Qal PERFECT with waw
    2. consumed/devoured ‒ BDB 37, KB 46, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT
  2. many evils and troubles will come
    1. "will come" ‒ BDB 592, KB 619, Qal PERFECT with waw
    2. evil ‒ BDB 949
    3. troubles ‒ BDB 865 I
  3. YHWH's presence (cf. Deut. 31:6,8) will not be with them (i.e. "our God is not among us")

entries.title: Deuteronomy 31:18
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:18 The threat from Deut. 31:17 (i.e. "I will hide my face from them") is emphatically repeated (Hiphil INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and Hiphil IMPERFECT of the same root, BDB 711, KB 771).

▣ "other gods" The Jewish Study Bible asserts that "our God" of Deut. 31:17 should be translated "our gods" and relate to "other gods" in Deut. 31:18 (cf. P. 439).

The first term (BDB 43, v. 17) seems to be a singular form derived from Elohim (BDB 43) in Deut. 31:18. It can be used of a pagan god (i.e. PLURAL VERBS, cf. 2 Chr. 32:15; Dan. 11:37), but also for YHWH (SINGULAR VERBS, cf. Deut. 32:15,17; Ps. 50:22; 114:7; 139:19; Prov. 30:5; Isa. 44:8).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 31:19 "write this song for yourselves"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 31:19 "write this song for yourselves" The "song" (BDB 1010) is mentioned five times in this chapter (vv. 19,21,22,30). It refers to "the Song of Moses" in Deuteronomy 32. This would be a witness for YHWH against the future actions of Israel. This, of course, is legal imagery (cf. Deut. 4:26; 30:19; 31:28; Josh. 24:22)! Israel was responsible to instruct every new generation in YHWH's law!

entries.title: Deuteronomy 31:20 "into the land flowing with milk and honey"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:20 "into the land flowing with milk and honey" See full note at Deut. 6:3.

▣ "they have eaten and are satisfied and become prosperous then they will turn to other gods" The hardest times for the people of God are during the times of great prosperity! We tend to forget so easily (cf. Deut. 6:10-15; 8:11-20; 32:15-18).

▣ Notice the downward progression into rebellion:

  1. they will turn to other gods ‒ BDB 815, KB 937, Qal PERFECT with waw, cf. Deut. 31:18; 29:18; 30:17
  2. serve them ‒ BDB 712, KB 773, Qal PERFECT with waw, cf. Deut. 4:19; 7:4; 8:19; 11:16; 13:6,13; 17:3; 28:14,36,64; 29:18,26; 30:17
  3. spurn Me ‒ BDB 610, KB 658, Piel PERFECT with waw, cf. Num. 14:11,23; Isa. 1:4
  4. break My covenant ‒ BDB 830, KB 974, Hiphil PERFECT with waw, cf. Deut. 31:16; Lev. 26:15; Jer. 11:10; 31:32

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

entries.title: Deuteronomy 31:21 "when many evils and troubles have come upon them"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:21 "when many evils and troubles have come upon them" These evils and troubles were mentioned in Deut. 31:17 and predicted in Deut. 4:30.

▣ "(for it shall not be forgotten from the lips of their descendants)" This is a promise of a faithful remnant and continued knowledge of YHWH's law.

SPECIAL TOPIC: REMNANT (THREE SENSES)

▣ "intent" The Hebrew word yetzer is sometimes translated "imagination of the heart" (BDB 428 I, it can be used in a positive sense, Isa. 26:3). This is the OT way of saying that YHWH knows the tendency toward rebellion which is within mankind (i.e. Gen. 6:5; 8:21; Ps. 103:14; Jer. 18:23).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

entries.title: Deuteronomy 31:23
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:23 Moses spoke these words to Israel in Deut. 31:6. Moses spoke these words to Joshua in Deut. 31:7 (cf. Deut. 1:38; 3:28). Now (Deut. 31:23) YHWH speaks these words directly to Joshua (cf. Josh. 1:6,7,9), who stood with Moses at the door of the tabernacle.

  1. "be strong" ‒ BDB 304, KB 302, Qal IMPERATIVE
  2. "be courageous" ‒ BDB 54, KB 65, Qal IMPERATIVE

▣ "I will be with you" This statement identifies the PRONOUN "he" of Deut. 31:23a. This is YHWH's greatest gift (cf. Exod. 3:12; 4:12,15; 33:14-16; Deut. 4:37; 31:6,8; Josh. 1:5)! This is the meaning of "Immanuel" (cf. Isa. 7:14; 8:8,10).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 31:24
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 31:24 See SPECIAL TOPIC: MOSES' AUTHORSHIP OF THE PENTATEUCH

entries.title: Deuteronomy 31:26 "beside the ark"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:26 "beside the ark" The KJV has "in," but the better translation is "beside" (NKJV, NRSV, TEV, NJB, cf. Exod. 25:16; 1 Kgs. 8:9); and for a description of "the ark" see Exod. 25:10-22.

In the OT apparently only the two tablets of stone on which the Ten Commandments written by God (Exod. 31:18) were contained in the Ark (as well as the pieces of the first set that Moses broke, e.g. Exod. 32:19; 34:1). There are three other items which were later placed beside the Ark:

  1. a jar of manna, Exod. 16:33-34
  2. Aaron's rod that budded, Num. 17:10
  3. this copy of the law written by Moses

However, there must have been some confusion about this within rabbinical traditions, because the author of Hebrews asserts that the Ark contained the stone tablets and #1 and #2 (cf. Heb. 9:4).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ARK OF THE COVENANT

▣ "covenant" See SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 31:27 "For I know your rebellion and your stubbornness"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:27 "For I know your rebellion and your stubbornness" Moses had experienced Israel's rebellious tendencies (cf. Deut. 31:21) during his lifetime (cf. Deut. 9:7-29).

▣
NASB  "stubbornness"
NKJV  "stiff neck"
NRSV, TEV, REB, Peshitta  "stubborn"
NJB, JPSOA  "stiff necked"
LXX  "hard neck"

The term is a combination of "neck" (BDB 791) and "stiff" or "hard" (BDB 904). Israel is often described by this unflattering combination (cf. Exod. 32:8; 33:3,5; 34:9; Deut. 9:6,13; 31:27). The VERB is used in Deut. 10:16; 2 Kgs. 17:14; Neh. 9:16,17,29; Jer. 7:26; 17:23; 19:15. The same thought is expressed in Isa. 48:4 and Ezek. 2:4; 3:7.

In a sense Deut. 31:27-29 are a prophecy, based on the past actions of Israel. This same kind of prophecy is also found in Josh. 24:19-20. Israel's best efforts were not enough. The first covenant would fail to restore the intended intimacy between YHWH and His highest creation (i.e. mankind) in the Garden of Eden. It would take the New Covenant (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-36) based on YHWH's actions. Mankind was incurably rebellious (cf. Gen. 6:5; 8:21; Jer. 17:9; Rom. 1-3; Gal. 3).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 31:28
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:28 This verse has three IMPERATIVAL VERBS:

  1. "assemble" ‒ BDB 874, KB 1078, Hiphil IMPERATIVE
  2. "speak" ‒ BDB 180, KB 210, Piel COHORTATIVE
  3. "call" ‒ BDB 729, KB 795, Hiphil COHORTATIVE

Moses addresses the leaders (i.e. elders and officers), who symbolize all Israel, directly. This may refer to a representative national council (e.g. Jdgs. 21:16).

▣ "the heavens and the earth to witness against them" These specific ratification witnesses are often mentioned in covenant contexts (cf. Deut. 4:26; 30:19; 31:28; 32:1).

In this chapter there are also two other witnesses:

  1. Moses' song, Deut. 31:19,21
  2. law scroll, Deut. 31:26

entries.title: Deuteronomy 31:29
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:29 Notice the downward progression after Moses' death (cf. Josh. 24:19-28):

  1. you will act corruptly ‒ BDB 1007, KB 1469, both the Hiphil IMPERFECT and the INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE, cf. Deut. 4:16,25; 9:12
  2. turn from the way ‒ BDB 693, KB 747, Qal PERFECT with waw
  3. you will do that which is evil (BDB 948 II) in the sight of the Lord ‒ BDB 793 I, KB 889, Qal IMPERFECT
  4. provoking Him to anger with the work of your hands (BDB 795 and 388, i.e. idolatry) ‒ BDB 494, KB 491, Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT,, cf. Deut. 4:25; 9:18; 32:16; 1 Kgs. 16:7; 2 Kgs. 17:7; 21:6; Jer. 25:6,7; 32:30; 44:8

entries.title: Deuteronomy 31:30
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:30 This verse should go with chapter 32.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. Why is God changing leaders?
  2. How is God's foreknowledge and man's choice related in this chapter?
  3. Why did Israel turn away from God?

entries.title: Deuteronomy 33:1 "the blessing. . .blessed"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
33:1 "the blessing. . .blessed" The VERB (BDB 138, KB 159, Piel PERFECT) and the NOUN occur in Deut. 33:1.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BLESSING

▣ "the man of God" This phrase (BDB 35 CONSTRUCT BDB 43) was used to describe prophets (cf. Josh. 14:6; 1 Sam. 2:27; 9:6-7; 1 Kgs. 9:6; 12:22; 13:1,30; 2 Kgs. 1:9-13; 5:8; 23:17; Jer. 35:4). Moses was a prophet (i.e. Deut. 18:15).

entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. This chapter is very similar to Genesis 49. Both reflect the ancient Jewish tradition of a Patriarchal blessing on the children (i.e. Jacob to his sons in Genesis 49). Here Moses is a surrogate father to the tribes of Israel and pronounces the family blessing and warning on each one.

  2. The song of chapter 32, with its severe warnings, must be combined with the blessing of Deuteronomy 33 to see the full counsel of YHWH's word (i.e. curses and blessings, cf. Lev. 26; Deut. 28).!

  3. This poem seems to break the continuity between Deut. 32:48-52 and Deut. 34. Why it was inserted here, when and by whom, cannot be answered. It is assumed to be an inspired poetic blessing linked to Moses.
    SPECIAL TOPIC: INSPIRATION

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Deuteronomy 33:2
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
33:2 This describes a revelatory appearance of YHWH to Israel (i.e. theophany). This awesome encounter between the Divine and humans was terrifying (cf. Exodus 19; Ps. 50:2-3). YHWH's presence was continued in the form of the special cloud (i.e, Shekinah cloud of glory; see SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEKINAH). YHWH came and stayed with His people from Mt. Sinai/Horeb until they crossed the Jordan. Even then, His special presence was with the Ark, above the wings of the cherubim.

It is obvious from this verse that YHWH is associated with mountains (cf. 1 Kgs. 20:23,28).

  1. Moriah (Gen. 22:2; 2 Chr. 3:1, site of the temple)
  2. Mt. Sinai/Horeb (Exodus 19-20)
  3. Mt. Seir (here, Jdg. 5:4)
  4. Mt. Paran (here, Hab. 3:3)
  5. Ebal/Gerizim (27:4; Josh. 8:30-33)
  6. Tabor (Jdgs. 4:6)
  7. Carmel (1 Kgs. 18:20-39; 2 Kgs. 4:25-27)
  8. Perazim (2 Sam. 5:20; Isa. 28:21)
  9. Mt. Zion (Isa. 2:1-4; Mic. 4:1-4; Ps. 68:16, name for Jerusalem)
  10. Mt. Nebo (Deuteronomy 34, to Moses only)

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHERUBIM

SPECIAL TOPIC: ARK OF THE COVENANT

▣ "Sinai" This is the place of the giving of the Law. It is called Sinai (BDB 696) only here in Deuteronomy. It is usually called Horeb (BDB 352).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOREB

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE LOCATION OF MT. SINAI

▣ "Seir" This name (BDB 973) has several different referents in the OT:

  1. It can refer to the land of Edom ‒ Gen. 32:3; 36:30; Num. 24:18; Deut. 1:44; 2:8,12,22,29; 33:1; Josh. 11:17; Jdgs. 5:4.
  2. It can refer to a mountain/hill in Edom ‒ Gen. 36:8-9; Deut. 1:2; 2:14; Josh. 24:4.
  3. It can refer to a people ‒ Gen. 36:20-30; 2 Chr. 25:11,14; Ezek. 25:8 (of Edom)
  4. It can refer to a mountain/hill in Judah ‒ Josh. 15:10(?).

▣ "Mount Paran" This is the mountain range (BDB 803) close to the plains of Moab (cf. Deut. 1:1) on the west side of Arabah, down the west side of the Gulf of Aqaba.

Perhaps this listing is of the travel of the children of Israel as they left Sinai going into the Promised Land (also can be a wilderness, cf. Num. 10:12; 12:16; 13:3,26). God was saying that He had been with them throughout the wanderings and He was still with them.

▣
NASB  "the midst of ten thousand holy ones"
NKJV, Peshitta  "with ten thousands of saints"
NRSV, REB  "myriads of holy ones"
TEV  "ten thousand angels were with him"
NJB    ——
LXX  "with myriads of Kades"

The MT here has "Ribeboth-Kodesh." Deuteronomy 32:51 translates similar consonants as "Meribah-Kadesh. This could refer to

  1. an unknown place name (JPSOA)
  2. "angels" (cf. Ps. 68:17; Dan. 7:10; Rev. 5:11)
  3. "saints" (LXX, cf. Deut. 7:6; 33:3; 14:2; 26:19; 28:9)

Rabbinical Midrash uses this as text to assert the intermediary role of angels (cf. Acts 7:53; Gal. 3:19; Heb. 2:2).

SPECIAL TOPIC: holy ones

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVENLY COUNCIL OF ANGELIC BEINGS

▣
NASB, JPSOA  "flashing lightning"
NKJV  "a fiery law"
NRSV  "a host of his own"
TEV  "a flaming fire"
NJB  "blazed forth"
NASB margin  "a fiery Law"
LXX  "angels with him"

Literally this is "fiery law" (BDB 77 and 206). However, in this context it refers to the coming glory of the brilliance of YHWH's glory (cf. Isa. 60:1-3).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY (OT, kabod)

entries.title: Deuteronomy 33:3 "He loves the people"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
33:3 "He loves the people" The VERB (BDB 285, KB 284, Qal PARTICIPLE) seems to reflect Deut. 4:37; 7:7-8; 10:15.

The OBJECT "people" is PLURAL and refers to the descendants of the Patriarchs.

▣
NASB  "All Your holy ones are in Your hand"
NKJV  "All His saints are in your hand"
NRSV  "All his holy ones were in your charge"
TEV  "protects those who belong to him"
NJB  "Your holy ones are all at your command"
JPSOA footnote  "All His worshippers in your care"
REB  "blesses his holy ones"
LXX  "All of the sanctified ones under your hands"

The term "holy ones" (BDB 481 CONSTRUCT BDB 872) refers to the covenant people. This could be translated "saints" (e.g. Deut. 7:6; 14:2,21; 26:19; 28:9; "holy people").

The JPSOA footnote says "the meaning of vv. 3-5 is uncertain." The Jewish Study Bible, p. 446, suggests that "'the hallowed'" originally referred to the divine council but that the poem's editors shifted the focus to Israel." It asserts that this was done to make sense of v. 4.

SPECIAL TOPIC: Holy Ones

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVENLY COUNCIL OF ANGELIC BEINGS

▣
NASB, JPSOA, Peshitta  "followed"
NKJV  "sit down"
NRSV  "marched"
TEV  "bow"
NJB  "fell"
REB  "sit"

This is literally "lie down at" (BDB 1067, KB 1730, Pual PERFECT, unusual VERB only here). It could also refer to the position of a learner

  1. bowed low, cf. TEV
  2. sit at your feet , cf. REB, NET Bible

"They" refers to the people of Israel.

▣ "Everyone receives of Your words" This refers to the giving of the law at Mt. Sinai/Horeb in Exodus 19-20 and following. God's people knew God's will and law. The covenant people have a special responsibility to reflect God's character.

All of them affirmed their willingness to follow God's law.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 33:4 "Moses charged us with a law"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
33:4 "Moses charged us with a law" This seems to confirm the idea in the preceding verses that the reference in Deut. 33:3 is to a place name and that these verses are talking about God's people, not angels.

▣ "A possession for the assembly of Jacob" The term "possession" (BDB 440) refers to an inheritance (BDB 439). It was used first of the tribe of Israel (Jacob, BDB 784) in Exod. 6:8 and is mentioned often in Ezekiel (cf. Ezek. 11:15; 33:24; 36:2,3,5).

The term "assembly" (BDB 875) means "congregation" (cf. same root in Deut. 23:2,3,4,8; 31:30).

Because of the parallelism in Deut. 33:4, this particular usage of "possession" may be imagery for the covenant (i.e. law). God's people possess a revelation as well as a land!

entries.title: Deuteronomy 33:5 "He was king"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
33:5 "He was king" This is a reference to YHWH as King (BDB 572 I, cf. Exod. 15:18; Num. 23:21; 24:7; 1 Sam. 8:4-9; Ps. 29:10).

▣ The last two lines parallel "heads of the people" and "the tribes of Israel." It refers to the inauguration of the covenant with the new people of God at Mt. Sinai/Horeb (cf. Exodus 19-20).

▣ "Jeshurun" This is literally "the upright ones" (BDB 449) and refers to Israel (cf. Deut. 33:26; 32:15; Isa. 44:2).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 33:6 "May Reuben live and not die"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
33:6 "May Reuben live and not die" Verse 6 has three Qal JUSSIVE forms:

  1. live ‒ BDB 310, KB 309
  2. die ‒ BDB 559, KB 562 (negated)
  3. be ‒ BDB 224, KB 243 (negated)

Reuben was the firstborn of Jacob, but he sinned against his father (cf. Gen. 35:22) and lost his preeminence (cf. Gen. 49:3-4).

▣
NASB  "Nor his men be few"
NKJV  "nor let his men be free"
NRSV  "even though his numbers are few"
TEV  "although their people are few"
NJB  "though his men be few"
REB  "may he be few in number"
JPSOA  "though few be his number"
Peshitta  "Let his people be numerous"
LXX  "Let him be many in number"

This is part of the loss of preeminence (cf. TEV, NJB). This phrase often means "not very many men" (cf. Gen. 34:30; Deut. 4:27; Ps. 105:12; Jer. 44:28).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 33:7 "Hear"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
33:7 "Hear" This VERB (BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERATIVE) is used often in Deuteronomy, but usually it is YHWH (or Moses) speaking to Israel.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (Shema)

▣ "O Lord" See SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "the voice of Judah" In context Moses is asking YHWH to hear Judah's prayer (i.e. the tribe of Judah's prayer). There is nothing in Moses' blessing that hints of Judah's special place as royal tribe, so evident in Jacob's blessing of Gen. 49:8-12.

The fact that the tribe of Simeon is not mentioned in chapter 33 has caused some to relate this prophecy to a later period when Simeon was incorporated into Judah (cf. Josh. 19:1-9; Jdgs. 1:3-4). Simeon's allotment was southwest of Judah, which was adjacent to the five powerful Philistine city-states.

▣
NASB  "With his hands he contended for them"
NKJV  "Let his hands be sufficient for him"
NRSV, REB  "strengthen his hands for him"
TEV  "Fight for them, Lord"
NJB  "that his hands may defend his rights"
Peshitta  "Let his hands contend for him"
LXX  "his hand will decide for him"

This Hebrew phrase is uncertain. It may refer to Judah defending itself against enemies, which may point toward the division of the unified monarchy in 922 B.C. into Judah and Israel (only speculation).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 33:8-11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
33:8-11 In the Qumran literature, scrolls found in caves northwest of the Dead Sea, Deut. 18:18 and Num. 24:15-17, have definite Messianic prophecies linked with this passage. They thought that the Messiah was related to the tribe of Levi (cf. Ps. 110:4-7; Zechariah 3-4).

This blessing includes not only the past faithful acts of Aaron (cf. Ps. 106:16), but also of Moses (cf. last two lines of Deut. 33:8 and Exod. 17:1-7).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 33:8 "Your Thummim and Your Urim"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
33:8 "Your Thummim and Your Urim" These two items (BDB 1070 and BDB 22) were

  1. a mechanical way (i.e. lots)
  2. a visible light which denoted a prophecy to know the will of YHWH
  3. Apparently they were kept by the High Priest in a pouch behind the breast plate (cf. Exod. 28:30; Lev. 8:8; 1 Sam. 14:37-42; 23:9-12).
  4. Exactly what they were and how they worked has been lost (cf. NIDOTTE, vol. 1, pp. 329-331).

SPECIAL TOPIC: URIM AND THUMMIM

▣ "Your godly man" This may refer to Aaron or Moses or the descendant of the High Priest, but the historical reference mentioned refers to Moses.

▣ "Massah. . .Meribah" Read Exod. 17:7. However, the rebellion at this location did not mention Levi or the priests in any way. The exact connection is uncertain.

▣ Apparently YHWH tested both Israel and her leadership during the wilderness wandering period to see if they really trusted Him and His care and guidance (cf. Exod. 17:7).

  1. proved/tested ‒ BDB 650, KB 702, Piel PERFECT
  2. strive/contend ‒ BDB 936, KB 1224, Qal IMPERFECT

 Notice that YHWH regularly tests (BDB 650) the motives and commitment of those who claim to know and trust Him:

  1. Abraham ‒ Genesis 22
  2. Israel ‒ Exod. 15:25; 16:4; 20:20; Deut. 8:2,16; 13:3 Jdg. 2:22; 3:1,4
  3. Moses ‒ Deut. 33:8
  4. Hezekiah ‒ 2 Chr. 32:31
  5. Jesus was also tested ‒ Matthew 4; Luke 4

This same word is used often for humans "testing" God, which is always seen in a negative light!

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD TEXTS HIS PEOPLE

entries.title: Deuteronomy 33:9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
33:9 This refers to the passage in Exodus 32, where Israel became involved in idolatry in the making and worshiping (i.e. sexual orgy) of the golden calf. At this point Moses ordered the faithful Levites (his own tribe) to kill many of their fellow Israelites in judgment (cf. Deut. 32:25-29).

By this action, even against their own family, they are honored for:

  1. they observed Your word ‒ BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal PERFECT, cf. Deut. 29:9
  2. they kept Your covenant ‒ BDB 665, KB 718, Qal IMPERFECT, cf. Ps. 25:10; 78:7; 119:2,22, 33,34,56,69,100,115,129,145

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

entries.title: Deuteronomy 33:10 "teach. . .put incense. . .and whole burnt offerings"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
33:10 "teach. . .put incense. . .and whole burnt offerings" These are the duties of the Levitical priests:

  1. teaching ‒ BDB 434, KB 436, Hiphil IMPERFECT, cf. Deut. 31:9-13, which includes judging, cf. Deut. 17:9-10
  2. duties at the tabernacle/temple
  3. remember, in Deuteronomy there is no disctinction bewteen the duties of the priests and Levites (i.e. Deut. 18:1)

SPECIAL TOPIC: LEVITICAL PRIESTS

▣ "to Jacob. . .to Israel" See SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name)

entries.title: Deuteronomy 33:11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
33:11 This short verse has four VERBS and two PARTICIPLES:

  1. "bless" ‒ BDB 138, KB 159, Piel IMPERATIVE, cf. Deut. 33:1,13,20,24; 28:3 (twice),4,5,6 (twice),8,12,19; 30:16. This is what YHWH wants to do!
  2. "accept" ‒ BDB 953, KB 1280, Qal IMPERFECT. This is a sacrificial term, cf. Lev. 1:4; 7:18; 19:7; 22:23,25,27, which can also mean "enjoy," Lev. 26:34 (twice)
  3. "shatter" ‒ BDB 563, KB 571, Qal IMPERATIVE, used of YHWH in Deut. 32:39, here of their enemies (cf. #4, #5, and #6)
  4. "those who rise up" ‒ BDB 877, KB 1086, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE, used of adversaries
    1. to God, Exod. 15:7
    2. to Israel, Exod. 32:25; Ps. 109:28
    3. to one's neighbor, Deut. 19:11
  5. "those who hate him" ‒ BDB 971, KB 1338, Piel PARTICIPLE, often in the Psalms for enemies, cf. Deut. 18:40; 44:7,10; 55:12; 68:1; 89:23
  6. "rise again" (negated) ‒ same root as #4, but here a Qal IMPERFECT. This could refer to the other Israelites who attacked Moses' and Aaron's leadership during the wilderness wandering period.
▣
NASB, NKJV, NRSV, JPSOA, Peshitta  "bless his substance"
TEV  "help their tribe to grow
  strong"
NJB  "bless his worthiness"
REB  "bless his powers"
LXX  "bless his strength"

This term (BDB 298) can have several connotations:

  1. its basic meaning is "capacity" or "power"
  2. "strength"
  3. "ability," "skills"
  4. "worthiness"
  5. "accomplishments"
  6. "possessions"

▣ "Shatter the loins" This is literally "break the thigh" (i.e. the largest muscle in the body used as a symbol for the whole person). This is Hebrew imagery for making someone powerless. It is even possible that it has the connotation of stopping procreation, thereby, no future generations.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 33:12 "Of Benjamin. . .beloved of the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
33:12 "Of Benjamin. . .beloved of the Lord" He (BDB 122) may be called "beloved of the Lord" because he was the favorite of his father, Jacob (cf. Gen. 44:20).

▣ "dwell in security by Him" The VERB (BDB 1014, KB 1496, is a Qal IMPERFECT, but in a JUSSSIVE sense, cf. Deut. 33:12 [twice],16,20,28; Exod. 25:8; 29:45,46; JPSOA does not translate this as a JUSSSIVE, but as a statement). YHWH is their close companion in Deut. 33:12.

The MT has "by Him" in line 2 but this word may be an ancient name for Deity. The UBS Text Project, p. 312, suggests "most-high." The LXX translates it as "God overshadows him all the days," which, if correct, shows this Divine name must start line 3 (NRSV, NJB, REB).

This ancient name (עלו, BDB 752-754, usually a PREPOSITION) for Deity might also appear in 1 Sam. 2:10, line 2.

▣
NASB, REB  "Who shields him all the day"
NKJV  "who shelters him all the day long"
NRSV  "surrounds him all day long"
TEV  "He guards them all the day long"
NJB  "protects him day after day"
JPSOA  "ever does protect him"
Peshitta  "The Lord shall have compassion on him"
LXX  "God over shadows him all day long"

The VERB (BDB 342, KB 339, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE) is used only here and can mean "to enclose" or "to surround" or "to cover."

▣
NASB, NKJV  "dwells between His shoulders"
NRSV, LXX, JPSOA  "rest between his shoulders"
TEV  "he dwells in their midst"
NJB  "dwells between his hillsides"

This is imagery for

  1. a place of peace and security (Deut. 33:20,28)
  2. living in a sheltered place (i.e. Shiloh, Bethel, or Jerusalem [a suggestion of S. R. Driver])

entries.title: Deuteronomy 33:13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 33:13 This verse refers to the abundance of moisture from dew and underground sources (cf. Gen. 49:25). Water meant agricultural abundance (cf. Gen. 49:25)!

entries.title: Deuteronomy 33:13-17
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
33:13-17 The longest of the blessings, except for Levi, goes to the sons of Joseph, Ephraim, and Manasseh (cf. Deut. 33:17, Joseph's two sons by Egyptian wives). These were the most powerful of the northern tribes.

  1. In Deut. 33:13-16b Moses enumerates agricultural blessings on these two tribes.
  2. In Deut. 33:16c,d Joseph's status in Egypt is acknowledged.
  3. In Deut. 33:17 the power of these two tribes is expressed in animal imagery.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 33:15 "the best things of the ancient mountains. . .And. . .of the everlasting hills"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 33:15 "the best things of the ancient mountains. . .And. . .of the everlasting hills" This may refer to trees, both for food and construction.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 33:16 "And the favor of Him who dwelt in the bush"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
33:16 "And the favor of Him who dwelt in the bush" This may refer to the burning bush (cf. Exod. 3:2-4). This word for bush (BDB 702) is used only five times in the OT, four of them in Exod. 3:2-4.

▣
NASB  "And to the crown of the head of the one
 distinguished among his brothers"
NKJV  "And on the crown of the head of him who was
 separate from his brothers"
NRSV  "on the brow of the prince among his brothers"
TEV  "because he was the leader among his brothers"
NJB  "on the brow of the consecrated one among his
 brothers"

This reflects Jacob's blessing in Gen. 49:26. The leadership and preeminence of Joseph continues in his sons' descendants.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 33:17 "And his horns are the horns of the wild ox"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
33:17 "And his horns are the horns of the wild ox" In Hebrew the word "horn" (BDB 901) is a symbol of power.

▣ "to the ends of the earth" This is a CONSTRUCT of BDB 67 and BDB 75. It has such powerful theological significance.

  1. uniqueness of YHWH (and thereby monotheism)
    1. Isa. 45:6,14; 46:9; 47:8,10
    2. Zeph. 2:15
  2. the power and glory of YHWH
    1. Prov. 30:4
    2. many of those under #3
  3. the extension of YHWH's worship and rule to all the earth
    1. Deut. 33:17
    2. 1 Sam. 2:10
    3. Ps. 22:25-31; 59:13; 67:1-7; 98:2-9
    4. Isa. 45:22; 52:10
    5. Jer. 16:19
  4. Messianic
    1. 1 Sam. 2:10
    2. Ps. 2:8
    3. Micah 5:4-5

▣ "the ten thousands of Ephraim. . .and the thousands of Manasseh" This phrase shows the priority of Ephraim in size and power.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THOUSAND (eleph)

entries.title: Deuteronomy 33:18 "Of Zebulun. . .And, Issachar"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
33:18 "Of Zebulun. . .And, Issachar" These two tribes are also listed together as in Gen. 49:13-15.

▣ "Rejoice" This VERB (BDB 970, KB 1333, Qal IMPERATIVE) is used in the sense of "enjoy the good, safe abundance of life."

▣ "going forth" This (BDB 422, KB 425, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) seems to be used in the sense of a free life (cf. Deut. 28:6,19; 31:2).

▣ "in your tents" This (BDB 13) refers to their home during the wilderness wandering period, but became imagery for one's house.

These two parallel lines imply a happy, settled life.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 33:19
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
33:19 The parallelism between "mountain" (BDB 249) and "offer righteous sacrifices" (cf. Ps. 4:5; 51:19) implies a worship setting (cf. Exod. 15:17).

The next interpretive question is, "Do the next two lines of poetry continue this thought or change to another topic?" Zebulun's involvement in the sea is mentioned in Gen. 49:13.

▣ "abundance of the seas and the hidden treasures of the sand" These two lines are parallel. They are both OBJECTS of one VERB, "suck" or "draw out" (BDB 413, KB 416, Qal IMPERFECT). This is imagery for abundance (cf. Deut. 32:13).

  1. The first one refers to:
    1. food (i.e. sacrifices or good living)
    2. merchandise (i.e. coral, shells, sponges or dye)
  2. The second is made up of two Qal PASSIVE PARTICIPLES:
    1. "to cover," but only here it means "reserved" or "laid up" (BDB 706)
    2. "to hide" (BDB 380)

They seem to refer to the shipping trade (cf. Gen. 49:13-14).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 33:20 "Blessed is the one who enlarges Gad"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
33:20 "Blessed is the one who enlarges Gad" This seems to be a reference to YHWH.

▣ "He lies down as a lion" The word is "lioness" (BDB 522, cf. Gen. 49:9; Num. 24:9; Job 4:11). The lioness was the one who hunted and provided food for the male lion and cubs. Gad was referred to as the lioness. The tribe of Gad was blessed because of their faithfulness in battle (cf. Gen. 49:19).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 33:21
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
33:21 This verse is a play on Gad or a valiant warrior (in the imagery of a lion). He chose part of the land on the eastern side of Jordan to inherit, but he and the Reubenites and the half-tribe of Manasseh were the first military group to go into battle in the Promised Land (cf. Josh. 4:12-13; 22:1-3).

SPECIAL TOPIC: LIONS (OT)

▣ "For there the ruler's portion was reserved" The Hebrew meaning is uncertain! JPSOA translates the line of poetry as "For there is the portion of the revered chieftain."

▣ "And he came with the leaders of the people" This may refer to

  1. these three tribes asking Moses and the elders for permission to settle on the eastern side of Jordan
  2. these three tribes going into battle first on the western side of the Lordan (cf. Josh. 4:12)

entries.title: Deuteronomy 33:22 "Dan is a lion's whelp, that leaps from Bashan"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
33:22 "Dan is a lion's whelp, that leaps from Bashan" The mention of Dan as somehow connected to Bashan (cf. Deut. 1:4; 3:1,3,4,10,11,13,14) is surprising. Originally Dan's tribal allocation by lot was in the southwest (i.e. the Philistine area) and later they moved to the far north (cf. Judges 18). This may be a prophecy connected to this unauthorized relocation.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LIONS IN THE OT

entries.title: Deuteronomy 33:23 "Take possession of the sea and the south"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
33:23 "Take possession of the sea and the south" The VERB (BDB 439, KB 441, Qal IMPERATIVE) is used several times in Deuteronomy for Israel to possess the land (cf. Deut. 1:8,21,39; 2:24,31; 9:23; 11:31; 17:14; 26:1). It implies a taking by force and securing it as a permanent inheritance.

SPECIAL TOPIC: POSSESS THE LAND

entries.title: Deuteronomy 33:24 "Of Asher he said
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
33:24 "Of Asher he said

 'More blessed than sons is Asher;

  May he be favored by his brothers'" This VERB (BDB 224, KB 243, "be") is a Qal JUSSIVE. This shows the working of the Hebrew mind. To an Israelite, a son was the greatest blessing possible.

The rabbis interpret this verse to mean that because of the extreme beauty of Asher's daughters they were more sought after than sons. The meaning of the MT text is uncertain.

▣ "And may he dip his foot in oil" The location of Asher, on the northern seacoast, is the best area for growing olive trees. This phrase possibly refers to the act of treading oil out of the olives by foot.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 33:25 "Your locks will be iron and bronze"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
33:25 "Your locks will be iron and bronze" The Hebrew root for "locks" (BDB 653) or "bars" (BDB 653) can also be translated "shoes" (BDB 653). The form used here is found only here. Because of Asher's geographical position, on the major highway route from the Fertile Crescent down to Egypt, if Asher fell, the whole land fell (from a northerly invasion). She was considered "the door and lock" to the Promised Land.

▣
NASB  "according to your days, so shall your leisurely
 walk be"
NKJV, NJB  "refuge"
NRSV  "He subdues the ancient gods"
TEV  "defense"
JPSOA  "your security last all your days"
LXX  "as your days, so is your strength"

The interpretive question is what does the last NOUN mean (BDB 179)?

  1. strength (i.e. vital life)
  2. security (i.e. no invasion)

entries.title: Deuteronomy 33:26 "There is none like the God"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
33:26 "There is none like the God" Sees note at Deut. 4:35.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANGELS AND DEMONS

entries.title: Deuteronomy 33:26-29
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 33:26-29 These verses are a transition section which praises YHWH's uniqueness and power! Jeshurun is used as a designation for Israel (cf. Deut. 32:15). These verses (i.e. Deut. 33:26 line b & c; Deut. 33:28 line c &d; Deut. 33:29 line f) use phrases that commonly referred to the fertility god, Ba'al, implying that all the things that had been said about Ba'al were not true about him, but were true of YHWH. YHWH is the only God.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 33:27 "The eternal God"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
33:27 "The eternal God" Elohim is often combined with attributes:

  1. the eternal Elohim, here
  2. the everlasting Elohim, Isaiah 26
  3. the true Elohim, 2 Chr. 15:3; Isa. 65:16
  4. the Elohim of all flesh, Jer. 32:27 (similar to Num. 16:22; 27:16)
  5. the Elohim of heaven, Gen. 24:3,7; 2 Chr. 36:23; Ezra 1:2; Neh. 1:4,5; 2:4,20
  6. an Elohim at hand (or near), Jer. 23:23
  7. Elohim of my (or our) salvation, Ps. 18:46; 24:5; 25:5; 27:9; 65:5; 79:9; 85:4; Isa. 17:10
  8. Elohim of my righteousness, Ps. 4:1
  9. Elohim who is my rock, 2 Sam. 22:3; Ps. 18:2
  10. Elohim who is my stronghold, Ps. 43:2
  11. Elohim who is my praise, Ps. 109:1

(This list is from BDB p. 44, #4, b.)

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.

▣
NASB, NKJV  "eternal"
NRSV, JPSOA  "ancient"
NJB, REB  "of old"
Peshitta  "from everlasting"
NET  "everlasting"

The MT has a term (BDB 869) that dentoes that which (or who) is "before." The KB 1069 also denotes "prehistoric" or "primeval" times. It is parallel to "the Ancient of Days" in Dan. 7:9. It refers to the God before time.

▣
NASB  "a dwelling place"
NKJV  "your refuge"
NRSV  "your dwelling place"
TEV    ——
NJB  "the well-spring of Jacob is chosen"
NET, JPSOA  "a refuge"

This term "dwelling place" (BDB 733) can refer to an animal's lair (cf. Job 37:8; 38:40; Amos 3:4) or imagery for the refuge offered by YHWH for His people (only here). A similar concept is found in Ps. 71:3; 91:9.

This is such a famous and encouraging verse. However, the MT is uncertain (i.e. JPSOA footnote). Here are the options.

  1. NRSV ‒ "He subdues the ancient gods"
  2. REB ‒ "He subdued te ancient powers"
  3. Peshitta ‒ "In the heaven of heavens is the dwelling of our God"
  4. LXX ‒ "And there is divine protection of yore"
  5. NJB ‒ "The God of old is our refuge"

Verses 26-27 continue the imagery of YHWH as Israel's (i.e. Jeshsurun) divine warrior (cf. vv. 2-5).

▣ "And underneath are the everlasting arms" This is imagery for:

  1. YHWH's fighting on their behalf (cf. line c, Deut. 33:29)
  2. YHWH's perpetual care and attention

YHWH is the God who acts! It is possible that this is an allusion to Gen. 49:24 (lines b & c).

▣ "Destroy" This VERB (BDB 1029, KB 1552, Hiphil IMPERATIVE) means "to exterminate." It is part of the terminology of "holy war," cf. Deut. 1:27; 2:22; 6:15; 9:20; Josh. 7:12; 9:24. If Israel is obedient to the covenant He will fight for them, but if not, He will fight against them (i.e. the Mosaic covenant is conditional)!

The Israelites were expected to dress for battle and take the field against her enemies, but it was YHWH who won the battle! Notice how YHWH's sovereignty and human actions work together.

33:28
NASB  "The fountain of Jacob secluded"
NKJV  "the fountain of Jacob alone"
NRSV, JPSOA  "untroubled in Jacob's abode"
TEV     ——
NJB  "the well-spring of Jacob is chosen out
REB  "Jacob dwells alone"
LXX  "alone in Jacob's land"

"Fountain" (BDB 745 II) means "spring" and refers to descendants. The term "secluded" (BDB 94, "alone") is imagery for security. Here, for the security of the Promised Land.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 33:29
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
33:29 This verse uses "holy war" terminology to describe YHWH's deliverance

  1. from Egypt (i.e. the Exodus)
  2. from the desert (i.e. wilderness wanderings)
  3. from the Canaanites (i.e. the Conquest)
  4. all future enemies (I.e. the surrounding nations of the ANE)
▣
NASB, NKJV  "tread upon their high places"
NRSV, Peshitta  "tread on their backs"
TEV  "trample them down"
NJB  "trample on their backs"
LXX, Peshitta  "tread on their neck"

K. A. Kitchen, Ancient Orient and Old Testament, pp. 164-165, has an interesting note about the word "Bãmã" (BDB 119).

"A lost meaning is sometimes recovered for a well-known word. 'Bãmã' is the common Hebrew word for a high place. In Ugaritic, it also means 'back,' and this rendering would also fit very well in Deuteronomy 33:29, in the ancient Blessing of Moses:

Thine enemies shall submit to thee,

 And thou shalt tread upon their backs'

  (rather than: 'on their high places').

The idea expressed is then similar to that in Joshua 10:24 or in Psalm 110:1, and finds plastic expression in Egyptian reliefs and statuary."

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. Why could Moses not enter the Promised Land?
  2. Why are there so many translations of Deut. 33:2-3?
  3. Why is Simeon not listed in blessings?
  4. Is there a Messianic reference in these blessings?

entries.title: Deuteronomy 34:1 "the plains of Moab"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
34:1 "the plains of Moab" This is the geographical setting of the conclusion of Numbers (cf. Num. 36:13), and the entire book of Deuteronomy (cf. Deut. 4:44-49). It is on the eastern side of Jordan, right across from Jericho (cf. Deut. 34:1).

▣ "to Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah" This same mountain is mentioned in Deut. 3:17. It is the Hebrew term for "ridge" or "height" (BDB 612 I). It seems that Mount Nebo and Pisgah (BDB 820 "cleft") refer to the very same mountain peak. YHWH uniquely chose this location to be able to fulfill His word to Moses that He would show him the Promised Land even though Moses would not be able to enter into it. Later, in Deut. 34:5, Mount Nebo will be the place of Moses' death. Also, Jewish tradition says that Jeremiah hid the Ark of the covenant on this mountain.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NEBO

▣ "And the Lord showed him all the land" There are several passages which record Moses' public sin before the people which kept him from entering the promised land (cf. Deut. 3:23-28; 32:48-52 and Num. 27:12-14). Moses made several prayers and requests to God about this, yet he was not allowed to enter into the Promised Land. Although sin always runs its course and has its consequences, the graciousness of God is seen in allowing Moses to see the Promised Land even though he could not enter it.

entries.content:

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Deuteronomy 34:2 "the western Sea"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 34:2 "the western Sea" This refers to the Mediterranean Sea (cf. Deut. 11:24). The term "western" is literally "the place behind" (BDB 30).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 34:3 "the Negev"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
34:3 "the Negev" This is the Hebrew word for "south country" (BDB 616) and it refers to the uninhabited pasture land which is south of Beersheba.

▣ "the plain" This refers to the depression known as the Rift Valley in which lies the Dead Sea. Jericho is at the northwest and Zoar at the southwest.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE GEOGRAPHICAL DIVISIONS OF THE PROMISED LAND

▣ "Jericho, the city of palm trees" Jericho is known as the city of palms (cf. Jdg. 1:16) and is one of the oldest cities in this part of the world. It was right across the Jordan River from the place where Israel camped.

▣ "Zoar" The word (BDB 858) means "insignificant" (cf. Gen. 19:20-22). This city is first mentioned in Gen. 13:10. See Josephus, Jewish Wars 4.8.4.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 34:4 "This is the land which I swore to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
34:4 "This is the land which I swore to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob" This is the fulfillment of God's promise to the Patriarchs recorded in Gen. 12:7; 26:3; 28:13. The promise to Abraham included both land and seed. The OT emphasizes the land and children while the NT emphasizes the special child (cf. Isa. 7-12). This ancient promise is repeated often. Here are some examples: Exod. 33:1; Num. 14:23; 32:11; Deut. 1:8; 6:10; 9:5; 30:20.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

▣ "I have let you see it with your eyes, but you shall not go over there" Apparently the sin of publicly striking the rock instead of speaking to it (cf. Num. 20:7-12) is the offense for which Moses has been judged. The people witnessed this flagrant disobedient act of Moses.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 34:5 "So Moses the servant of the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
34:5 "So Moses the servant of the Lord" The term "servant of the Lord" is an honorific title

  1. given to Moses
  2. given to Joshua only after his death
  3. conferred upon King David
  4. later refers to the coming Messiah (cf. the Servant Songs of Isaiah 40-56)

It may be the source of the NT Pauline phrase, "slave of God." The concept of an OT servant is extremely significant. In the OT election or servanthood was to fulfill the purpose of God, not necessarily for salvation. Cyrus II is called "God's anointed" (cf. Isa. 44:28; 45:1) and Assyria is called "the rod of His anger" (cf. Isa. 10:5). This cruel nation and pagan king fit into God's plan but were not spiritually related to Him.

The terms "election" and "choice" have a spiritual connotation only in the NT.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MY SERVANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: OT TITLES FOR THE SPECIAL COMING ONE

SPECIAL TOPIC: HE CHOSE US

▣ "died there in the land of Moab, according to the word of the Lord" The literal Hebrew is "by the mouth of the Lord," (BDB 804), which seems to be imagery for the word of God (cf. Gen. 41:40; 45:21; Exod. 17:1; 38:21; Num. 3:16,39).

However, the rabbis say that this is the "kiss of God." They say that God kissed Moses on the mouth and took away his breath. This is very similar to our cultural idiom "the kiss of death." If so, it is a beautiful account of the balance between the justice and mercy of God in the life of Moses.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN

entries.title: Deuteronomy 34:6 "And He buried him in the valley in the land of Moab"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
34:6 "And He buried him in the valley in the land of Moab" The "He" implies God Himself. This is much like Gen. 7:16, where God Himself closed the large door to the ark. One reason for God burying Moses Himself is because God has taken away all of the ancient sites and artifacts that we might worship instead of Him. Notice that Moses was not buried on Mount Nebo itself but down in the valley.

The strange NT passage in Jude 9 is related to this account, but how is not exactly clear. Jude 9 seems to quote an extra-canonical book known as The Assumption of Moses. The exact purpose for the devil wanting the body of Moses is uncertain.

▣ "but no man knows his burial place to this day" This is obviously the work of a later editor. Many assert that Moses could not have written this last chapter which relates to his death. Rashi says that Joshua wrote about Moses' death, while IV Esdras asserts that Moses wrote of his own death. I believe in Mosaic authorship of the Torah, but that does not rule out some editorial comments such as this which appear from time to time. The similarity of the Hebrew between the Pentateuch and the book of Joshua seems to imply that Joshua did have a part in writing Moses' memoirs. However, the significant place of Ezra in rabbinical Judaism as the editor of the entire OT is also a possibility.

SPECIAL TOPIC: EDITORIAL ADDITIONS TO DEUTERONOMY

entries.title: Deuteronomy 34:7 "Although Moses was one hundred and twenty years old when he died"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
34:7 "Although Moses was one hundred and twenty years old when he died" This one hundred and twenty year span is developed in Stephen's sermon in Acts 7:23ff into a threefold division of forty years each:

  1. forty years in the educational system of Egypt
  2. forty years in the very desert into which he would later lead the children of Israel
  3. forty years in the wilderness wandering period

D. L. Moody said, "For 40 years Moses thought he was a somebody. For 40 years he thought he was a nobody. For 40 years he found out what God can do with a nobody."

▣ "his eye was not dim, nor his vigor abated" This seems to refer to the health of Moses, while Deut. 31:2 seems to be an excuse given by Moses for why he cannot enter the Promised Land (that he was too weak and old). This is not a contradiction, but one more attempt by Moses to try to explain away his sin by either blaming the people or his age or other factors.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 34:8 "So the sons of Israel wept for Moses. . .thirty days"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 34:8 "So the sons of Israel wept for Moses. . .thirty days" This would be one lunar cycle. This same amount of time was given to the mourning of Aaron (cf. Num. 20:29).

entries.title: Deuteronomy 34:9 "Now Joshua the son of Nun"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
34:9 "Now Joshua the son of Nun" The name Joshua means "YHWH saves" (BDB 221). It is the very same name as "Jesus" (i.e. Palestinian Aramaic, cf. Matt. 1:21). It is made up of the Hebrew word, "Hosea," which means "salvation" and an abbreviation of the Covenant name for God (ya) attached to the beginning.

▣ "was filled with the spirit of wisdom" This concept of "filled" (BDB 569, KB 583, Qal PERFECT) should be compared with Num. 27:18 and a similar concept used of the artisans in Exod. 28:3. Obviously the Spirit of God was involved in the lives of people in the OT as well as the NT.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE BIBLE

▣ "wisdom" This seems (BDB 315) to refer to Joshua's ability to guide the people into battle and in administrative justice. Joshua was not from the tribe of Levi and, therefore, could not in any way be a priest, but he was a gifted leader.

▣ "for Moses had laid his hands on him" This concept of laying on of hands is very significant in the OT. We see this very act in Num. 27:22-23; also note Deut. 31:1-8. It is somehow related to the laying on of hands on the sacrificial victim where somehow the sin is transferred. In some way Moses' leadership was transferred to Joshua.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LAYING ON OF HANDS IN THE BIBLE

entries.title: Deuteronomy 34:10 "Since that time no prophet has risen in Israel like Moses"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
34:10 "Since that time no prophet has risen in Israel like Moses" Verses 10-12 are a comment from Moses' scribe or, more probably, a later editor. This apparently refers to the Messianic prophecy of Deut. 18:15-22. This theme is developed in Heb. 3:1-6, where Jesus and Moses are contrasted.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHECY (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE SUPERIORITY OF THE NEW COVENANT OVER THE MOSAIC COVENANT

▣ "whom the Lord knew face to face" The term "knew" (BDB 393, KB 390, Qal PERFECT is a Hebrew idiom for "intimate, close fellowship" (cf. Gen. 4:1; Jer. 1:5). It does not refer to cognitive knowledge. The phrase "face to face" shows the intimacy with which God spoke to Moses (cf. Exod. 33:11; Num. 12:6-8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

entries.title: Deuteronomy 34:11-12
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
34:11-12 Verse 11 seems to imply that the plagues of Egypt, which took a period of about eighteen months, were meant to judge the gods of Egypt and to try to lead the Egyptians to a place of trust in YHWH. Verse 12 shows us that the miracles that God did against the Egyptian gods were also meant to increase the faith of the Israelites just as Jesus' miracles were to increase the faith of the disciples. It is also possible that Deut. 34:12 relates to the wilderness wandering period.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. Why is the geographical location of the events in the book of Deuteronomy so significant?
  2. Why did God hide the grave of Moses?
  3. How does Deut. 34:7 seem to contradict 31:2?
  4. What is the significance of Moses laying on of hands on Joshua? How does this relate to modern ordination?
  5. Why is Joshua not considered a prophet like Moses (cf. Deut. 34:10)?
  6. What is the purpose of miracles (cf. Deut. 34:11-12)?
